title: Bengals News: Bears joint practice
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals and Chicago Bears will get a joint practice in before their game on Saturday. It will be a chance for the team to get an extended look at their players against a different unit than the very familiar faces of their own teammates. We will surely be looking at how each unit […]
full_text: CINCINNATI, OHIO - NOVEMBER 2: Andrei Iosivas #80 of the Cincinnati Bengals runs the ball against Tyrique Stevenson #29 of the Chicago Bears during the NFL 2025 game between Chicago Bears and Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on November 2, 2025 in Cincinnati, Ohio. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals and Chicago Bears will get a joint practice in before their game on Saturday. It will be a chance for the team to get an extended look at their players against a different unit than the very familiar faces of their own teammates. We will surely be looking at how each unit performs, but most importantly everyone simply will be holding their breath hoping everyone makes it out of the practices healthy. There will almost certainly be some fights as these are teams that likely practice two different ways. It will be interesting to see how the new look defense measures up (albeit in a practice setting without tackling) against yet another offense. It simply will not be as intense as the preseason game will be, but with a unit that has been overhauled so much, you take any chance to see how they are measuring up before the season. Tell us down in the comments who you hope shines bright during the joint practice. Bengals News Brothers In Arms Zac And Press Taylor Hope Practice Makes Perfect “This is probably as good as my parents could have asked for,” muses Bears offensive coordinator Press Taylor driving into work the other day. “There’s not going to be a winner or a loser. We’re all together on the same field and no stakes. I think they like that.” It may not be the Harbaugh Brothers meeting in the Super Bowl, but it is still cool to see two brothers meet on an NFL field. A lot of work goes into being a coach at that level and even more luck. Ja’Marr Chase Ranked No. 16 on NFL Top 100 List Chase was named Associated Press First-Team All Pro for the second consecutive season in 2025 after tallying 125 receptions for 1,412 yards and eight touchdowns. He became the third player in NFL with at least 125 receptions in consecutive seasons and set the Bengals single-season record with seven 100-yard receiving games. Chase became the fifth-fastest player in NFL history to cross the 6,000 yards receiving threshold during Week 7 against the Pittsburgh Steelers last season, hitting the milestone in his 69th regular-season game. Just a friendly reminder that the only thing good about the NFL Top 100 is the little videos of players talking about the guys who made the list. Chase is either the No. 1 or No. 2 wide receiver in the NFL depending on if you ask someone in Minnesota or not. Him being at 16 is silly. Murphy and Turner are emerging as young cornerstones on the Bengals’ defense “Why wouldn’t I go against the best receiver?” Turner said. “It’s as simple as that. He makes me way better. I’m going to make sure I make him way better. I evolve every year and keep getting better. He works. I work. We’ve got the best quarterback. It can’t get better than this. That’s how I look at it, and it pays off.” Cincinnati is banking quite a bit on these young players, and if they play as well as the Bengals are hoping they will have to pay to keep them. Both are heading into their final seasons of their contracts. Hopefully they can retain both. This Bengals Veteran Could Be Cincinnati’s Next Surprise Cut Candidate “Tanner Hudson could be on the outs within a healthy Cincinnati Bengals tight end room,” Moton wrote. “In 2024, Erick All Jr. tore his ACL and missed the entire 2025 campaign. Mike Gesicki missed four games last year. They’re both at full strength. By the way, Cincinnati selected Jack Endries in the seventh round of this year’s draft. Hudson shouldn’t be so surprising. The tight end room is stacked currently. Hudson is 31-years-old and they have young guys like All, Endries and even Cam Grandy. All of these young guys have shown serious promise and most of them have the added benefit of being solid to good blockers as well. Hudson has had memorable time in Cincinnati, but there is a new wave of players coming in. NFL News NFL Network: Texans WR Jayden Higgins (torn ACL) out for 2026 season The No. 34 overall pick of the 2025 NFL Draft, Higgins caught 41 passes for 525 yards and six touchdowns as a rookie, finding himself in an elevated role following Tank Dell’s season-ending injury suffered late in the 2024 campaign. Always unfortunate to see a young player go down like this before the year even starts. The Houston Texans really need as much help as they can get at wide receiver after CJ Stroud regressed last season. Seahawks sign CB Trevon Diggs as Terrion Arnold deal remains in limbo The move comes after the Seahawks put the signing of former first-rounder Terrion Arnold on hold. Arnold is facing eight felony charges in connection with a February robbery and kidnapping. Schefter added that the club still plans to sign the former Detroit Lions corner, who is expected to land on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. It is quite interesting that the Seahawks plan on signing both players. Obviously, Arnold’s situation has so much more going on beyond football, and Diggs has not been the same player that made him a household name early in his career. Seattle seems to be hedging their bets on a couple low-risk signings. One potential first-time Pro Bowler from each AFC team heading into the 2026 NFL season DJ Turner II’s play surged in 2025. Unfortunately, the rest of a moribund Bengals defense left him an afterthought. The sticky cover man netted a -6.2% CPOE, fifth-best among all CBs (min. 500 coverage snaps) and a -0.1 EPA per target, per Next Gen Stats. With an upgraded unit around the rising CB, Turner’s play should improve even more in 2026. DJ Turner should have been a Pro Bowler last season. He was one of the biggest snubs. If Cincinnati is a better team, he should get the attention he deserves. It would also help if the defense wasn’t one of the worst units in NFL history.

title: Jonathan Allen is bringing a Nick Saban mentality to the Bengals defense
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals have spent much of the offseason trying to fix a defense that simply wasn’t good enough. Jonathan Allen is making sure nobody starts celebrating the finished product before the work is done. Allen, now entering his 10th NFL season, has brought more than an accomplished résumé to Cincinnati. The two-time Pro Bowler […]
full_text: The Cincinnati Bengals have spent much of the offseason trying to fix a defense that simply wasn’t good enough. Jonathan Allen is making sure nobody starts celebrating the finished product before the work is done. Allen, now entering his 10th NFL season, has brought more than an accomplished résumé to Cincinnati. The two-time Pro Bowler is also bringing some of the lessons he learned playing for Nick Saban at Alabama, including Saban’s famous disdain for “rat poison.” In other words, don’t start believing all the nice things people are saying about you. That message seems particularly appropriate for a Bengals defense generating considerably more optimism than it did a year ago. “For me, I try to keep it stupid simple,” Allen told WLWT’s Charlie Clifford. “I try to focus on day-by-day, try to take it play by play, and you’ll end up where you want to be one day. You focus on the little things you’ve got to do to get to the ultimate goal.” Jonathan Allen's leadership is already on display in Cincinnati Year 10 in the league. Still wearing the 'Bama headband & going back to lessons from Nick Saban: -"Rat Poison" -"For me I try to keep it Stupid Simple" -"Some people hear 'potential' and get excited. I just hear a… pic.twitter.com/6MgrNAb2V0 — Charlie Clifford (@char_cliff) August 18, 2026 That’s a philosophy Allen learned long before arriving in Cincinnati. Allen played four seasons at Alabama, where he became one of the best defensive players in college football. As a senior captain in 2016, he recorded 16 tackles for loss and 10.5 sacks and was a unanimous first-team All-American and SEC Defensive Player of the Year. He also won the Bronko Nagurski Trophy, Chuck Bednarik Award, and Ted Hendricks Award. Allen was part of three College Football Playoff teams at Alabama and helped the Crimson Tide win the national championship following the 2015 season. Now, a decade later, some of those lessons are still showing up. “This defense has a lot of potential,” Allen said. “Some people hear ‘potential’ and get excited. I just hear a group that hasn’t done anything yet. “Our job hasn’t even started yet. Until the games start flying, we’ve got to keep our heads down and do the work.” That’s the kind of message the Bengals hoped Allen would bring when they signed him in March. Cincinnati added the veteran defensive tackle after his one-year stint with the Minnesota Vikings, where he started all 17 games in 2025 and finished with 68 tackles, seven tackles for loss and 3.5 sacks. Before that, Allen spent eight seasons in Washington after being selected in the first round of the 2017 NFL Draft. He earned consecutive Pro Bowl selections following the 2021 and 2022 seasons and enters 2026 with 469 career tackles, 67 tackles for loss and 45.5 sacks in 126 regular-season games. That experience matters for a Bengals defense undergoing a significant makeover. When Allen signed with Cincinnati, he made it clear that winning was one of the attractions. He said the Bengals were one of the places where he believed he could compete for a Super Bowl, pointing specifically to the opportunity created for the defense by playing alongside Joe Burrow and Cincinnati’s offense. But Allen also understood that Cincinnati needed improvement on the other side of the football. So far, there have been encouraging signs. The Bengals opened the preseason with a 16-14 victory over the Detroit Lions, with Al Golden’s defense creating turnovers and getting contributions from both veterans and young players. Jordan Battle and Russ Yeast came away with interceptions, while rookie pass rushers Cashius Howell and Landon Robinson were among the young defenders who flashed. Allen isn’t interested in handing out trophies for August practices or preseason promise, though. Allen spent enough time in Tuscaloosa to understand Saban’s lesson: Potential doesn’t win anything. Neither does praise. Production does.

title: Browns HC Todd Monken: ‘It looked like we belonged’
summary: The Cleveland Browns have done a lot of things since returning to the NFL in 1999.  To wit: But one thing they have rarely done is look like they belong on the field. Browns fans know the feeling. The team has all summer to prepare for the opening game of the season, only to come […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - JUNE 09: Head coach Todd Monken of the Cleveland Browns looks on during the Cleveland Browns Mandatory Minicamp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on June 09, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns have done a lot of things since returning to the NFL in 1999. To wit: They have employed a lot of full-time head coaches. They have employed numerous general managers. They have wasted countless draft picks. They have lost games in ways that are hard to describe – even if you witnessed them live. They have used more starting quarterbacks than seems possible. But one thing they have rarely done is look like they belong on the field. Browns fans know the feeling. The team has all summer to prepare for the opening game of the season, only to come out and perform as if it is the first time they have ever seen a football. Or fans will watch the Browns in the 1 p.m. game on a given Sunday, then sit, stunned, during the late games as two teams play something that only resembles what the Browns did earlier in the day because it involves a football and is played on a 100-yard field. Todd Monken on the Browns’ practice with the Bills: “It didn’t look like we were out of place. It looked like we belonged.” pic.twitter.com/oW40he2MJh — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) August 20, 2026 But on Thursday, for at least one day, the Browns showed they might finally be starting to figure this whole thing out. At least that is the impression that head coach Todd Monken took away from today’s joint practice against the Buffalo Bills when asked about the performance of the offense : “The one thing I would say, maybe it was just me, it didn’t look like we were out of place. It looked like we belonged. That’s all we wanted to see: do we belong? Does our first eleven give us a chance to move the ball and score? I felt that way today.” Monken also tossed some praise toward the offensive line, which is slowly rounding into form while also dealing wth injuries : “There were some mistakes there, but we made some plays. Over the course of whatever amount of snaps, you wanted to see us be able to run it. We hit a few balls down the field. We hit some short third downs, So, you wanted to see it all. I may feel different in two or three hours, but as of right now, I left the field going, ‘We’ve got some guys to work with.’” So what does this all mean in the grand scheme of the season? Maybe nothing, but maybe it is the start of the team beginning to believe in itself and embrace what could be possible if they can play as a cohesive unit, rather than being their own worst enemy – especially on offense. It could still all fall apart on September 13 against the Jacksonville Jaguars, but for one afternoon the Browns actually looked like a professional football team. For now, that is good enough. Or, as Monken put it after practice , “Was that a lot of fun? Holy shit.”

title: NFL expansion overseas? Now more likely than not, so Browns travel plans might be even more
summary: When the 2026 NFL schedule was revealed in May, two things were apparent for the Cleveland Browns: There weren’t any prime-time games, and with the nine contests planned for the league’s international series, the Browns were omitted, despite rumors of a game in Paris. Every other AFC North Division club is included in this year’s […]
full_text: Cleveland Browns walk out onto the pitch ahead of the NFL International match at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London. Picture date: Sunday October 5, 2025. (Photo by Bradley Collyer/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images When the 2026 NFL schedule was revealed in May, two things were apparent for the Cleveland Browns: There weren’t any prime-time games, and with the nine contests planned for the league’s international series, the Browns were omitted, despite rumors of a game in Paris . Every other AFC North Division club is included in this year’s offering. Then Vegas came out with their preseason odds. The Browns are +2100 to win the AFC North Division (last place), and +25,000 to capture the Super Bowl (#29). RELATED: MAKE YOUR PLANS AS THE 2026 SCHEDULE IS HERE In the 1970s, the “World Football League” was invented with the idea of bringing the sport of American Football to a global scale. That was the grand plan. In the first year, the new entity established a club in Toronto, which was later relocated to Memphis. As a league that touted a global blueprint, all of the clubs were based in the United States, and there weren’t any actual international teams whatsoever. The selling point with this new league was that it would gradually place teams in other countries. London versus Los Angeles. Tokyo against New York. Berlin takes on Birmingham. What occurred instead was that every franchise was located in the United States, and the league folded midway into its second year of existence. The “National Football League” (NFL) had played some exhibition contests with Canadian Football League clubs in the 1950s and 1960s in both the United States and in Canada. Its first international game played outside the confines of North America happened in 1976 when the San Diego Chargers played the St. Louis Cardinals in Japan in a game labeled “The Mainichi Star Bowl.” This year, the league is playing nine regular-season games in other countries, including the first held in Australia and France. Now, the NFL is admitting that one day it will plant a team in another country. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said in an interview with former NFL defensive player and German-born Markus Kuhn on German media outlet RTL/ntv , he stated that the league has full plans to eventually place a team permanently based outside the confines of the United States. Goodell said: “At some point, there will be NFL teams outside the USA. I have no doubt that this will happen one day.” The big questions are which nation, and whether that would be an expansion team or an existing franchise that will relocate. Notice that Goodell used the word “teams” instead of just one franchise. Also note that Goodell used the words “will be” and not “might be.” Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk had this take regarding the commissioner’s statement: “That is the most unequivocal, unconditional, clear statement I’ve seen of indication and confidence that the NFL is going to have teams in other countries. I think we kinda know it’s going to happen, but to hear the commissioner say it that clearly, that’s significant.” On the surface, the most feasible locations would be either in Mexico or Canada. Both would satisfy his clarifications of “outside the USA.” Mexico City has long been a probable location to place a franchise since it is close to the mainland and would be in the same time zone as other NFL cities, being a central standard time zone city. Travel would not be an issue as well. Estadio Azteca Stadium is an excellent venue that holds 87,500 patrons and has hosted several World Cup finals. Canadian cities would be another matter. The NFL has had a gentlemen’s agreement with the “Canadian Football League” (CFL) for decades, just like it has had with college football and high school football programs. The NFL isn’t looking to quash or interfere with the lesser league and levels. Good luck to our friends up North ‼️ #GoBills x @BlueJays pic.twitter.com/Gn9lrmce9m — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) October 3, 2025 The Buffalo Bills at one time had plans to expand the team’s fan base in Southern Ontario . They had been playing a preseason game in Toronto for years and were set to schedule one home game a year, but eventually, that thought was abandoned. The CFL cried foul and didn’t want any new team to affect the fanbase of their CFL affiliate, the Toronto Argonauts. Then there is Bill C-22: the Canadian Football Act. Introduced in 1974, its purpose was to give the CFL a government-protected monopoly over professional football in Canada. There have been many NFL preseason games held in various Canadian cities over the decades, but the NFL has a friendly relationship with the league and has no interest in maneuvering into its territory. The NFL has zero financial interest in the CFL, whether that be ownership stakes or operational partnerships. In 1997, the NFL loaned the CFL a $3 million interest-free loan in order to stabilize the league. As far as players, the NFL is allowed to sign CFL players who have reached the option year of their contract, but that’s it. While Mexico is a large possibility, going into Canada is a dead issue. In the past, the NFL has always dodged the question of international expansion. They have used descriptions such as “trying to expand the sport” and “our hope one day.” To date, it’s always been blanket statements that have never nailed down what the league’s future stance actually is. There is a strong possibility that the league will want to create new teams in Europe. Germany and England are the most logical locations. Both countries draw very well with the NFL International Series and had large crowds back in the 1990s when the NFL established “NFL Europe,” an NFL farm-system league. A franchise in either London or Munich/Berlin/Frankfurt, Germany would draw extremely well and become successful from minute one. Both countries have embraced the game of American Football, and the NFL as a viable entertainment option. This year alone, three games are scheduled in London while one will be played in Munich. The Jacksonville Jaguars annually play one home game in London and consider that city their second home. Their fan base is called the “Union Jax,” which has a membership that exceeds 40,000. At one time, it was rumored that the Jags would eventually relocate to London. However, placing any team in any European country creates a huge problem: time zones. Travel is already an issue with NFL teams during the regular season. Players and coaches love going over to other countries as long as their bye week is the following weekend. This allows everyone to spend some time in a foreign country, go sightseeing, and explore the local food. But if any team has a game in Europe and then a game the following week, for one, the travel is long and tedious, with numerous airports to visit. The flights are long, to the tune of 15 hours, and each player’s body has instant fatigue, which means they must arrive earlier than for any normal scheduled game. Florio explained: “The travel is an issue. There are advances in the return of supersonic travel. The Concorde is long gone, but there are different planes. Then there are the tax rates in the other countries and the exchange rate. The league is going to have guys who will say, ‘I don’t want to play in London. I don’t want to live in Germany. I didn’t sign up to play pro football and get shipped off to Australia.’ London’s going to be the first candidate.” The NFL has been monitoring the developments of supersonic travel. But each of these planes that would qualify is not very big. It might require an entire fleet in order to get all of the players, coaches, cheerleaders, front office, trainers, and medical personnel, not to mention all the equipment. By installing a franchise in another country, does this mean that at some point a Super Bowl could be hosted on foreign soil? Say it ain’t so. Goodell addressed that: “There…

full_text: WEST LAFAYETTE, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 30: Dylan Downing #22 and Drew Biber #82 of the Purdue Boilermakers celebrate a touchdown during the first half against the Illinois Fighting Illini at Ross-Ade Stadium on September 30, 2023 in West Lafayette, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Especially with the current 90-man roster, the Cleveland Browns are always in the process of trying to find the right fits for what they need. Sometimes it is less about talent and more about fit or filling in for injured positions. Cleveland GM Andrew Berry has spent much of the summer looking for a veteran defensive end , having to settle for signing someone who hasn’t played a snap in the regular season yet . The Browns tight end position was added to the list of positions of interest over the last few days as a few came in for workouts, while another could depart to return to the college ranks . With Joe Royer still absent and Dae’quan Wright potentially heading back to Ole Miss, it was no surprise that the team signed TE Drew Biber on Thursday. Biber was signed by the Green Bay Packers as an undrafted free agent after this year’s NFL draft. Mostly a blocking tight end, Biber caught 15 passes in four years with Purdue, then 18 last season with the Minnesota Golden Gophers. To make room for Biber, Cleveland placed TE Jack Stoll on injured reserve. Stoll was signed in free agency this year, with a history as a quality blocking tight end . The Browns did not disclose the injury that led Stoll to be placed on IR, nor when it occurred.
author: Jared Mueller

title: Cowboys countdown to kickoff: Top 100 iconic games – Day 24
summary: It is Day 24 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like […]
full_text: UNITED STATES - JANUARY 10: Football: NFC Playoffs, San Francisco 49ers Dwight Clark (87) in action, making catch and scoring game winning touchdown vs Dallas Cowboys, San Francisco, CA 1/10/1982 (Photo by Andy Hayt/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images) (SetNumber: X26441 TK1) It is Day 24 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff. We are looking back at the 100 most iconic games in Dallas Cowboys history. The countdown will leads us right up to the opening game of 2026. Our look back doesn’t depend on just one criteria for our rankings. We take into consideration things like how big the game was for the organization, how memorable the game was, games that had unusual events take place, games that are a part of NFL lore, Cowboys firsts, and games where the Cowboys just plain dominated. Variety is the spice of life and we have all different kind of Cowboys games to review. At the bottom, we’ll link each day of the countdown so you can go back and check out any you missed. It’s Day 24 of our 100-day countdown to kickoff, when we revisit one of the most painful, yet historically important games, in Cowboys history. Dallas stood 51 seconds away from another Super Bowl appearance, only for Joe Montana and Dwight Clark to create the moment everyone refers to as “The Catch”. Sunday, January 10, 1982 Candlestick Park, San Francisco, California Final Score: San Francisco 49ers 28, Dallas Cowboys 27 The Cowboys entered as established NFC royalty. They had reached the conference championship nine times since the 1970 merger and had already eliminated San Francisco from the playoffs three times during the previous decade. The 49ers represented the emerging challenger, having finished 13-3 under Bill Walsh and beaten Dallas 45-14 during the regular season. San Francisco opened the scoring when Montana found Freddie Solomon for an eight-yard touchdown. Rafael Septien answered with a 44-yard field goal before a 49ers fumble gave Dallas a short field. Danny White capitalized by throwing a 26-yard touchdown to Tony Hill, moving the Cowboys ahead 10-7. The lead continued to change hands during the second quarter. Montana escaped pressure and connected with Clark for a 20-yard touchdown, but Dallas responded after a pass-interference penalty moved the ball deep into San Francisco territory. Tony Dorsett completed the drive with a five-yard touchdown run, giving the Cowboys a 17-14 halftime advantage. San Francisco moved back in front during the third quarter after linebacker Bobby Leopold intercepted White and returned the ball to the Dallas 13-yard line. Johnny Davis eventually scored from two yards out, putting the 49ers ahead 21-17. It was another costly swing in a game filled with turnovers and sudden changes in momentum. Dallas answered in the fourth quarter. Septien’s 22-yard field goal cut the deficit to one before the defense recovered another San Francisco fumble near midfield. White then found Doug Cosbie for a 21-yard touchdown, restoring a 27-21 Cowboys lead with 10:41 remaining. The Cowboys appeared ready to protect that advantage after Everson Walls recorded his second interception of Montana. Dallas drained nearly five minutes before punting, leaving San Francisco at its own 11-yard line with 4:54 remaining. Montana responded by directing an 89-yard drive, steadily moving the 49ers into scoring position through short passes, runs and a reverse to Solomon. Facing third-and-three from the Dallas six, Montana rolled right while Ed “Too Tall” Jones and Larry Bethea applied pressure. He lofted the ball toward the back of the end zone, where Clark leapt above Walls and secured the six-yard touchdown. Ray Wersching’s extra point gave San Francisco a 28-27 lead with 51 seconds left. The game was not over. White immediately connected with Drew Pearson for 31 yards, and Eric Wright’s tackle prevented Pearson from escaping for a potential touchdown. Dallas had reached the San Francisco 44 with 38 seconds remaining and needed only a field goal, but Lawrence Pillers beat the protection on the next play, forced White to fumble and allowed Jim Stuckey to recover. This game belongs on the countdown because losses can be as historically significant as victories. “The Catch” did not immediately end Dallas’ relevance, the Cowboys returned to the NFC Championship Game the following season, but it became the symbolic transfer of NFC power. San Francisco advanced to its first Super Bowl, defeated Cincinnati and began a run that produced four championships during the 1980s. #Cowboys vs #49ers 1982 The Catch Final Score: San Francisco 49ers 28, Dallas Cowboys 27 #DallasCowboys #NFL (📽️: @nfl ) pic.twitter.com/fgMq0zJt2C — Mike Poland (@kenfigkowboy) August 20, 2026 Interesting Facts About the Game The catch made by Clark that sealed the win for the 49ers is still hotly debated today. Was Montana trying to throw out of bounds and got lucky? Was it directed pass intended for Clark? summary: The Dallas Cowboys and New Orleans Saints could not seem to stop fighting one another during their scrimmage on Tuesday, and now they are paying for it. The NFL announced on Thursday that Dallas and New Orleans have each been fined $500,000 for the “actions” that took place. This is obviously not a good look […]
full_text: WOODLAND HILLS, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 11: Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys after joint practice between the Dallas Cowboys and the Los Angeles Rams at Rams Village at Warner Center on August 11, 2026 in Woodland Hills, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys and New Orleans Saints could not seem to stop fighting one another during their scrimmage on Tuesday, and now they are paying for it. The NFL announced on Thursday that Dallas and New Orleans have each been fined $500,000 for the “actions” that took place. This is obviously not a good look for anyone involved. The NFL has confirmed that the #Cowboys and #Saints have each been fined $500,000 for the actions that took place at the joint practice between the teams earlier this week. — Mike Garafolo (@MikeGarafolo) August 20, 2026 It was documented as the scrimmage wore on how the Cowboys and Saints simply could not stop fighting each other . There was never any specific culprit named from the “action”, but Donovan Ezeiruaku was ejected in terms of transactional outcomes. Brian Schottenheimer has said at many turns that the Cowboys need to be more disciplined this season, and this is certainly a step backwards in that effort. Obviously this was not an actual game and things can be said about who started what, but the facts are now that Dallas has literally been fined for improper activity of this sort. Hopefully it is a learning opportunity moving forward.

title: 5 Cowboys to watch in Preseason Week 2 against Arizona Cardinals
summary: Time is running out for players to lay claim to one of the coveted few remaining roster spots with the Dallas Cowboys this year. This week’s matchup with the Arizona Cardinals in Week 2 of preseason could be paramount for some players to cement their role with the team this year, or not. Whatever the […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - AUGUST 15: Israel Abanikanda #30 of the Dallas Cowboys runs with the ball during the fourth quarter during the NFL preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on August 15, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Jack Compton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Time is running out for players to lay claim to one of the coveted few remaining roster spots with the Dallas Cowboys this year. This week’s matchup with the Arizona Cardinals in Week 2 of preseason could be paramount for some players to cement their role with the team this year, or not. Whatever the case, there can be a lot of the line for some players. While everyone suiting up this week against the Cardinals will be under the microscope, there are a handful who we believe should be watched more closely than others. Some of them need to prove their spot on the depth chart of their given positions, while others are still on the roster bubble trying to earn a job. We’ll let you decide which is which. WR Camden Brown After a strong showing throughout training camp followed by a two-touchdown performance against the Seattle Seahawks in preseason Week 1, Camden Brown is someone that everyone will be watching closely against the Arizona Cardinals. He’s currently the favorite to win the fifth and probably final WR spot with the Cowboys. Another strong performance like last week could all but seal it. There’s already been talk about him replacing the No. 6 jersey, the same as Donovan Ezeiruaku, he’s currently donning with another number. LB Jaishawn Barham After missing some time in training camp with a groin injury as well as last week’s preseason game against the Seahawks, Dallas’ third-round pick this year, Jaishawn Barham, is expected to make his Cowboys debut against the Cardinals. It’s unknown how much he will play, probably no more than a dozen snaps, but it will be good to see him on the field in action after the way he’s been talked about throughout training camp. This especially true considering he could be competing for a starting job this year as a rookie. OT Nate Thomas Nate Thomas seems to have sadly regressed from last season. He is still currently the Cowboys swing tackle as of now, but if he doesn’t show improvement, and quickly, it may result in an outside addition being brought in to help stabilize the position. From top to bottom, Dallas’ OT position is still one of the team’s biggest concerns. If Thomas can at the least regain his 2025 form it eases those concerns, if not, Jerry Jones and Company may be looking for another swing tackle to improve things for the better. OLB Marist Liufau Despite being new to the OLB position, Marist Liufau shows promise as a pass rusher coming off the edge. He’s currently probably in a head-to-head battle with Sam Williams to earn the six and probably final spot at OLB after the recent addition of Von Miller, but could possibly have the slight edge over his competitor. With his off-ball/OLB position flex as well as his special teams value, there’s a lot of ways can be utilized by the Cowboys. He still has a lot to prove though, which is why he’s someone to watch this week against Arizona. RB Israel Abanikanda Although he’s been performing just as well as anyone throughout training camp/preseason, Israel Abanikanda is still a sleeper in the Cowboys backup RB competition and a long shot to make the roster. That doesn’t mean he’s not someone to keep an eye on though. He averaged 5.1 yards per carry last week against the Seahawks, behind only Malik Davis’ 5.6 yards per carry. With Jaydon Blue and Phil Mafah both banged up, Abanikanda could receive more playing time against the Cardinals, possibly putting himself further in contention for a roster spot.
author: Brian Martin

title: Cowboys history says playoffs are coin flip for second year of head coaches
summary: The 2026 season marks the second in which Brian Schottenheimer is the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys. By all measures, to this point obviously, his second year promises to be significantly different from his first. Defining success for a Cowboys head coach has been difficult ever since the onset of The Drought™. This is […]
full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 3: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer of the Dallas Cowboys looks on during training camp at River Ridge Playing Fields on August 3, 2026 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 season marks the second in which Brian Schottenheimer is the head coach of the Dallas Cowboys. By all measures, to this point obviously, his second year promises to be significantly different from his first. Defining success for a Cowboys head coach has been difficult ever since the onset of The Drought™. This is a franchise fighting a now officially 30-year old (and counting) shadow and so to some nothing is truly success except escaping it. Speaking pragmatically, reaching the playoffs is a good place to start. The Cowboys missed the playoffs in Schotty’s first season and the one that preceded it, so missing out again would mean over 1,000 days with no postseason activity. Schottenheimer is the 10th head coach in franchise history, and interestingly it is sort of a coin-flip as to whether or not one reaches the playoffs by their second season in charge: Tom Landry……….. No Jimmy Johnson….. No Barry Switzer……… Yes Chan Gailey………… Yes Dave Campo……….. No Bill Parcells………… Yes Wade Phillips……… Yes Jason Garrett………. No Mike McCarthy…….. Yes This is admittedly a bit arbitrary. Football has changed a lot since the Cowboys were founded in 1960 so you have to understand there is context necessary for each and every situation. Still though, for the most part, recent history suggests that the Cowboys should reach the playoffs by a head coach’s second season in charge. Three of the last four have done so with Jason Garrett being the exception, and for what it’s worth the Cowboys had de facto playoff games in the final week of his first two regular seasons. Not the same, but again, context. For the most part fans are feeling that the Cowboys are a playoff-caliber team this season. They have to play the games. You don’t make it in August. All of that stuff. But it stands to reason that the Cowboys will be a playoff team before Schotty’s second season is over. Right?
author: RJ Ochoa

title: 3 bubble players pushing for a Cowboys roster spot
summary: The time is quickly approaching when the Dallas Cowboys will have to make some tough decisions in order to get under the league mandated 53-man roster limit. Many players have the ease of mind that their roster spot is secured, leaving those currently sitting on the bubble fighting for one of the few spots still […]
full_text: The time is quickly approaching when the Dallas Cowboys will have to make some tough decisions in order to get under the league mandated 53-man roster limit. Many players have the ease of mind that their roster spot is secured, leaving those currently sitting on the bubble fighting for one of the few spots still open. It’s a few of those players we wanted to shine the light on today. LB Justin Barron After hauling in three INTs in the scrimmage with the Los Angeles Rams and a another strong showing against the Seattle Seahawks in the first preseason game, Justin Barron has suddenly gone from a roster longshot to someone who will be difficult to cut. He seems to have grown leaps and bounds from last year to this after joining the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent out of Syracuse, pushing Shemar James and Curtis Robinson for one of the final LB roster spots. S Julius Wood Can the Cowboys afford to carry five safeties on the active roster? Probably not, but Julius Wood is certainly making his case they should. He’s been impressive throughout training camp and it’s carried over so far into preseason. He’s known more as a downhill number from the safety position, but has played deep, in the box, and slot for Christian Parker. That versatility and position flex is worth keeping around. He was cut last year, can he avoid that fate a second time? DT Tommy Dunn Tommy Dunn, an undrafted free agent out of Kentucky this year, is starting make some waves along the Cowboys defensive front recently. He was credited with four total pressures in Saturday’s preseason game against the Seattle Seahawks and has proven to be a strong run defender, both at the point of attack and in pursuit. With the players ahead of them on the depth chart and the number of DTs the Cowboys will likely carry on the active roster, he someone they do ideally prefer to clear waivers and re-sign to the practice squad.
author: Brian Martin

title: Cowboys news: Takeaways from joint practice with the Saints
summary: The Cowboys joint practice with the Saints had several scuffles but there were also some intriguing observations when it came to what happen on the field. Terence Steele has been the starting right tackle in Dallas for quite some time now, but unfortunately, there’s still some questions regarding if he’s the answer going forward. Christian […]
full_text: The Cowboys joint practice with the Saints had several scuffles but there were also some intriguing observations when it came to what happen on the field. Terence Steele has been the starting right tackle in Dallas for quite some time now, but unfortunately, there’s still some questions regarding if he’s the answer going forward. Christian Parker has tunnel vision when it comes to getting the defense in Dallas on point, even if its to detriment of his sleeping habits. The Cowboys were able to get veteran pass rusher Von Miller signed, but the incentives in his deal make it an even bigger win for the franchise. Notes and observations from Dallas Cowboys-New Orleans Saints joint practice – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram There were plenty of fireworks in the Cowboys joint practice with the Saints, and fists began flying on multiple occasions. However, some positive developments came about for Dallas as well. Amid Fights, Defense Finds Pass Rush Cowboys defense vs. Saints offense periods observed: 1.5 of 3 Even though this side of the field was marred by at least five scuffles, there was still some good work from the Cowboys pass rush to pull out of it. While Saints quarterback Tyler Shough had an overall solid day in the pass game, his offensive line didn’t do him many favors. Rashan Gary had two sacks, Malachi Lawrence had a sack and Shemar James had a sack in periods observed by the Star-Telegram. Mailbag: Is right tackle a concern? – Mickey Spagnola, DallasCowboys.com There were still some questions about the left tackle spot in Dallas coming into training camp. The bigger issue may be on the right side, despite Terence Steele holding down the position for several years now. Mickey: Well, who might you suggest? Starting tackles in this NFL are not a dime a dozen, and there is no obvious replacement for Terence Steele on the current roster. Worse, you might have asked who is the backup swing tackle? Did not think current backup candidate Nate Thomas did himself any favors with his performance in the Seattle preseason game and not sure you want to start or trust a fourth-round rookie in Drew Shelton to handle either of those jobs. Christian Parker’s Unhealthy Sleeping Habits Could Be Key To Dallas Cowboys Success – Randy Gurzi, SI.com Cowboys’ defensive coordinator Christian Parker is stepping into the unknown when it comes to calling plays for an entire unit. According to him, he’s not sleeping much, but that may be a good thing. The first-year defensive coordinator is so dedicated to the job that there are rumors he very rarely sleeps. During a Wednesday press conference, Parker was asked about his unhealthy sleeping habits and while he didn’t want to dive too deep into the number of hours he sleeps, Parker did admit that his focus on work often leaves him little time for himself. “That’s not something I wanna talk about. I’m not exactly proud of that, but the job has to get done. I just go down that rabbit hole and then look up and the time is gone,” Parker said via Patrik Walker. Von Miller contract incentives finally revealed, and new intel makes the Dallas Cowboys look even better – Mauricio Rodriguez, AtoZ Sports Veteran pass rusher Von Miller is now in Dallas, and it didn’t cost much to get him here. When looking at the incentives in his deal, it makes the addition even sweeter. The Dallas Cowboys’ signing of Von Miller keeps getting better and better. As I indicated in an earlier article, Miller signing a one-year contract worth $5.5 million was the perfect confirmation of the team’s intentions with him: He’s here to be a rotational piece, not a star. Well, the latest contract intel is already making the deal age like fine wine. Let’s look at the contract incentives and projected cap number. CeeDee Lamb applauds impact of Cowboys OC Klayton Adams: ‘The scheme is amazing’ – SportsDay Staff, Dallas Morning News When Klayton Adams joined the Cowboys’ staff in 2025, their running game immediately took a step up. In his second year, his detail and preparation have caught the eye of All-Pro wide receiver CeeDee Lamb. What has Klayton Adams meant to the run game last year, going into this year? What does he bring that’s difference-making? Lamb: The scheme is amazing. Oh my God. I’ll be up there in the meetings. I’m taking notes, but I’m just watching him design, and when we get into gameplanning, obviously it’s much more shorter, so right now we’re just reinstalling everything in which we did in minicamp, and we put the plays on film so we can go over it in film and see what we’re going to carry over to the season. Cowboys’ Donovan Ezeiruaku is the only thing stopping his Year 2 breakout – Jason Kandel, The Landry Hat Donovan Ezeiruaku was gotten into multiple fights during training camp. He has unlimited potential, but he needs to control himself a little better. The Cowboys have a no-fighting rule, but things always get a little chippy. The more alarming aspect of this is that NFL rules mandate players get sent off for throwing a punch. The message should have been clear after last time, especially since this defense is better with him on the field. Ezeiruaku doesn’t turn 23 until September, so while he’s obviously plenty talented, he needs to be able to keep his composure. He was also arrested this offseason for reckless driving, so it hasn’t exactly been a banner offseason for the second-year pro. Daily discussion question: Which preseason game do you think is the most important nowadays?
author: Matthew Lenix

By all accounts, he is 100% back from that injury and has looked really good in training camp so far. title: Broncos sign veteran safety Taylor Rapp
summary: According to multiple reports, including ESPN’s lead NFL insider Adam Schefter, the Denver Broncos are signing veteran safety Taylor Rapp. To make room for Rapp on the roster, the Broncos have waived/injured linebacker Levelle Bailey, according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis. He will revert to the season-ending IR list after suffering a broken leg in […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 18: Taylor Rapp #9 of the Buffalo Bills celebrates in the fourth quarter during the NFL 2025 game against Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium on September 18, 2025 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to multiple reports, including ESPN’s lead NFL insider Adam Schefter, the Denver Broncos are signing veteran safety Taylor Rapp. To make room for Rapp on the roster, th e Broncos have waived/injured linebacker Levelle Bailey , according to 9NEWS Denver’s Mike Klis. He will revert to the season-ending IR list after suffering a broken leg in the game vs. the Falcons. Former Bills safety Taylor Rapp signed today with the Denver Broncos. pic.twitter.com/yJFSKkUJyj — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) August 20, 2026 Taylor Rapp is only 28 years old and is a former 2nd-round pick in the 2019 NFL Draft by the Los Angeles Rams. He is an experienced safety with a ton of starting experience who has spent time with the Rams and previously with the Buffalo Bills, but will now join the Broncos’ secondary. During his seven seasons in the NFL, Rapp has appeared in 93 games while starting in 72 of those games. Last season, he appeared in six games for the Buffalo Bills before a knee injury ended his season, and he was placed on the injured reserve. Throughout his career, Rapp has totaled 488 tackles, 11 tackles for a loss, 2 sacks, 12 interceptions, 31 pass deflections, and 2 forced fumbles. Rapp will bring some much-needed depth to their safety position and likely fill the third safety role that was previously held by PJ Locke last season. The Broncos did not bring anyone in to fill that role during the offseason and allowed their young safeties to compete for that job throughout camp. Well, with camp ending, the Broncos did not see enough from their young players and now turn to Rapp to be their third safety this upcoming season. I really like this move because the safety depth was truly the Broncos’ only weakness on the roster. Their young linebackers appear to be stepping up, but the safety depth just never looked great. Now, Rapp adds depth, plenty of starting experience, and knowledge to that room and will provide insurance if anything were to happen to starting safeties Talanoa Hufanga or Brandon Jones. Outside of All-Pro special teamer Devon Key, the rest of the Broncos’ safety depth is now on the hot seat. JL Skinner looked to have a good showing in the preseason opener, but could be on the outside looking in. Tycen Anderson was signed as a special teams ace, but has he shown enough to make the 53-man roster? Then you have 7th-round rookie Miles Scott, who could be heading to the practice squad. We will see how it shakes out and which of these players stand out during the Broncos’ second preseason game tomorrow night vs. the Green Bay Packers. We’ll have more on this developing story soon.

title: 2026 Denver Broncos Training Camp: 5 things we learned from Broncos Camp
summary: The Denver Broncos had their final training camp practice of the summer on Wednesday and are now one step closer to their Week 1 matchup vs. their divisional rivals, the Kansas City Chiefs. This training camp lacked some of the overall drama of previous Broncos Camps, but certainly was full of storylines and developments that […]
full_text: ENGLEWOOD, CO - JULY 31: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos throws a pass during training camp at Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit on July 31, 2026 in Englewood, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos had their final training camp practice of the summer on Wednesday and are now one step closer to their Week 1 matchup vs. their divisional rivals, the Kansas City Chiefs. This training camp lacked some of the overall drama of previous Broncos Camps, but certainly was full of storylines and developments that should have all of Broncos Country excited for the weeks and months ahead. So, with all that said, here are the five things I believe we learned from Broncos Camp this year. Bo Nix is healthy and set for a big season Before camp even started, we had an idea that Nix would be good to go. He was a limited participant in the mandatory minicamp practices and was seen working out prior to camp and looking good to go. However, people still had concerns and wanted to see Nix move on the practice field and practice fully. Well, they got that and more. Nix practiced fully on Day 1, and that continued throughout the entirety of training camp. He never missed a session, took every first-team rep in team drills, and simply proved he was back to 100%. Broncos fans I asked Bo Nix all of your MANY ankle questions and concerns. Now let's believe him & move it along. @Broncos @UpAndAdamsShow pic.twitter.com/mbB8hMjWur — Kay Adams (@heykayadams) August 10, 2026 As for the season ahead, I believe Nix is set for a big year. We have seen growth each and every season, and he really turned it on late in the season last year and in the playoffs vs. Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills. He also will have newly promoted offensive coordinator and play caller Davis Webb in his ear, calling plays this season. The two have a great relationship, and it will bring some fresh ideas, aggressive plays, and hopefully a better offense moving forward. Then, you have the addition of star wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. He’s a home run threat whenever he touches the ball and will open things up for everyone on offense. This is the year Nix takes that next step, silences all the naysayers out there, and establishes himself as one of the top quarterbacks in the NFL. Pat Bryant is ready to emerge Probably the biggest winner of training camp has to be second-year wide receiver Pat Bryant. He entered camp in a battle for the WR3 spot with Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin and leaves camp as the clear winner. He was the storyline for just about every practice and became Nix’s most trusted target throughout the two weeks of camp. Veteran Courtland Sutton did not practice every day due to some load management stuff, and Jaylen Waddle and Marvin Mims missed a week plus of practices due to some minor injuries. So, Bryant was constantly out there, performed well, and simply ran away with the job. Head Coach Sean Payton was asked How the hell are you going to keep him off the field, Payton responded, “We’re not. We’re going to play him”. Pat Bryant, aka Patty 🧊, hype is real @heykayadams asked Broncos HC Sean Payton "how they're going to keep Bryant off the field " He said "we're not" pic.twitter.com/28mrMR6KQR — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 10, 2026 We saw this last season when it appeared Bryant took over the WR2 role opposite Courtland Sutton late last season. His role began to grow, and he was making plays on the field. Unfortunately, injuries derailed what looked to be a promising late season/postseason run for Bryant, but he carried that momentum into the offseason and now into training camp and hasn’t looked bad. This has Sean Payton excited for Bryant’s potential moving forward. “No. I’m excited, I’m happy because you kind of saw the beginning of it last year, but like any young player, maybe you didn’t see it as consistently as you’re seeing now. He’s a confident player with strong hands. That ability to be on the ground and not alter your feet or your foot path, I think really serves him well. Then like anything, you have a good practice, then you have two, and then pretty soon there are a couple stories, and then there’s five stories and then all of a sudden, you’re like, ‘Hey…’ You guys have seen these guys grow right before our eyes, and it’s happened, I’m sure, more than a number of times. It’s good to see.” Bryant figures to have a big role in the Broncos offense simply because he can do it all. He can play inside/outside; he is known for his blocking, strong, reliable hands, makes plays in the middle of the field and red zone, can run after the catch, and as defensive coordinator Vance Joseph noted, he’s the complete package. “He’s the guy in that room — he blocks, he catches the ball in traffic, he can track the ball vertically, he’s great in the red zone. He’s the complete package. He’s got great size and he loves to play. He’s the same player every day.” Bryant’s emergence isn’t a knock on Marvin Mims or Troy Franklin either. Mims was having an equally strong start to camp before he suffered a soft tissue injury and still figures to have a role in this offense. Troy Franklin also made some plays and had a strong finish to camp, so he will figure into the mix as well, but Bryant is still the clear winner from this group. Jaylen Waddle is going to be a difference-maker The Broncos’ big offseason addition was making a blockbuster trade with the Miami Dolphins for star wide receiver Jaylen Waddle. He gives the team a much-needed explosive playmaker who completely changes the identity of their offense, and so far, he has lived up to those expectations. Even though Waddle missed a week-plus of training camp practices due to a minor soft tissue injury, his impact on the team and the offense was evident when he was out there. He’s the fastest player on the field, runs great routes, stops and starts quickly, and is able to separate no matter who is covering him, including former Defensive Player of the Year and CB1 in the NFL, Pat Surtain II. During Wednesday’s final training camp practice, Waddle, who returned to the field this week after his injury, made arguably the play of camp. He beat and burned Surtain, who had him in one-on-one coverage DEEP for a 60-yard touchdown grab. He had a step or two on the All-Pro corner and showed off his elite speed and playmaking ability. Best pass of Camp: Bo DEEP to Waddle who burned Surtain. Perfect throw about 50-60 in air. — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) August 19, 2026 If Waddle can do this to Pat Surtain II, the best cornerback in the NFL with a Hall of Fame-caliber career, he can do it to anyone, at any time. After practice, Surtain II told reporters that Waddle is very difficult to cover, and that it’s tough, but that it’s fun to compete against a player like Waddle. “It’s very difficult as a [defensive back]. It makes you think for sure. It makes you think [about] what route he could be running and it doesn’t make him one-dimensional when he’s able to stop and start like that. It’s definitely tough, but it’s fun to compete against that.” Waddle’s impact on this offense should be immense. Not only for what he can do as a player, but also for how he should open up things around him. Waddle is an explosive playmaker who can take a simple slant 70 yards to the house if he is able to get free or just run past you on a go route and make a big play down the field. That type of playmaking ability is going to keep defenses honest and open things up for Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Evan Engram, and the rest of the Broncos’ playmakers. Sutton is typically getting a team’s best corner, but now he can use his size, strength, and elite go-up-and-get-it ability to make plays against a team’s second or third-best corner. Same goes for Bryant, who should have opportunities open up outside or inside and get plenty of one-on-one looks. The middle of the field and the flats should open up for the backs and tight…

summary: Tue Denver Broncos handled the Atlanta Falcons with ease in Week 1 of the NFL preseason. This Friday, the Broncos host the Green Bay Packers at home for their second game of their preseason slate. Here are three players Broncos Country should keep their eye on closely during the game. Kage Casey — Offensive Lineman […]
full_text: DENVER , CO - JANUARY 4: Sai'vion Jones (95) of the Denver Broncos celebrates recovering a fumble after Nik Bonitto (15) strip sacked Trey Lance (5) of the Los Angeles Chargers during the fourth quarter of the Broncos' 19-3 win at Empower Field at Mile High in Denver, Colorado on Sunday, January 4, 2026. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Tue Denver Broncos handled the Atlanta Falcons with ease in Week 1 of the NFL preseason. This Friday, the Broncos host the Green Bay Packers at home for their second game of their preseason slate. Here are three players Broncos Country should keep their eye on closely during the game. Kage Casey — Offensive Lineman The Broncos drafted Kage Casey out of Boise State with one of their fourth-round selections in the 2026 NFL Draft. A three-year starter at left tackle in college, Casey has made a switch to the inside to start his NFL career. The rookie has earned praise in camp from coaches and teammates and will be an important depth piece for Denver’s offensive line this season. In Week 1 of the preseason against the Atlanta Falcons, the rookie offensive lineman saw the most snaps of any player on offense with 66. He looked good at left guard in pass protection. I was also impressed with his ability to get to the second level with his run blocking. Earlier last week, Head Coach Sean Payton mentioned that Casey may wind up seeing some reps at center throughout the rest of training camp and the preseason. Denver is still a little banged up with injury at the position, so I’m wondering if we will see Casey get some opportunities at the pivot or if they will just roll with Calvin Throckmorton and Gavin Ortega again in Week 2 versus the Packers. https://t.co/gFGI4EsAe2 — MileHighReport (@MileHighReport) August 11, 2026 Sai’vion Jones — Defensive Lineman With the departure of John Franklin-Myers to the Tennessee Titans, the Broncos will need someone on their defensive line to step up to make up for his snap share. Eyioma Uwazurike appears poised to be first in line for an increase in reps. Uwazurike was the player to earn that nod in the preseason opener against the Falcons. Another player vying for a chance for more playing time is second-year defensive lineman Sai’vion Jones. A third-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, Jones didn’t see a lot of action last year as a rookie. Last week against Atlanta, he logged only 24 defense snaps in the second half and posted just one tackle and one quarterback hurry. It usually takes a few seasons for developmental defensive lineman to hit their stride, but I’m hoping to see more from Jones this week against the Packers. Whether it’s flashing more as a pass rusher are doing a better job against the run, Jones has a lot to show to prove he can be an important part of Denver’s defensive line rotation in 2026. RJ Harvey — Running Back RJ Harvey impressed as a versatile player for the Broncos last season as a rookie. He led all rookies in the NFL with twelve touchdowns in ‘25. Harvey was close to being a 1,000-yard all-purpose player for the team and was an integral part of the Broncos’ passing game. However, Harvey struggled to carry the load in the second half of the season as a rusher when J.K. Dobbins was hurt. Against the Falcons, Harvey had five carries for just 16 yards. That’s a 3.2 yard per carry average and certainly won’t cut the mustard when the rubber meets the road in the regular season. That’s where I’m hoping to see more growth from Harvey. Will his vision and consistency as a runner between the tackles improve? If he wants to make a jump in his second season in the NFL, it’s an absolute must. Otherwise, I can see rookie running back Jonah Coleman supplanting him as a rusher. He also didn’t have any receptions in the preseason opener, so I’m hoping to see Davis Webb and the Broncos’ offense get him involved that way.

title: Evan Engram impressed with Justin Joly and Dallen Bentley
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. With just ten days until roster cutdowns, the Denver Broncos have two preseason games remaining. This Friday, they’ll take on the Green Bay Packers. After that, the preseason finale will be a week later against the Minnesota Vikings. Those two games will be pivotal for rookies and depth players looking to […]
full_text: ENGLEWOOD, CO - JULY 31: Justin Joly #80 of the Denver Broncos stretches during training camp at Broncos Park Powered by CommonSpirit on July 31, 2026 in Englewood, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. With just ten days until roster cutdowns, the Denver Broncos have two preseason games remaining. This Friday, they’ll take on the Green Bay Packers. After that, the preseason finale will be a week later against the Minnesota Vikings. Those two games will be pivotal for rookies and depth players looking to make the final 53-man roster. One position where things are up for grabs is at tight end. This offseason, the Broncos opted to bring back all their tight ends from last season. Additionally, they utilized two selections on Day 3 of the 2026 NFL Draft to add to their room. In the fifth-round, they took North Carolina State standout Justin Joly . A lot of draft analysts thought he was a steal considering his collegiate resume. Joly was one of this past draft’s most productive tight ends. In 49 games, he reeled in 166 receptions, racked up 1,978 receiving yards, and 15 touchdowns. In the seventh-round, the Broncos selected Utah prospect Dallen Bentley . After having just three catches in between his sophomore and junior campaigns, Bentley had a meteoric rise in production as a senior. He hauled in 48 catches for 620 yards and 6 touchdowns for the Utes in 2025. Yesterday after practice, veteran tight end Evan Engram spoke highly of their progression since being drafted. “They’ve been doing great. ‘DB’ and Justin have been awesome. They’ve been learning. Rookies have their moments and they take their bumps and their bruises, but they’ve been responding really well,” stated Engram with respect to his first impressions of the Broncos’ newest additions at tight end. “They’re competing. They’re handling things the right way. They’re doing well in a difficult offense to learn, especially as a rookie, but very proud of the progress they’ve made.” With the steep learning curve at the position, t’s unlikely either will be major pieces in the Broncos’ offensive plans for the upcoming season. However, both have the traits and talent to grow into starting-level players. In the preseason opener versus the Falcons, Joly and Bentley both saw 23 snaps on offense. However, the duo was only targeted once in the passing game, with Joly securing a catch that went for no yards. Over the next two weeks, I’m looking forward to seeing them get some targets. Both flashed in college with their receiving ability. I’m hoping Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb can direct some plays their way against Green Bay and Minnesota. From my perspective, Joly looks like a potential heir apparent to Engram giving his versatility and utilization as a move tight end, while Bentley has the size and blocking ability to have a shot to be a future player at inline for the franchise. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .
