title: If Stetson Bennett hits trade block, Browns make most sense
summary: Even with Ty Simpson waiting in the wings for the starting job someday, Stetson Bennett remains in the lead to be the L.A. Rams backup quarterback behind Matthew Stafford. However, if the Rams decide that Simpson is ready to be Stafford’s backup already, then there could be a situation developing with the Cleveland Browns that […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - AUGUST 15: Quarterback Stetson Bennett IV #13 of the Los Angeles Rams prepares to hand off the football in the first quarter of an NFL preseason game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Even with Ty Simpson waiting in the wings for the starting job someday, Stetson Bennett remains in the lead to be the L.A. Rams backup quarterback behind Matthew Stafford. However, if the Rams decide that Simpson is ready to be Stafford’s backup already, then there could be a situation developing with the Cleveland Browns that makes a trade connection seem plausible, according to analysts at ESPN. Kevin Clark of ESPN raised the idea this week on an episode of “The Mina Kimes Show,” trying to advance the idea that Bennett’s college offensive coordinator, Todd Monken, might be interested in injecting Bennett into the quarterback battle with his current team, the Browns. “Who was Stetson Bennett’s college offensive coordinator, who just swears by the guy?” Clark asked, continuing: “They had a rocky relationship but they ended up winning national championships over it, and now he speaks glowingly…Should [the Browns] go out and get another quarterback? I’m just throwing it out there.” There is some logic behind all of this. Clark laid out why it makes sense for the team that would be acquiring Bennett. As for the Rams, they obviously have a lot invested in Ty Simpson already while Bennett is clearly not part of the franchise’s long-term plans. He’s only under contract through this season as it is. Any potential return for Bennett would be modest at best, of course. Los Angeles couldn’t make a move for a completely conditional pick, that’s not nearly valuable enough for a current backup quarterback, even if he’s not exactly the best one in the sport. But you aren’t going to recoup his initial draft capital cost from 2023 either (a fourth-round pick), so the front office would have to weigh whether or not Bennett is worth a sixth, or even more likely seventh, rounder. Ty Simpson is more physically gifted than Stetson Bennett. So Simpson has a chance to become a starter, and Bennett does not. Bennett, who doesn't have starter upside, thrived in the preseason last year. Preseason football is a place for everybody who made it this far. — TurfShowTimes (@TurfShowTimes) August 16, 2026 The biggest risk here is that Matthew Stafford misses a prolonged amount of time and Simpson simply isn’t ready to play. If you ship Bennett out, you’re one unfortunate play away from that reality. Then, you’re talking about finding another option who could survive in the system for multiple games, which at this moment would include … Jimmy Garoppolo ? Admittedly, this scenario is unlikely. The return would have to blow Les Snead’s socks off (and probably Sean McVay’s, too) and Simpson would have to have had a genuinely superb, transcendent camp and preseason. We know Simpson is entering the NFL as a project with limited playing time from college, so putting the backup job for a Super Bowl contender on his shoulders is a massive ask. That’s not intended to oversell Bennett, who has played a whopping zero snaps in the NFL since being drafted in 2023. However, he has been with the team since then, he’s familiar with their expectations and he at least knows the system. All those things combined are why this is an interesting hypothetical. Of course, the Browns seem content to just let Sanders and Watson duke it out in one of the more unpleasant quarterback battles of recent memory, so that option may not be on the table after all.

title: Rams have fared well in international games in LA return
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are three weeks away from playing the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. Between the excitement of the upcoming season and the league’s recent desire to have an NFL team outside the US, let’s look at how the Rams have fared overseas. Since the start of the NFL International Series, the Rams […]
full_text: Fans arriving before the NFL International match at the Wembley Stadium, London. Picture date: Sunday October 19, 2025. Photo credit should read: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire. RESTRICTIONS: Use subject to restrictions. Editorial use only, no commercial use without prior consent from rights holder. (Photo by Bradley Collyer/PA Images via Getty Images) | PA Images via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are three weeks away from playing the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. Between the excitement of the upcoming season and the league’s recent desire to have an NFL team outside the US, let’s look at how the Rams have fared overseas. Since the start of the NFL International Series, the Rams have gone 3-2. Their five games are tied with the Patriots and Raiders for the most in the league, behind the Jaguars (14), Dolphins (7) and Vikings (6). The team’s season opener will be their first played outside London. Their 2018 thriller against the Chiefs was originally supposed to be played in Mexico City, but was moved to the LA Coliseum because of poor field conditions at Estadio Azteca . Los Angeles is also currently on a three-game overseas winning streak, all have which have occurred in the Sean McVay era. Patriots 45, Rams 7 (2012) Sam Bradford and company didn’t stand a chance. In their only international game while based in St. Louis , the Rams actually scored first in this one. However, it was all Tom Brady and the Patriots from there. New England scored on its first five possessions and ran up a 28-7 lead at halftime. Brady threw four touchdown passes, including two to Rob Gronkowski, who finished with 146 yards on eight receptions. Okay, moving on, nothing else to see here! Giants 17, Rams 10 (2016) This one was at least competitive, but still managed to be quite ugly. LA starter Case Keenum threw four interceptions, with two of them going to Giants safety Landon Collins. In this one, Collins’ had his iconic 44-yard pick-six — you know the one — which led to New York tying the game about halfway through the second quarter. The Giants were offensively challenged throughout game, as they were outgained by 113 yards. Turnovers simply made the difference. Keenum was also mercifully benched for a rookie Jared Goff a few weeks later. Rams 33, Cardinals 0 (2017) Finally a win! The Rams notched their first overseas victory in a dominant win over the rival Cardinals. Arizona was outgained 425-196 and amassed only 10 first downs compared to LA’s 28. Los Angeles held the ball for nearly 40 minutes, as the Cards with an aging Adrian Peterson in the backfield rushed for 25(!) yards. Zoo-wee mama! That win helped propel the Rams to a surprise NFC West title in McVay’s first season. Rams 24, Bengals 10 (2019) Call this the OG Cooper Kupp game. Against the winless Bengals, Kupp torched Cincinnati to the tune of 220 receiving yards on seven receptions. Best of all, he did it in just over a half, with 165 of those yards coming before halftime. The highlight of the matchup was a 65-yard touchdown pass on a double reverse flea-flicker that put the Rams ahead for good in the second quarter. Cincy finished a league-worst 2-14, but managed to select Heisman Trophy winner Joe Burrow with the top overall pick in the 2020 NFL draft. Burrow, as we know, helped lead the Bengals back to the Super Bowl in his second season as starter, where they’d lose to Kupp and the Rams. Rams 35, Jaguars 7 (2025) It’s amazing to think this was the Rams’ first international game in six years, and the lone one for Stafford in an LA uniform to date entering this season. Stafford certainly made the most of it by having five touchdown passes, despite throwing for under 200 yards. Three of those touchdown passes went to Davante Adams, who would finish atop the NFL leaderboard with receiving touchdowns at seasons end. Matthew Stafford faced a season-high 55.9% blitz rate against the Jaguars and threw all five of his touchdowns against the blitz. Stafford tied Patrick Mahomes and Baker Mayfield for the most TD passes against the blitz in any game since 2016. #LARvsJAX | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/kkDwSMpf5B — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) October 19, 2025 Additionally, Stafford’s five touchdown passes were the most thrown in an international game. While he didn’t get knighted following his performance, he did eventually earn All-Pro and MVP honors. Hopefully, he can have an encore down under, and put the Whiners on the barbie while he’s at it.
author: Evan Craig

title: Aaron Donald risks tarnishing his legacy if he stays retired
summary: As Aaron Donald continues to tease fans with indirect hints that he’s working towards a comeback with the Los Angeles Rams, he also risks alienating and frustrating those same people who believe he’s returning if he later announces that he’s going to stay retired. Even if it’s his right to make an attempt, and even […]
full_text: THOUSAND OAKS, CALIFORNIA - FEBRUARY 11: Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams during practice in preparation for Super Bowl LVI at California Lutheran University on February 11, 2022 in Thousand Oaks, California. The Rams will play against the Cincinnati Bengals in Super Bowl LVI on February 13. (Photo by Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images) | Getty Images As Aaron Donald continues to tease fans with indirect hints that he’s working towards a comeback with the Los Angeles Rams, he also risks alienating and frustrating those same people who believe he’s returning if he later announces that he’s going to stay retired. Even if it’s his right to make an attempt, and even if he’s being genuine in his interest to come back, it’s been nearly three months of speculation already — that he’s fueled himself — and Rams fans are expressing a contempt for seeing Aaron Donald’s name in the news that we’ve never seen before. If Donald comes back, then he’s a hero. If he doesn’t though, some Rams fans will feel they’ve been used. I'm to the point where I feel the need to mute the words "Aaron Donald" on this app until after this does or does not happen. https://t.co/g02LdpKrtR — SeattleRams (@seattlerams_nfl) August 16, 2026 On June 1, 2026, Donald made an Instagram post of him working out with the hashtag “#ready” that many people ran with as an indication that he’s on the precipice of making a return announcement. Ironically, we’ve since had 10 weeks of Aaron Donald headlines that make it clear, “He’ll only come back when he’s ready.” So…I guess he wasn’t #ready then? No, in fact, that’s not even why Donald used that hashtag, which some of you already know. Maybe it’s the fact that most Rams fans don’t know why he used the word “ready” that has inspired this many headlines about Aaron Donald to be created. Ready is the name of his protein bar and sports drink franchise. @ready_nutrition Ready® Co-Owner @Aaron Donald shares his favorite Ready® products and why he’s proud to be part of a brand he truly believes in. Ready® was thrilled to be part of this special day with Aaron and the @AD99Foundation #fyp #aarondonald #protein #proteinbar #proteinwater #interview ♬ original sound – Team Ready In one of the most electric interviews of all-time, Donald reveals that his favorite Ready protein bar is… chocolate peanut butter! On June 2, one day after his #ready post, that’s when Pat McAfee goes on his show and tells the world that he texted Donald and that the Myles Garrett trade has “got me thinking” about a return . Who would ever accuse McAfee of being brand-focused and financially motivated? You wake up and open Draft Kings. You hammer the Pat McAfee featured parlay just like normal. You turn on ESPN and watch Pat McAfee debate AI Pat McAfee. During the 16 straight commercials you play the new McAfee album. Banger. You DoorDash the new Pat McAfee meal. Life is good. — Karen McGee (@karenmotherof2) August 14, 2026 But to be fair, Donald hasn’t say much about Ready since June 1, and really he hasn’t said anything at all. If this were to promote his brand, he’s doing a very bad job at it. Donald isn’t speaking to the media, he’s not taking interviews, he’s not going on podcasts, which are all things he could be doing with his name in the news every day. Certainly an Aaron Donald appearance on McAfee this week would get millions of views even if he didn’t want to talk about coming out of retirement. That’s how much interest there is around him right now. So we can assume that Donald’s training, and his two official workouts with the Rams when he used their facilities in an official capacity, are all genuine efforts to see if he can play and maybe get a second Super Bowl ring. This still wouldn’t stop the fact that many Rams fans are getting tired of news about a player who isn’t on the team and who they fear still won’t be when all these rumors stop. In a recent Feed post by our own John Newman, “Do you think Donald is serious?”, many fans talked about Donald in a way that I’ve never heard Rams fans talk about Aaron Donald before. Here are some of the top comments: SlowTightEnd: “Actually, I don’t think he’s serious. And, I think it’s an unnecessary distraction for the team. Frankly, AD was seriously injured in that 2022 fiasco season and missed a lot of games. Then he was good in 2023, but not his former sensational self. I sure wish we’d had him in 2024 and 2025. Especially the latter year where just another sack or two versus Sam Darnold would’ve likely meant a SB Championship. But after two years off and at age 35, no $30M payday please.“ And I’m not highlighting any of your comments to disparage fans or Donald. This is just how many people are starting to feel and let’s call a spade a spade: It’s fascinating and unexpected. Ramaha: “At this point I don’t really care. The Rams don’t need him. This is an asinine luxury. Play or don’t. Think the Rams players are tired as hell about questions about AD. At what point does he become a distraction?“ What was once a fun idea has now become an unwelcome distraction. Rams62: “If he isn’t serious about coming back then I think this is lousy and cheap way to get some attention.“ And therein lies the heart of the problem if Donald doesn’t come out of retirement. Even if it’s just because he tried and decided he doesn’t have the juice anymore, perception is reality. Many will feel duped. ohramsfan: “I think since it was disclosed he has a production group in place for a possible documentary, that’s all this is, meaning promotion for his yet to be filmed documentary… I hope he proves me wrong, but the longer it goes the less I believe him returning.“ If an AD documentary does get released in the future, detailing these months, it could do more harm than good. Just another fake reality show? Tom House: “He’s like a week away from slightly tarnishing his otherwise impeccable legacy. Only ’cause indecision makes you look weak.“ This comment was 3 days ago, so the clock is ticking on the decision. Although Aaron Donald tarnishing his legacy with Rams fans would be like Tom Cruise tarnishing his legacy with the Church of Scientology (meaning there’s almost no wrong that can be done), he’s still going from infallible to fallible the longer this drags out. Maybe Donald just doesn’t want to be added to the roster yet. It could behoove the team to wait until after final cuts. But these reports could have stayed in the shadows. Sean McVay could have refused to talk about Donald to the media, and instead he is surprisingly candid about it and happy to receive questions that aren’t actually about the team. That feels a little unusual and perhaps he’s too elated to talk about Donald. Does he know the outcome already? If Aaron Donald announces his return this month, his reputation with Rams fans will go above heights we ever thought was possible. Even if he’s not his old self, fans will appreciate the effort. However, if Donald stays retired, and then goes on McAfee and promotes Ready protein bars, and releases a documentary about his attempt to return, his legacy will take a hit that we’ve never seen before.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams vs Saints: How to watch on TV, stream or listen on radio
summary: Coming off an opening week 20-12 win on the road against the Kansas City Chiefs, the Los Angeles Rams return home and roll out the welcome mat for the New Orleans Saints. The Week 2 matchup at SoFi Stadium is set for Saturday August 22, with kickoff scheduled for 1 p.m. PST. It will be […]
full_text: Rams tight end Davis Allen shows the proper straight arm technique (Photo by Ronald Martinez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Coming off an opening week 20-12 win on the road against the Kansas City Chiefs, the Los Angeles Rams return home and roll out the welcome mat for the New Orleans Saints. The Week 2 matchup at SoFi Stadium is set for Saturday August 22, with kickoff scheduled for 1 p.m. PST. It will be a long week for the Saints, along with Week 2 of the NFL preseason, they will have participated in two controlled scrimmages this week. They took on the Dallas Cowboys on Tuesday and are mixing it up with the Rams today. New Orleans second-year coach Kellen Moore approaches preseason games similarly to L.A. head man Sean McVay, he sits a lot of his contributors and generally puts the bottom half of his roster into action. The Rams took it a bit farther and did not play 41 players. Hard to put a finger on how this game will play out, with all the bottom of the roster players involved, there’s reason to think it could recede into a mistake-filled snooze fest. summary: The Los Angeles Rams have had some injuries on the offensive line and Alaric Jackson could be suspended, so with Taylor Decker still one of the best overall free agents available right now, would Les Snead want to add the veteran tackle as an insurance policy? Decker and Matthew Stafford have experience together from their […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-December21: Offensive tackle Taylor Decker (68) of the Detroit Lions walks on the field ahead of an NFL football game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, December 21, 2025. (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams have had some injuries on the offensive line and Alaric Jackson could be suspended, so with Taylor Decker still one of the best overall free agents available right now , would Les Snead want to add the veteran tackle as an insurance policy? Decker and Matthew Stafford have experience together from their days with the Detroit Lions, so the reigning MVP would likely have some information for the team to consider, if it came to making a move on his former teammate. DO IT: Should Los Angeles Rams REUNITE Matthew Stafford with THIS Free Agent Tackle to Solve Issues? (11alive.com) “With Keagen Trost out “a few weeks” and Alaric Jackson likely facing a suspension, the Los Angeles Rams could turn to free agent tackle Taylor Decker to add OL depth” Los Angeles Rams vs. New Orleans Saints: How to watch, listen to and live stream 2026 Preseason Week 2 (therams.com) “The Rams host the Saints on Saturday at SoFi Stadium for Week 2 of the NFL preseason, in what will be Los Angeles’ lone home game of the preseason. The two teams last met in Week 8 of the 2025 season at SoFi Stadium, where the Rams beat the Saints 34-10. Quarterback Matthew Stafford went 24-for-32 passing for 281 yards and four touchdowns, and wide receiver Puka Nacua had a team-high 95 yards while Davante Adams led the team with two receiving touchdowns. Running back Kyren Williams went for 114 yards on the ground and a touchdown on 4.6 yards per carry. Defensively, cornerback Emmanuel Forbes Jr. had an interception and defensive end Braden Fiske had a sack and a tackle for loss. Kickoff for Saturday’s game is scheduled for 1:00 p.m. pacific time on Rams TV affiliate KCBS.“ NFL Preseason Week 2: Saints-Rams and the exhibition games that matter this week (fansided) “Still thinking we could get some official word on Aaron Donald’s future by this weekend. I don’t think he’s going through all of this to opt to stay retired, and he also doesn’t have to be ready to go Week 1. This is about the Super Bowl in LA. Ty Simpson was nearly perfect against the Chiefs last week. Sean McVay knows how to bring a QB along, but this was pretty ridiculous even for him. Hard to think Simpson could pull that off again. McVay tends to be very careful about who he plays and what he shows in the preseason and if Simpson does duplicate that outing, will he be put on ice till the regular season, too?“ Frustrating end to Rams receiver’s preseason is painful deja vu (ramblinfan) “The Rams announced the move alongside the addition of former Raiders receiver Alex Bachman, who has five career catches for 43 yards. Williams’ bad luck continues for second straight year with Rams Williams was waived last season on August 19, and let go two days later. There has been no update on whether Williams’ return timeline changed from a “few weeks” into something more severe, prompting the Rams to remove him the active offseason roster. If he goes unclaimed on waivers, the Rams can either place him on injured reserve or release him with an injury settlement. According to transaction logs, Williams agreed to the latter in 2025 a day after landing on IR.“ Beat still unsure if Rams will extend Puka Nacua (nbcsports) “Nacua is entering the final year of his contract. Atkins writes that it is only a matter of time before “Nacua lands a monstrous extension,” but whether it comes from the Rams or another team, presumably via free agency or a trade, remains a question. Both the team and player reportedly “hope” that Nacua remains a Ram long term, and the team is “encouraged by some of the steps he’s taken this offseason.” The superstar wide receiver still has a civil suit that must be dealt with and the league has not yet clarified whether it intends to suspend him. For now, Nacua is a member of the Rams’ explosive offense and can be treated as a locked-in WR1, albeit with some suspension risk.” What New Puka Nacua Trial Date Means for Rams and Possible NFL Suspension (si.com) “With the trial now set for 2028, the NFL may have to make a decision on Nacua well before the civil case is resolved. While the legal process hasn’t taken its course, the NFL can discipline a player even without criminal charges. It’s unlikely that the NFL will wait 19 months for the trial to take place. The NFL can still interview Nacua and his accuser as well as witnesses to help inform their decision. With that said, if the NFL doesn’t believe that it has enough evidence to make a decision, the league could close the investigation and Nacua wouldn’t face discipline.” LA Rams’ $124 Million All-Pro Projected to End Pro Bowl Drought (sports.yahoo) “The prediction stands out because McDuffie owns first-team and second-team All-Pro honors from his time with the Kansas City Chiefs , yet he has never received a Pro Bowl nod. Patra wrote in his NFC first-time Pro Bowl candidates that McDuffie had been “ignored by Pro Bowl voters” in Kansas City and suggested his move to Los Angeles could finally change that. He also mentioned McDuffie’s versatility and willingness to contribute against the run as reasons he is at the top of the league for his position.” 2 Reasons The Los Angeles Rams’ 2026 Season Could Be Turbulent (stadiumrant) “The first reason the Rams’ 2026 season could be a bit disappointing is the age of quarterback Matthew Stafford . He is currently 38 years old. It’s an age that doesn’t guarantee success for the next season. Quarterbacks who typically reach that age range have declined quickly. The two most recent examples are Peyton Manning and Aaron Rodgers. In 2013, Manning was the best quarterback in the league. He threw for a record-breaking 5,477 yards and 55 touchdowns with a 115.1 passer rating. That was Manning’s age 37 season. Just two years later, he threw for nine touchdowns and 17 interceptions and missed a handful of games. It was the worst season of his career.” Rams All-Pro Puka Nacua misses practice with muscle soreness. McVay expects him to return next week (apnews) “Head coach Sean McVay said Nacua felt the soreness in his psoas — a muscle that runs from the back through the pelvis to the legs. “Puka is doing good,” McVay said. “We’re just being smart with him. Expect him to be back next week, ready to go.” Nacua is heading into his fourth season with the Rams in the final year of his rookie contract, but he has been a full participant in training camp and preseason workouts. The two-time Pro Bowl selection led the NFL with 129 receptions last season and ranked second with 1,715 yards receiving. Defensive end Myles Garrett also skipped Thursday’s practice to rest his knee, which has swelled at times during the past month with the Rams. Garrett also is expected to be in practice next week.” 2026 NFL Preseason Week 2: 10 things to watch (nfl.com) “Every NFL team handles the preseason differently these days, but typically, Week 1 is something of an amuse-bouche: a small bite to tickle the taste buds. In Week 2, we’re in for more of a hearty appetizer. The main course is still a few weeks away, but this stage of the meal should provide enough nourishment (i.e., starter snaps) to tide us over for a bit. So, what’s on offer across the NFL? I have an apps menu! Below, you’ll find this week’s 16-game schedule, followed by 10 things to watch — and I’ve divided my analysis into four different subsections for your tasting delights. Bon appétit!” Comment of the Day: Not time to panic, but there are some valid reasons to be concerned about this team in L.A.…

title: Fernando Mendoza has some struggles in preseason win over Houston
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders played at the Houston Texans on Thursday night in a 22-20 win at the Houston Texans. Here are some highlights: As expected, the Raiders starting offense didn’t play. That is a strong indication that Kirk Cousins is very much the expected starter for Week 1. The only starter to play with […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 20: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders looks to pass during the second quarter of the game against the Houston Texans at NRG Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders played at the Houston Texans on Thursday night in a 22-20 win at the Houston Texans. Here are some highlights: As expected, the Raiders starting offense didn’t play. That is a strong indication that Kirk Cousins is very much the expected starter for Week 1. The only starter to play with rookie Fernando Mendoza was wide receiver Jalen Nailor. Playing against Houston’s second-string offense (the Texans gave their starters the night off after their dominant performance against the Raiders in the joint practice Tuesday) Mendoza hit Nailor for a 22-yard gainer. But the drive went sour for Mendoza when he threw an 80-yard Pick Six to rookie linebacker Wade Woodaz. Mendoza threw the ball behind his target. It was a bad throw by the rookie. ESPN has unveiled a new scorebug for the 2026 NFL season: pic.twitter.com/Gs9BgRAuzK — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) August 21, 2026 After some struggles, Mendoza hit fellow rookie Malik Benson for an 18-yard completion. They have build a good chemistry this summer. Benson did have two drops later in the quarter. He will have to prove he can deliver in the regular season. Mendoza, who was under a lot of pressure behind the No. 2 offensive line, had some issues, but did connect on six straight passes at one point. He was facing the Texans’ third-string defense some in the second quarter. He didn’t play after the first half. He completed 8 of 15 passes for 86 yards with the one interception. His quarterback rating was 42.6. It wasn’t a great night for the No. 1 overall pick. He was better last week against Arizona. But it’s a learning process. It will be interesting to see how much he plays next week in the preseason finale against San Francisco. While there had been some media momentum that Mendoza, who played a lot under center with a weak offensive line, could steal the starting job for Week 1, but it seems like Cousins is still very much the leader for the job. However, coach Klint Kubiak refused to name Cousins the starter Thursday night. Kubiak said Mendoza has “plenty he can learn from,” this performance. The Raiders’ first-unit defense didn’t play after having a rough go of it in the preseason opener against Arizona last week and in a joint practice at Houston on Tuesday. Star defensive end Maxx Crosby didn’t play last week and likely won’t play again until the season opener at home against the Miami Dolphins on September 13. Crosby is returning from a knee surgery and he has been working every day at training camp and he did work against the Texans on Tuesday. The Texans got the ball first and most of their starters, including quarterback C.J. Stroud, were in the field. Cornerback Darien Porter was the Raiders’ only possible starter on defense. Other Raiders’ starters included defensive end Malcolm Koonce, and rookies, cornerback Zeke Masses and safety Treydan Stukes. The Texans ate up the Raiders on the ground early. It was predictable because the Raiders’ ground defense has been bad this summer and Houston starting tailback Woody Marks was playing and he finished the drive with a 20-yard touchdown run, with several broken tackles, against the Raiders’ overmatched second unit. Stroud beat Porter on third and 11 on the first drive. Las Vegas defensive coordinator Rob Leonard was blitzing some, but the Raiders couldn’t generate much pressure early. The Raiders’ deep backups came back from a 20-3 deficit, capped by a 98-yard drive led by Aidan O’Connell in the final 97 seconds of the game. O’Connell, a very strong No. 3 quarterback, was 15 of 24 passing for 166 yards. Drives like that could help the Raiders trade O’Connell by the August 30 53-man roster deadline if they wish. The kicking battle is probably over. Veteran Matt Gay hit a 52-yard field goal in the second quarter. He is leading the battle with rookie Kansie Matsuzawa, who really hurt himself with two missed extra points, following a poor showing last week. It’s very likely Gay will win the kicking job. Matsuzawa could stick around on the practice squad. The Texans’ second-team offense took over on their second drive. So, the only team either team had most of their starters on the field was when Houston’s offense had the first drive of the game. Rookie running back Mike Washington continued to flash with a 33-yard run. He has been great this summer and will get playing time. Rookie cornerback Jermod McCoy had a great play in the second quarter, but was called for taunting (yes, it was a weak call). But his coverage was vital after a rough game last week, his first since injuring his knee in 2024. Jordan Meredith was the Raiders’ starting center. The Raiders continued to be sloppy with nine penalties. They have 17 in two games. Defensive end Patrick Johnson has flashed big time and had a big strip sack, and could maybe be a bubble player. Stukes and linebacker Tommy Eichenberg (who struggled last week) made some plays. Stukes, a second-round pick, really stood out after a slow training camp. It will be interesting to see how much he plays early in the regular season. Dylan Laube was a factor as a receiver out of the backfield and then scored on a 4-yard run in the third quarter. He has a strong chance to stick around on the 53-man roster again. The Texans were 6 of 8 on third down and had seven plays of 10 or more yards in the first half. Raiders’ defensive lineman Thomas Booker had a sack in the second quarter. The Raiders’ backups ran well and former Texans’ running back Dare Ogunbowale Linebacker Buddy Johnson suffered a shoulder injury. The cart came out for cornerback Chigozie Anusiem, who had a knee injury. It did nto look for good the player, who was facing an uphill battle to make the 53-man roster. Newly signed defensive tackle Foley Fatukasi was active late in the game. Jack Bech, Porter and A.J. Cole were the Raiders’ captains in the game. Reserve pass-rushers Jahfari Harvey and Cian Slone played well. Slone has had a good preseason. In the end, the comeback from the deep backups was nice, but it was a fairly sloppy overall game for Las Vegas. Hey, it’s the preseason and this was a typical preseason game.

title: Raiders Film Room: Kubiak has a plan for Mike Washington JR
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders drafted Mike Washington Jr. in the fourth round of the 2026 draft. This shows the Raiders have a vision for playing smash-mouth football with a mix of Washington Jr. and Ashton Jeanty. Washington Jr. comes from a system at Arkansas that was different from Klint Kubiak’s. At Arkansas, Washington Jr. ran […]
full_text: Aug 13, 2026; Paradise, Nevada, USA; Las Vegas Raiders running back Mike Washington Jr. (30) carries the ball against the Arizona Cardinals in the first half at Allegiant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Las Vegas Raiders drafted Mike Washington Jr. in the fourth round of the 2026 draft. This shows the Raiders have a vision for playing smash-mouth football with a mix of Washington Jr. and Ashton Jeanty. Washington Jr. comes from a system at Arkansas that was different from Klint Kubiak’s. At Arkansas, Washington Jr. ran a gap scheme primarily, whereas Kubiak prefers a wide zone scheme. The question became what plan would best maximize Washington Jr.’s talents at the next level. The first preseason game of 2026 gave fans a taste of what it could look like when Washington Jr. is the running back. He finished with 63 yards on six carries with an explosive 53-yard run in the second quarter. Kubiak’s plan is to get Washington Jr. in space. Of the six carries, three were wide zone or a toss play. An example is below in the 2nd quarter. Raiders run an outside zone play to help get him in space to the outside. Washington Jr. does a good job reading and getting outside with patience, allowing blocks to develop, and gets 4 yards. All the other runs were gap scheme runs or duo. Duo is a run where the running back starts his flow on the strong-side A gap. Then Washington Jr. reads the blocks and chooses which gap he wants to hit. Of course, on this run there was excellent blocking in front of him to allow him to get to the second level. He does the rest and ends with a 53 yard run. The blocking on this Mike Washington Jr run. Grant, Mafi, and Meredith set it up. Jack Bech with the crack opens it up late, and Washington Jr does the rest. pic.twitter.com/4pjdAWrgtC — Marcus Johnson (@TheMarcJohnNFL) August 14, 2026 Washington Jr. exhibited the home run ability that makes him an intriguing one-two punch with Jeanty. Kubiak has a plan for the young running back, and it is off to a great start.

title: Miami Dolphins fans shouldn’t panic after rough day against New York Giants
summary: Miami Dolphins fans could be forgiven for feeling a little uneasy after Thursday’s joint practice with the New York Giants. The Dolphins’ offense struggled to consistently move the football, while the Giants’ pass rush repeatedly found its way into the backfield. But before anyone declares the season over in August, there is an important piece […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 20: Malik Washington #6 of the Miami Dolphins speak to the media after a joint practice with the New York Giants at Baptist Health Training Complex on August 20, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Rich Storry/Getty Images) | Getty Images Miami Dolphins fans could be forgiven for feeling a little uneasy after Thursday’s joint practice with the New York Giants. The Dolphins’ offense struggled to consistently move the football, while the Giants’ pass rush repeatedly found its way into the backfield. But before anyone declares the season over in August, there is an important piece of context to remember — this was a joint practice, not a regular-season game . Head coach Jeff Hafley has been very clear about what he wants from these sessions. Rather than wasting time designing a game plan specifically to beat the opposing team, Miami’s new head-man-in-charge wants his players to face difficult situations and find out who can execute. That philosophy was particularly evident on Thursday against New York when the team’s offensive line couldn’t handle blitzes the Giants were sending Malik Willis’ way. The Giants certainly provided a difficult test. Their defensive front consistently created pressure, with Abdul Carter, Brian Burns, Kayvon Thibodeaux and others making life difficult for Malik Willis. Reports indicated the Giants recorded at least six sacks, with Brian Burns suggesting the actual number was even higher. But Willis offered perhaps the most important perspective afterward. The Dolphins quarterback acknowledged the Giants’ defensive success while pointing out that Miami wasn’t game planning specifically for the Giants. He said, “ We weren’t game planning for those guys, ” adding that the offense would have “ a few better options on some plays where we were just kind of stuck, ” if it had been a regular season contest. That’s the distinction Dolphins fans should keep in mind. Miami absolutely needs to improve its pass protection. Thursday exposed problems that coaches will undoubtedly put under the microscope, but the Dolphins also weren’t unveiling their regular-season offensive plan. The real test comes when Miami has a week to study an opponent, identify its tendencies and build a protection plan specifically designed to neutralize its best pass rushers. So, yes, Thursday was ugly. But ugly film in August can be useful film. And if Hafley and his staff learn from it, that may ultimately be exactly what this joint practice was supposed to accomplish.

(Photo by Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images) Last week, I asked the following question about former Miami Dolphins greats: If you could choose only one, which former Miami Dolphins player, in their prime, do you believe would translate to today’s game, and why would you place them on the team’s current roster? Below are some of your thoughts and answers- Longtimefan points to the greatest QB this team has ever seen. Dan Marino, and to me it’s not even a close second. Marino was a difference-maker at the most important position in football. Miami7 says it’s obvious, but I have seen plenty of Phins fans who aren’t as high on Marino as some of us who actually got to see him play. The question ‘should have’ been stated “other than Marino”….obvious James, no? Csonka would relegate Achane to a Mercury Morris role (under-utilized by no fault of his own, though Achane as a receiving threat is by far superior). Today’s team/roster? I think JT would be the guy. ………..Larry Little was a great response. Kuech is up there too! Warfield (my all-time fave) or Clayton were great as well. With Zach/AJ or Buonicontti, we have a solid LB corps so they’re presence less ‘needed’ currently. Surtain/Madison/X would all be solid answers. Oldarmyguy went with a guy who hated the Bills so much that he said he would retire rather than play for them. Bryan Cox for sure. Fits the new culture Hafley wants. title: Dolphins rumors include eyeing Packers’ Carrington Valentine
summary: The Miami Dolphins could be looking to make a move to bolster their defensive secondary. According to Easton Butler, the Dolphins have been in contact with the Green Bay Packers about the availability of cornerback Carrington Valentine. Given Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley moved to Miami this offseason after having been the Packers’ defenisve coordinator, […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - JANUARY 10: Carrington Valentine #24 of the Green Bay Packers looks on during an NFL wild card playoff game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on January 10, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins could be looking to make a move to bolster their defensive secondary. According to Easton Butler , the Dolphins have been in contact with the Green Bay Packers about the availability of cornerback Carrington Valentine. Given Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley moved to Miami this offseason after having been the Packers’ defenisve coordinator, there is a familiarity with Valentine built into the Dolphins’ decision makers. Valentine was a seventh-round pick by the Packers in 2023. Since being selected, he has appeared in 49 games, including 30 starts, and recorded 107 tackles, 18 passes defensed, two interceptions, two forced fumbles, and a fumble recovery. According to Butler, the Cincinnati Bengals and Pittsburgh Steelers have also reached out to Green Bay about Valentine’s availability. The Packers have Valentine listed as a starter on their unofficial depth chart, and they could be looking to keep him in that role heading into the season – making a trade unlikely unless some team is willing to overpay in the deal. Green Bay already has question marks at depth for their cornerbacks and is dealing with injuries, including a hamstring issue for Valentine, and it would again seem to make a trade unlikely. Would you make a trade for Valentine? What would you offer the Packers to add the former seventh-round pick? Head to the comments to let us know.

title: Dolphins tackle Austin Jackson ejected from Giants joint practice
summary: The Miami Dolphins are hosting the New York Giants in a joint practice on Thursday, giving both teams a chance to workout against another team and different players. The experience against another team is important for both the players and the coaches trying to get a full evaluation of the team. The situation does lead […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 30: Austin Jackson #73 of the Miami Dolphins takes the field prior to a game against the New Orleans Saints at Hard Rock Stadium on November 30, 2025 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are hosting the New York Giants in a joint practice on Thursday, giving both teams a chance to workout against another team and different players. The experience against another team is important for both the players and the coaches trying to get a full evaluation of the team. The situation does lead to frustration at times, however, as one side does things a little differently or executes a drill at a different speed. That frustration can boil over, though Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley has said he will not tolerate those frustration turning into something dirty. “Should there be a punch? No, if there’s a punch thrown, they’re out,” Hafley told the media prior to the team’s joint practice against the Washington Commanders last week. “And that’s what I told the team. It’s exactly what I’ve told the team throughout camp. And we’ve been fortunate, there haven’t been a lot of fights. We don’t have time for that.” On Thursday, right tackle Austin Jackson discovered Hafley is more than just words; he upholds the standards he sets. According to South Florida Sun Sentinel reporter David Furones, Jackson threw a punch at a Giants player during Thursday’s practice. Furones and Miami Dolphins on SI reporter Alain Poupart both highlighted that Jackson was immediately kicked out of practice. The frustrations and scuffles were not limited to just Jackson, with reports of multiple incidents flaring up – but they did not reach the point of anyone else throwing a punch. Jackson’s ejection from the workout loses the team’s top right tackle some potentially key repetitions as he and the offensive line prepare for the regular season. Hafley wants the Dolphins to be more physical this year, but clearly he wants them to be disciplined in their application of that physicality. He proved he was a man of his word and that he holds the team to standards on Thursday when Jackson stepped outside that discipline. Miami and New York will face each other on Saturday in the second week of the preseason schedule.

title: The Phinsider Mailbag: A 1,000 yard player, Willie Gay, and more
summary: Earlier this week, we reintroduced our mailbag here on The Phinsider. Over in The Feed, we asked for your questions and you responded – especially this week’s mailbag MVP, Phoenix6. I also wanted to try something new for this year’s mailbag. Rather than just gathering your questions and providing answers, I wanted to bring in […]
full_text: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 13: Willie Gay Jr. during the Miami Dolphins training session ahead their upcoming the National Football League (NFL) 2025 Madrid Game against Washington Commanders at Riyadh Air Metropolitano on November 13, 2025, in Madrid, Spain. (Photo By Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images) | Europa Press via Getty Images Earlier this week, we reintroduced our mailbag here on The Phinsider. Over in The Feed, we asked for your questions and you responded – especially this week’s mailbag MVP, Phoenix6. I also wanted to try something new for this year’s mailbag. Rather than just gathering your questions and providing answers, I wanted to bring in some of our staff to have more of a round-table conversation about each of your questions. Thanks to Marek Brave for joining me in breaking down your questions about any potential 1,000-yard players this year, linebacker Willie Gay’s roster battle, and reasons for concern coming out of the Dolphins’ Preseason Week 1 loss to the Washington Commanders. As we prepare for this weekend’s Preseason Week 2 game against the New York Giants, it is time to empty the mailbag and bring you our roundtable answers: Dolphins 1,000-yard player in 2026 KN: The obvious answer is running back De’Von Achane, who should lead the team in touches and could be looking toward 1,500 yards rushing alone. For receivers, I would not be surprised if Caleb Douglas or Chris Bell push toward 1,000 yards, but Malik Washington finishes with more receptions than either of them. MB: Achane will be the focal point for the Dolphins’ offense week in and week out. Jeff Hafley recently joked that he planned on giving him 40 touches a game. We’ll see if that actually was a joke, or instead, a premonition. Health permitting, Achane should surpass 1,000 rushing with multiple games still left on the schedule. Willie Gay in jeopardy of making 2026 roster KN: I think Gay will be an interesting watch for the rest of the preseason. He flies around the field and looks like someone who should be making an impact, but he is buried on the depth chart for a reason and he was not a key member of the team last year. He could factor into the rotation at linebacker and be a factor on special teams coverage, but I think the Dolphins coaching staff would rather have a younger, developing player on the roster in that role than Gay. If he balls out in the final two preseason games, maybe he forces the team to find a way to keep him, but I think he is probably a roster cut at this point. MB: Despite being a player who has made impact plays at times in his career, Gay hasn’t been able to put it all together during his six seasons in the league. As such, he’s never had more than 2.5 sacks in any given year. He has taken offense to being called out for “freelancing” a bit too much on the field, but when you watch the tape, you see a player who is oftentimes out of place. I wouldn’t be surprised at all if he were let go on cut-down day. KN: I think, despite being a recognizable name on the Dolphins’ reset roster this year, Gay has to make a strong impact on special teams if he wants to ensure he is back with the team. I agree, I would not be surprised if he is among the team’s roster cuts on August 30. “Welcome to the NFL” moment MB: I’ll go a little off the radar here and predict Dolphins’ rookie linebacker Trey Moore will have a hit on an opposing quarterback this season that would have made the old ESPN segment “Jacked Up!” from back in the day. His versatility will allow him to catch an offense off-guard, leading to a massive moment for the youngster. KN: “Jacked Up” – the days of talking about player safety but all the highlights were the hits causing injuries. What a different time. I think guard Kadyn Proctor will have that “welcome to the NFL” at some point when a defensive tackle blows him up on a rush, something I hope happens in the preseason rather than in the games that count. As for the “Jacked Up” hit on an offensive player, it will probably be Caleb Douglas or Chris Bell, just based on the positions they play. Someone will light them up at some point as they cross the middle of the field. Giving the hit? Linebacker Jacob Rodriguez will probably crush someone at some point, just based on the way he plays and flies around the field. Kyle Louis, either as a linebacker or a safety, could make that happen as well. Preseason Week 1 leaves concerns KN: Depth is the easy answer here. The Dolphins are a young team trying to quickly rebuild, and it is hard to do that and say you have enough depth. The rebuild should focus on finding starters who fit the new system; then you can add depth. Miami is in the former stage, not the latter. Next year, they will be able to round out the depth better. MB: I am concerned about the Dolphins’ secondary. They invested a late first round pick in Chris Johnson, and I think he will turn out to be a good pro, but the transition from college to the NFL for rookie cornerbacks has traditionally been a bumpy one. JuJu Brents is a player I’ve been high on since his time with the Iowa Hawkeyes before transferring to Kansas State, however, he has an extensive injury history and Miami has very little depth at corner. Let’s all form a circle, light some candles, join hands and pray that the injury bug misses South Florida this season. KN: The good thing is, Storm Duck should be an in-season reinforcement for the secondary. Of course, they have to get there first. For a specific position, I am concerned about punting. Bradley Pinion did not inspire confidence with his kicks on Friday. He averaged 44.8 yards and had a 53-yard kick, but it never looked fluid, and there were a couple of kicks that were short or nearly blocked. Maybe it was a one-off in the first preseason game, but special teams matter, and if the Dolphins cannot trust their punter, it is a concern. Starting safety KN: Based on the depth chart, Zayne Anderson has the early lead for that spot – and given the ties to the Green Bay Packers and head coach Jeff Hafley, that could make sense. Anderson has been more of a special teams player during his career, however, so either the Dolphins coaching staff are expecting a big step forward for him as he moves into his sixth season, or they are still working out who will actually take that top spot. I would watch Louis Moore, the undrafted rookie, over the next couple of weeks. If the Dolphins want to find out exactly what they have in their younger players this season, throwing Moore into the rotation, if not starting, could be an option. Major Burns was impressive on Friday, playing with speed and seeming to be everywhere; the 2026 UFL interceptions leader could factor into the decision by the end of the summer. And you cannot discount Kyle Louis, the team’s fourth-round pick who has been practicing as a linebacker thus far, starting to pick up safety reps at practice. If Miami wants to get him on the field despite a crowded linebacker corps, moving him to safety is an option MB: Keep an eye on rookie Michael Taaffe. The Texas product has impressed his coaches thus far, and as we know, the 2026 season will be about developing the team’s young core and getting them ready to make an impact when the Dolphins are expected to be a more legitimate contender in 2027 or 2028. Taaffe is a smart, instinctual guy, which is a very important quality for a safety to embody as the last line of defense for his team. KN: I will admit, I have a blind spot when it comes to Taaffe, but I will make sure to watch for him this weekend.

De’Von Achane is one of the best running backs in football despite still being just 24 years old. He rushed for 1,350 yards in 2025, with 4.1 of his 5.7 yards per carry coming after contact. Three seasons into his career, he has yet to earn a PFF grade below 80.0. Meanwhile, left tackle Patrick Paul took a significant step forward in his second season, improving his PFF grade from 44.9 as a rookie to 66.2 last season. They also had a really strong draft, as seven of the players they drafted earned PFF grades above 75.0 in their final seasons in college. It wouldn’t be a huge shock to see six or more of this class wind up as starters by the time the 2027 NFL season begins. title: Vikings-Ravens Joint Practice: Day Two Report
summary: The Minnesota Vikings and Baltimore Ravens completed the second day of joint practices today, ahead of their preseason game on Saturday. The weather was cloudy with some raindrops at times and cooler than yesterday. There were once again some former Vikings in attendance- Randy Moss again and Matt Birk- who played for the Ravens as […]
full_text: The Minnesota Vikings and Baltimore Ravens completed the second day of joint practices today, ahead of their preseason game on Saturday. The weather was cloudy with some raindrops at times and cooler than yesterday. There were once again some former Vikings in attendance- Randy Moss again and Matt Birk- who played for the Ravens as well- among them. Once again, the day started with a Kevin O’Connell press conference: LIVE: Head Coach Kevin O'Connell talks to the media https://t.co/atWbPFu4CO — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) August 20, 2026 Vikings Win the Day Taking an overall view to start off the report, the Vikings defensive units continued to not allow much at all from the Ravens offense. There were no deep completions for the Ravens in two days of practices and most of the day for the Ravens offensive units was a mix of defensive stops and short gains. The Vikings defense once again won the final two minute drill- both the first and second units- and the Vikings’ dominance seemed to grow to where the Ravens offense couldn’t get to mid-field starting from their own 25-yard line in the final two-minute drills. For the Vikings’ offensive units, there were still struggles and miscues, but overall less than yesterday, especially the first-team, which had a bit more success moving the ball early in full team drills and once again won the two-minute drill with about a 50-yard drive with 1:15 remaining to kick the winning field goal. Murray had a few completions on the drive, including a deep sideline shot to Jauan Jennings over his shoulder that put the Vikings in field goal position. The offense was helped by a 15-yard penalty on the Ravens- not sure what the call was, however. In any case, the drive culminated with a 45-yard field goal from Will Reichard (held by Brett Thorson) to win the drill. But overall for the offense, it was still a work in progress. The Ravens have a good defense- especially the secondary – which made moving the ball difficult. But both the first and second team units had a bit more success moving the ball today. Murray continued to target Justin Jefferson the most but had other completions to Hockenson and the key completion of the day to Jauan Jennings. There were fewer pass breakups than yesterday, but there were still some of those. The feeling I came away with was that practice makes progress and the Vikings offense continues to improve gradually. Kyler Murray threads it to TJ Hockenson. (Via Vikings IG) pic.twitter.com/4T0vOhuZte — VikingzFanPage (@vikingzfanpage) August 20, 2026 Up and over to Jauan‼️ pic.twitter.com/ScNchQCSex — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) August 21, 2026 Right there for Jauan Jennings 🙌 pic.twitter.com/IPp2TTSlZT — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) August 21, 2026 J.J. McCarthy was a little better today- a bit crisper- but he did give up a pick six – or would have been a pick six but he might have been sacked first. But he was also successful in moving the offense during the final two-minute drill with a few completions that got the Vikings within field goal range. But then on the final play of the drive Demond Claiborne broke one outside for a 30-ish yard touchdown run that had everyone cheering and teammates celebrating in the end zone. Demond Claiborne is pure SPEED. (Via Vikings IG) pic.twitter.com/uyKbnbewtM — VikingzFanPage (@vikingzfanpage) August 20, 2026 Defensively, it seemed like contributions were coming not just from Dallas Turner and Blake Cashman and Jalen Redmond- and Turner again had an excellent day- but also from Caleb Banks, Eric Wilson, Levi Drake-Rodriquez, Elijah Williams, Jake Golday, and Domonique Orange. Banks had a TFL on Derrick Henry that stood out, Wilson had a sack- so did Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins but that might have been a cleanup sack due to a Dallas Turner pressure. LDR, Williams, and Orange had run stuffs and Golday a big TFL. It was good to see some incremental improvement from the new guys on the defensive interior. Overall, the Vikings’ defensive units looked even better than they were yesterday and they limited the Ravens offensive units to mostly short gains on runs and passes, but mixed in sacks and stuffs, TFLs and PBUs as well. Lamar Jackson was also pressured enough where he was off on some of his throws which made it that much more difficult for the Ravens first team offense to move the ball in full team drills. I’m a Bateman truther but he has to have this man 💔💔💔 pic.twitter.com/s0TphZkSTk — Corey:) (@BRISIELBOYZ) August 20, 2026 Individual Player Mentions Looking back now on both days of the joint practices, here are some notes on individual player performances: Dallas Turner continues to show every sign of having a breakout season. He gave Pro Bowl tackle Ronnie Staley more than he could handle on many occasions. He had three sacks in full team drills by most counts today. The signs of Turner’s improvement go back to the last half of last season, but his performance in joint practices is just another stronger indication this could be a special season for the first-round draft pick in 2024. Offensively, Myles Price was the standout. He was the most targeted receiver and he caught just about everything thrown his way, whether in position drills, redzone, or full team drills. He looks sharp and confident. I don’t know that it will translate to a lot of offensive snaps this season, but he has certainly solidified his roster spot as possibly WR4. #Vikings WR Myles Price’s eyes lit up when asked about his experience with Randy Moss in the WR room yesterday: “Oh my gosh. He was sitting right next to me… he’s sitting casually, I’m eating my food, and he tapped me like, ‘Right here, you could’ve gave him this instead of… pic.twitter.com/NKDCkOHLEb — VikingzFanPage (@vikingzfanpage) August 20, 2026 On the other side, Charles Demmings- the star of training camp up to joint practices- has struggled more the last couple days. He gave up a deep ball yesterday and has gotten beaten at least a few times in redzone drills or flagged for DPI or holding. Hopefully this will be a lesson that allows for future growth of the promising cornerback. Jacob Thomas continued his assent up the safety depth chart during joint practices, where he drilled with the first team and had some first team reps- although most came with the second team. At this point he looks to be fourth on the safety depth chart behind Josh Metellus, Jay Ward and Theo Jackson, by-passing third-round pick Jakobe Thomas who hasn’t played much or impressed due to some back tightness. It’s been a pretty quiet training camp for Jordan Addison, and that continued through both joint practices. He really hasn’t been targeted much in full team drills and I’m not sure if he’s had any really noteworthy catches. He did have a couple targets by Kyler Murray in joint practices, including a bomb today, but neither were completed. He did have a nice grab in redzone position drills. It appears that Murray is more focused on developing a rapport with Jefferson at the moment, but hopefully he will be able to focus on Addison later before the season starts. Jordan Addison vs. Chidobe Awuzie pic.twitter.com/ENa50gNVkc — Ahmad Hicks (@AhmadHicksTV) August 20, 2026 While there is incremental improvement for Domonique Orange and Caleb Banks, I wouldn’t overstate it. There is still improvement needed before they will be able to handle more significant reps and not be liabilities. But there is progress and hopefully that will continue for the rest of training camp and into the season. Jake Golday is also showing improvement and had a nice run stuff today in addition to a good performance last Saturday. Tai Felton is still showing improvement over a year ago, which might be lost in the shuffle a bit. Jay Ward has also played well overall. I’m not sure if he’ll be a starter, but a good chance that he will. He has a slighter build than some other safeties, but he’s not afraid to lay the wood, as Jaxson Dart can attest. Brett Thorson continues…

title: Aggressive Patriots defense stacking interceptions in Eagles joint practices
summary: On Thursday, the commencement of the New England Patriots’ joint practice marked the end of a two-day session with the Philadelphia Eagles, where New England’s defense secured seven interceptions across both workouts. With only one turnover through the first six practices of training camp, veteran safety Kevin Byard challenged the safeties to secure more takeaways, […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 20: Marcus Jones #25 of the New England Patriots runs during a joint practice with the Philadelphia Eagles at Gillette Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Billie Weiss/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Thursday, the commencement of the New England Patriots’ joint practice marked the end of a two-day session with the Philadelphia Eagles, where New England’s defense secured seven interceptions across both workouts. With only one turnover through the first six practices of training camp, veteran safety Kevin Byard challenged the safeties to secure more takeaways, Dell Pettus shared earlier this summer. Just hours later, Pettus came away with the defense’s second interception of the summer. But now, the cornerbacks are getting involved. Nickel cornerback Marcus Jones secured three turnovers throughout the joint sessions, with two on Thursday. “I feel like we’re always trying to get turnovers,” Jones said after Thursday’s practice. “I’m a hard critic of the [defensive back] room, so I feel like there’s always room for improvement, for sure.“ During the 11-on-11 period, Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts targeted wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks toward the sideline, but Jones leapt in front to jump the route, getting his feet down before falling out of bounds. “I was in front of [Wicks]. [He’s a] great route-runner and everything like that. I kind of felt the pressure of him trying to get back to the sideline and everything, and I made sure to drive toward him a little bit,” Jones said. “And then next, I was like, ‘When the ball is in the air, you have to make a play.’” The Houston product’s first pick of the day also came against Hurts, plucking a pass out of the air that hit the hands of the opposing running back. He also jumped another Hurts sideline throw on Wednesday in seven-on-seven drills, returning the turnover for a hypothetical pick-six. A common session in both practices was a series of two- and one-minute drills under pressure. Cornerback Kindle Vildor prematurely ended a Tanner McKee two-minute drive on Wednesday, intercepting a sideline pass intended for a comeback route. “I feel like every time we get on the field, we’re trying to be aggressive,” Jones added. “[The] only way you can make turnovers is by being aggressive and violent, which we always talk about. And then always make the plays that you need to make.” Competition has been a common theme for improvement this offseason with this Patriots roster, a culture instilled by head coach Mike Vrabel. Jones described the team as competitive, and because they know the Eagles carry themselves the same way, their “big thing” is bringing energy to the turf. Additionally, that same on-field intensity is channeled toward the group’s goal for 2026 to become the No.1 scoring defense in the NFL. “Oh, man, [confidence] is at an all-time high,” Jones continued. “We know when it comes down to it, we want to be the number one scoring defense. And when it comes down to that, you know, it’s everyone on the back end making plays. So us as [defensive backs], we understand that. And whenever we do make turnovers, man, as you can tell, we’re trying to score with the ball. We don’t get too many opportunities like that, so we have to take advantage of it.” Following the seven-interception performance, Jones believes it heavily impacts the unit’s confidence approaching 2026. He explained that as a defensive back, you need to have the confidence to know when to break on the ball and how to go get it. They’ll have another chance on Saturday to continue generating turnovers in New England’s preseason game against Philadelphia at Gillette Stadium at 7 p.m. ET.

title: Contract details for Patriots free agency signing Greg Van Roten
summary: After losing both Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich to injury in their preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts, the New England Patriots explored the free agency market to further bolster their depth along the interior offensive line. They ended up signing three players in the days after the game. But while Darrian Dalcourt and Joseph […]
full_text: Greg Van Roten, a guard with the NY Giants, speaks to the press after a practice at Quest Diagnostics Training Center, East Rutherford, NJ, May 28, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co After losing both Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich to injury in their preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts, the New England Patriots explored the free agency market to further bolster their depth along the interior offensive line. They ended up signing three players in the days after the game. But while Darrian Dalcourt and Joseph Michalski were low-cost investments, the team decided to spend quite a bit of money to bring in Greg Van Roten . What this shows is that the 36-year-old appears to be in the team’s plans for 2026. OL Greg Van Roten: Contract details Base value: $3,000,000 Maximum value: $4,500,000 Guarantees: $1,000,000 Base salary: $500,000 Signing bonus: $500,000 2026 (age 36): Base salary: $1,480,000 Signing bonus: $500,000 Roster bonus: $1,020,000 Incentives (LTBE): $1,500,000 Salary cap hit: $4,500,000 Van Roten had remained unsigned since his prior contract with the Giants expired in January. He nonetheless ended up receiving a deal from the Patriots that clearly is above the $1.3 million that would have been the veteran minimum for a player of his experience. Besides getting a partially-guaranteed $1.48 million salary, the team also added a $500,000 signing bonus as well as $2.52 million dependent on availability and performance. He has $1.02 million in roster bonuses on the line as well as up to $1.5 million in playing time incentives, both of which considered likely to be earned and therefore part of New England’s salary cap calculations. At $4.5 million, his cap number is only slightly below that of starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker ($4.78M), one of the players Van Roten will be backing up this year. And what the relatively high guarantees in particular show is that the Patriots very well might be counting on that. Even though Ben Brown is a strong candidate to resume his spot as the top interior backup once he returns from his injury, Van Roten looks like the frontrunner to fill that role until then. This also means he might just sneak his way onto the 53-man roster despite only joining the team in mid-August.

title: Patriots defense rises to Mike Vrabel challenge in second Eagles joint practice
summary: The New England Patriots were ready to turn the page on their first joint practice with the Philadelphia Eagles almost immediately, but Mike Vrabel nonetheless made sure to hammer the point home. And not just that. The second-year head coach actively challenged the team, and especially its defense, to come back stronger after what had […]
full_text: Foxborough, MA - August 15: New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel at practice on August 15, 2026. (Photo by Barry Chin/The Boston Globe via Getty Images) | Boston Globe via Getty Images The New England Patriots were ready to turn the page on their first joint practice with the Philadelphia Eagles almost immediately, but Mike Vrabel nonetheless made sure to hammer the point home. And not just that. The second-year head coach actively challenged the team, and especially its defense, to come back stronger after what had been an uneven outing on Wednesday. Whatever buttons he managed to push by doing so, it worked: New England’s defense had a solid outing on Thursday. For linebacker K.J. Britt, it all started with Vrabel’s messaging and how it energized that side of the ball. “We had energy today. It didn’t matter who we played against today on defense,” Britt explained. “We can win a lot of games with the energy we played [with] today. That started from Vrabel just challenging us earlier this morning, challenging us last night. Just the culture here, how everybody wants to play football. It’s a football team.” How exactly Vrabel challenged his team, Britt was not willing to share. “I’d rather keep it in-house,” he added. “But Vrabel, he does a good job just keeping us on our toes, making sure that we get the best out of us. And we’ve got a defense that wants to respond to it. We’re not going to take it. We just want to build off of it and have fun with it. At the end of the day, we just want to have fun with it.” Fun was indeed being had by the Patriots defense on Thursday. Besides adding two more interceptions to bring the tally to seven over two days of work, the unit also showed some improvement rushing the passer and particularly stopping the run; after the Eagles had found success on Wednesday especially when stressing the edge, New England was markedly more sound against Saquon Barkley and company. The Patriots will still be first to tell you that they have considerable room for improvement, but Thursday was still a step in the right direction. A step prompted by their head coach’s challenge. “Once you come out here, your competitive nature is going to take over. And once your competitive nature takes over, you just play your game,” Britt said. “We got our eyes in the right spots today, and made sure that we were able to fly around and play ball.”

title: Patriots reach injury settlement with offensive lineman Andrew Rupcich
summary: The 2026 campaign is back on for Andrew Rupcich. The New England Patriots reached an injury settlement with the interior offensive lineman on Thursday, according to the NFL transaction wire. He will go through waivers entering the weekend with the chance to be claimed elsewhere. A return to Foxborough at a later date also cannot […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - MAY 27: Andrew Rupcich #67 of the New England Patriots during New England Patriots OTA on May 27, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. Sportswire) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The 2026 campaign is back on for Andrew Rupcich. The New England Patriots reached an injury settlement with the interior offensive lineman on Thursday, according to the NFL transaction wire. He will go through waivers entering the weekend with the chance to be claimed elsewhere. A return to Foxborough at a later date also cannot be ruled out. ESPN’s Mike Reiss reported last weekend that the 6-foot-6, 325-pound Rupcich had been diagnosed with a strained MCL after exiting in the fourth quarter of the preseason opener against the Indianapolis Colts. He saw 58 offensive snaps as team’s starting left guard and stayed on the sideline for the closing minutes of the 13-13 tie. Despite avoiding surgery, a move to injured reserve followed along with the additions of Darrian Dalcourt, Joe Michalski and veteran Greg Van Roten to the offensive line. Rupcich, 27, was in contention for a 53-man roster spot this August after joining New England’s practice squad last September and signing a futures contract in February. The product of NAIA’s Culver-Stockton entered the NFL with head coach Mike Vrabel’s former Tennessee Titans as an undrafted free agent in 2022. He appeared in 12 games while in the AFC South, including a pair of starts, before heading to the AFC East in 2025. It marks the second settlement in a week’s time for New England. Four players remain on the organization’s injured reserve. The season-ending group includes running back Myles Montgomery, wide receivers Jimmy Kibble and Jeremiah Webb, as well as tight end Julian Hill. The preseason continues Saturday versus the Philadelphia Eagles on the heels of joint practices. Kickoff at Gillette Stadium is set for 7 p.m. ET.

title: 5 performances of note from the second Patriots-Eagles joint practice
summary: The public portion of the New England Patriots’ 2026 training camp is over, and it ended with one of the most eventful days of the summer. Squaring off against the Philadelphia Eagles for a second straight day of joint practices, the two-hour session saw a heavy focus on the red area and therefore plenty of […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 19: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles reacts with Milton Williams #97 of the New England Patriots during a joint practice at Gillette Stadium on August 19, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Billie Weiss/Getty Images) | Getty Images The public portion of the New England Patriots’ 2026 training camp is over, and it ended with one of the most eventful days of the summer. Squaring off against the Philadelphia Eagles for a second straight day of joint practices, the two-hour session saw a heavy focus on the red area and therefore plenty of touchdowns. To recap Thursday’s practice, please check out our Patriots training camp notebook . In the meantime, here is who caught our eye for better or worse. Standout of the day CB Marcus Jones: On a day that saw the two defenses make up some ground on their offensive counterparts, one player stood out above the rest. After already catching one interception on Wednesday, Jones added two more against Eagles starting quarterback Jalen Hurts during Thursday’s session. His first pick came after a Milton Williams pressure that would have been a sack in a real game setting, and saw him capitalize on a tipped catch; Jones would have returned the pick for a touchdown had the play not been blown dead. The second INT, meanwhile, saw him undercut a throw down the sideline intended for Dontayvion Wicks. The team captain toe-tapped his way to getting both feet down in bounds. A look at Jalen Hurts’ 2 interceptions from Thursday’s joint practice 😮‍💨 (🎥 @Patriots ) pic.twitter.com/RGnmk6fCGv — Carlos A. Lopez (@LosTalksPats) August 21, 2026 Other performances of note WR A.J. Brown: Even though he was the target on both of Drake Maye’s interceptions on the day, Brown had another good day against his former team. Going mostly against first-team All-Pro Quinyon Mitchell, the ex-Eagle impressed. He started the day by beating Mitchell on a one-handed, toe-tap catch in the corner of the end zone in 1-on-1s and later caught three touchdowns against him in 2-on-2s. He later also drew a pass interference flag against his former teammate and hauled in two more receptions during full team work. DT Milton Williams and DT Cory Durden: Speaking of former Eagles, Milton Williams continues to be the Patriots’ best defensive lineman and most consistent performer up front against both the pass and the run. He had a would-be sack before Marcus Jones’ interception and assisted on a tackle for loss against Saquon Barkley. Cory Durden, meanwhile, also was quite disruptive on Thursday and helped shore up the run defense. He also had a would-be sack and drew a hold on a two-point attempt during team periods. ED Elijah Ponder: The Patriots’ edge had a better overall day than it did on Wednesday, and Elijah Ponder was a big reason why. The second-year man provided some good pressure despite working against one of the best tackle pairing in football. He had a would-be sack in 11-on-11s and even recorded a pass breakup near the goal line while covering a wheel route. Other players worth highlighting include wide receivers Kayshon Boutte and Kyle Williams, who both had some good moments and caught impressive touchdowns from Tommy DeVito, as well as a competitive Kindle Vildor, who saw reps as a starting cornerback opposite Carlton Davis at one point. Young offensive tackles Will Campbell and Caleb Lomu, meanwhile, had their ups and downs: the former continued to be challenged by Eagles edge Jalyx Hunt’s pass rush, while the latter surrendered a would-be sack in 11-on-11s and struggled in 1-on-1s. With the two joint sessions now in the books, the attention will turn to Saturday’s preseason game. Kickoff at Gillette Stadium is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET.
