title: 4 position battles the 49ers are looking to resolve against the Chargers
summary: The San Francisco 49ers have several players vying for roster spots. Some players are fighting uphill battles, others are looking to carve out roles, while a few are trying to prove to the coaching staff that they’re worth keeping around. The 49ers are still looking to find which receiver/returner, left guard, linebacker, and defensive tackle […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - JANUARY 05: Jacob Cowing #19 of the San Francisco 49ers during the NFL game at State Farm Stadium on January 05, 2025 in Glendale, Arizona. The Cardinals defeated the 49ers 47-24. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers have several players vying for roster spots. Some players are fighting uphill battles, others are looking to carve out roles, while a few are trying to prove to the coaching staff that they’re worth keeping around. The 49ers are still looking to find which receiver/returner, left guard, linebacker, and defensive tackle can solidify themselves on the depth chart. We’ll focus on those four positions and players in Thursday’s preseason game against the Los Angeles Chargers. Can Jacob Cowing overtake Jordan Watkins for the final spot? Jordan Watkins played a total of 63 snaps last week. That is somebody the team is trying to evaluate. Watkins spent most of his time out wide at receiver. He only played six snaps in the slot. Watkins caught six of his nine targets for 59 yards, including 23 yards after the catch. Two of those targets came behind the line of scrimmage, and another three were underneath nine yards. His best play didn’t count. It was a 20-yard reception where Watkins caught a pass that was behind him. Watkins has been up and down in August. Catching the ball with consistency has been a struggle, as has dealing with physicality. On De’Zhaun Stribling’s 32-yard reception, Watkins was still dancing his way into the route after Kurtis Rourke was blitzed. Those are the little things that will make quarterbacks look the other direction, which is why we saw Rourke look for Malik Turner more than Watkins when he was in. Most of Watkins’ targets came with Adrian Martinez under center. Watkins didn’t have a chance to return a kick. He fair-caught one punt return and returned the other one for four yards. Watkins will look to fend off Jacob Cowing, who looked great during OTAs, but has been sidelined for multiple weeks with a hip injury. I have a soft spot for Cowing. He’s one of the few players who plays as fast as his 40 time. He can legitimately run by any defensive back, and that’s something the 49ers took advantage of the second he returned to practice last Saturday and Sunday. It was also the case in the final OTA practice. Cowing will also get a crack at both return spots, alongside Watkins and undrafted rookie Will Pauling. If the former two can make a splash play on special teams, it’ll be difficult to keep either off the roster. But the 49ers are going to need Cowing’s dynamic ability at Z receiver with Ricky Pearsall sidelined. Deebo Samuel can take some of that workload, but I can’t imagine teams would defend the 49ers the same way they would with Cowing’s speed on the field as they would with Samuel or Demarcus Robinson. These next two weeks are huge for Cowing. Will his body hold up? There are no wrong answers for the 5th defensive tackle spot What if I told you James Thompson Jr. had the 13th highest win percentage among all defensive tackles during the first week of the preseason? Thompson Jr. won 18.2% of his rushes. Sebastian Valdez was 31st with 13.3%. Bryson Eason was a dominant force against the run, leading the way with a 10% run stop percentage. Eason didn’t do much as a pass rusher, while Thompson Jr. and Valdez left some meat on the bone defending the run. They all have vastly different play styles, which is why this training camp battle is the most fun. Thompson Jr. plays like somebody who is 6’6”. His pad level and technique aren’t great, but he has the length and quickness to be disruptive. Valdez has all-upper-body strength, while Eason plays with a lower center of gravity and an exceptional IQ. Who can put it all together? Who will take a step backward? It’s not all about highlight plays, which is why I lean toward Eason continuing to piece together plays that make him the most reliable moving forward. Thompson Jr. is making it more and more difficult, though. Whenever you’re ready, left guard The clock is ticking. The 49ers are running out of time to find out if the starting left guard is on the roster. They’ll default to Robert Jones if they have to, but the signs are pointing to the team wanting Carver Willis to win that job. I’d expect Willis to play left guard for the first half with the starters tonight. From an evaluation perspective, it’s a great opportunity to see Willis go up against the type of quality veterans he’ll see weekly. He’ll go against 315-, 317-, and 340-pound defensive tackles. Willis shouldn’t be threatened in pass protection, but if he can hold his ground against the run, that might be enough for the coaching staff to name him the starter. Technically, it’s a three-man race. Connor Colby didn’t play a snap at left guard in the preseason. That could change tonight with Dominick Puni sidelined with a concussion. Expect Robert Jones to play right guard early on with Nick Zakelkj taking the role that Kion Smith had in the second half last week. That allows Colby to get reps at left guard in the second half — if it’s truly a competition. Who plays where and how often will tell us the left-guard hierarchy. I’m leaning toward the rookie. Keeping the kids over the vets at linebacker? There’s a free-for-all behind Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw. The 49ers seem like they’re enamored with rookie Jaden Dugger, who is in line to be the third linebacker — he essentially played that role with the starters in the joint practice on Tuesday. But there were enough clips from that setting that would lead you to believe Dugger still has a long way to go before he can be relied on, which is expected for a fifth-round pick. Garret Wallow is the veteran whom the team trusts to get everybody lined up and play on passing downs. He came in for Nick Martin in those situations during the first preseason game. If Martin plays with the same inconsistent trigger he did last week, I’m not sure how the Niners roster him. Tatum Bethune was better than Martin, although he wasn’t without mistakes, either. Larry Worth III remains the wild card. He played with the starters in the red zone on Tuesday, which tells you Raheem Morris is intrigued by his skill set. Would the Niners dare reset the roster by keeping players like Worth III over the likes of Luke Gifford/Garret Wallow? It’s a dangerous game to play when you side with youth and athleticism over experience. It’s difficult to tell which linebackers are a lock after the trio of Warner, Greenlaw, and Dugger, which makes preseason games all the more important.

title: 3 things to watch in 49ers-Chargers: Will someone step up at left guard?
summary: It’s game day for the San Francisco 49ers, following a spirited joint practice with Jim Harbaugh and the Los Angeles Chargers. Regardless of your feelings about how the joint practice went, the 49ers left without serious injuries and head into tonight’s preseason matchup set to play “some starters.” Which starters and for how long is […]
full_text: It’s game day for the San Francisco 49ers, following a spirited joint practice with Jim Harbaugh and the Los Angeles Chargers. Regardless of your feelings about how the joint practice went , the 49ers left without serious injuries and head into tonight’s preseason matchup set to play “ some starters .” Which starters and for how long is anyone’s guess, but we’re approaching the stretch run ahead of cutdown day. Here are three things to watch tonight: Will someone take control of the left guard spot? Robert Jones, Connor Colby, and Carver Willis have all mixed in at left guard during training camp, but according to reports, the 49ers are no closer to naming a starter. Even worse, nobody has separated themselves or been particularly impressive. Naming a starter will help build continuity on the offensive line, but it doesn’t solve the spot. Will the 49ers choose someone in the building or explore options outside via trade or wait for cutdown day to bring in a veteran? No matter how you slice it, left guard has to be a concern for the team and any fan. The safety position All the good vibes after the joint practice and preseason game against the Titans are gone for the safety positions. With a few clips from the joint practice against Justin Herbert and the Chargers, safety has made safety a concern. One has to wonder: will we see Ji’Ayir Brown and Marques Sigle a lot tonight, in an effort to clear up the position? While the starting cornerbacks have received good reviews, the two safety spots still need, and tonight could go a long way toward instilling confidence in the position. The WR battle We’ve seen enough. De’Zhaun Stribling is a mix of Terrell Owens and Randy Moss and is ticketed for a gold jacket. Mike Evans won’t go tonight after dealing with a small injury in the joint practice. That leaves Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, and Will Pauling fighting for two spots after Demarcus Robinson and Deebo Samuel. We haven’t seen Christian Kirk, but Kyle Shanahan did say how much he loves Kirk; if he can’t get on the field, what does it matter? The battle between Watkins, Cowing, and Pauling is interesting, as the winner of the spot will have to play special teams in some capacity. It feels like Cowing is in a make-or-break spot, with Watkins impressing in the preseason opener. Pauling has received good reviews, but could be slotted for a practice squad spot unless he shows out tonight.

title: The 49ers need more from their early-round picks on the defensive line this season
summary: Pro Football Focus wrote about each team’s biggest concern heading into the 2026 season. For the San Francisco 49ers, it’s the “misses” along the defensive line: The 49ers need much more from their first- and second-round picks on the defensive line this season. Last season, Mykel Williams played just 385 snaps before suffering a season-ending injury, earning a 54.7 […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - DECEMBER 28: Alfred Collins #95 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates a win against the Chicago Bears following the game at Levi's Stadium on December 28, 2025 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pro Football Focus wrote about each team’s biggest concern heading into the 2026 season. For the San Francisco 49ers, it’s the “misses” along the defensive line: The 49ers need much more from their first- and second-round picks on the defensive line this season. Last season, Mykel Williams played just 385 snaps before suffering a season-ending injury, earning a 54.7 PFF grade and generating only 19 pressures on 245 pass-rushing snaps. Alfred Collins stayed healthy and logged 550 snaps, but his 35.0 PFF grade was tied for the second-lowest among the 94 interior defenders who played at least 300 snaps. San Francisco still has plenty of talent on defense, but not enough to absorb misses on premium draft picks along the defensive line. Both Williams and Collins will be expected to take significant steps forward in 2026. This year is huge for Williams. The 49ers did everything they could within reason to set him up for success this offseason. They added a proven NFL defensive tackle in Osa Odighizuwa and a designated pass rusher in Romello Height. Those moves let Mykel stay on the edge on early downs before kicking inside on obvious passing downs. In turn, Williams should consistently have 1-on-1s. Fifteen rookies played at least 20% of their team snaps in 2025. Among them, Williams ranked 11th in winning percentage as a pass rusher at 8.8%. Twelve played at least 20% of their team’s running downs. Williams fared much better here, recording a 6.2 stop percentage with an average depth of tackle of -0.1 yards, which was the only negative number in the group. In fact — it’s a small sample size of 133 snaps— Williams had the lowest average depth of tackle among any player. As noted, Collins’ grade was alarmingly low as a rookie. Of the 18 rookie defensive tackles who played at least 20% of the snaps in 2025, Collins finished 14th in run stop rate with the 12th lowest average depth of tackle, at 2.5 yards. Another potential concern that showed up in the first preseason game was Collins’ missed tackle rate. He had the sixth-highest among rookie defensive tackles at 14.3%. It’s easier to have faith in Mykel, despite him coming off a serious knee injury. He’s 22, plus the traits are there, as are the surroundings. Collins, who turns 25 in October, hasn’t shown us any consistency to suggest he can take the next step as a player. After a couple of highlights in Week 5 against the Rams last year, Collins went nearly three months without another game where he flashed, and that was against the Titans. Williams gets a pass if he has a slow start to the season. Collins does not. The 49ers need Collins to play up to his draft status for the defense to reach its ceiling this year.

Starting quarterback Cam Ward has also routinely carved up the starters for most of training […]
full_text: Feb 7, 2024; Las Vegas, NV, USA; Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Joshua Williams (2) during a press conference before Super Bowl LVIII at Westin Lake Las Vegas Resort and Spa. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con Much is being made about the Tennessee Titans’ supposed ongoing struggles in the secondary . It was undeniably disappointing to watch San Francisco 49ers backup quarterback Kurtis Rourke complete 12-of-14 passes against the Titans’ starting secondary in the first preseason game . Starting quarterback Cam Ward has also routinely carved up the starters for most of training camp. Head coach Robert Saleh isn’t panicking, but recently admitted there should be a sense of urgency. Understandably so. The Titans committed more than $100 million in free agency to new starting cornerbacks Cor’Dale Flott and Alontae Taylor, and they’ve been at the forefront of the struggles. With the Titans doing some soul searching, you wonder if cornerback Joshua Williams could contribute something positive at cornerback. He was the third cornerback the Titans signed in free agency earlier this offseason. His shared history with Mike Borgonzi and the Kansas City Chiefs made him a target. Williams has been wearing a yellow non-contact jersey at training camp due to a pectoral muscle injury. Coach Saleh recently claimed he’s close to shedding that jersey and being a full participant at practice. Saleh also praised his length and work ethic, and Jim Wyatt noted he had a pass breakup during individual drills earlier this week. Saleh: CB Joshua Williams getting closer to where he's cleared for full contact (is currently wearing a yellow jersey because of pec injury) @Titans — Jim Wyatt (@jwyattsports) August 17, 2026 Williams is long and competitive. He possesses the physical profile Coach Saleh prefers in his cornerbacks. If Taylor and Flott struggle into the regular season, perhaps Williams will start getting worked into the rotation. For now, he’s simply focused on being healthy enough to contribute once his number is called. Williams was signed to essentially play the Darrell Baker Jr. role from last season. He’s the top reserve cornerback who can play starting reps if Taylor or Flott get injured. The Titans’ secondary is fluid as they search for answers. Perhaps Williams can provide one.

title: Washington Commanders 91-man 2026 preseason Game 2 roster/depth chart
summary: Reviewing the roster limit As you are probably aware, the NFL CBA allows each team to have 90 players on its offseason roster, but it also makes provisions for a 91st player who joins the team via the International Player Pathway (IPP) program. For the last several years, the Commanders have made use of this […]
full_text: Reviewing the roster limit As you are probably aware, the NFL CBA allows each team to have 90 players on its offseason roster, but it also makes provisions for a 91st player who joins the team via the International Player Pathway (IPP) program. For the last several years, the Commanders have made use of this IPP exemption, as they have again this season, so Washington’s offseason roster limit is once again 91 players. Washington’s 91st player via the IPP is currently edge rusher TJ Maguranyanga , who spent the 2025 season on the Commanders roster. Surprising number of roster changes since the Dolphins game In the four days that followed the Dolphins game, the Commanders announced eight roster moves. Released/waived (2) K Jake Moody Most people were surprised, not by the result, but by the timing of the end of Washington’s kicker competition. After the release of Jake Moody, undrafted rookie place kicker Drew Stevens was declared the winner of the roster spot that the two had been competing for since OTAs. Now, Stevens will have two preseason games to build his confidence and cement his spot as the permanent kicker on a team that has signed 20 guys to the role in the past 25 seasons. P Matt Haack Another non-surprise came when the team released punter Matt Haack , who had been signed to punt during camp while Tress Way recovered from a pectoral injury he sustained during a “flex off” with former Redskins player and now-Hollywood actor Terry Crews . Injured Reserve (2) When a player is placed on injured reserve during training camp, he is ineligible to return to play for the team that season, though he can be waived with an injury settlement and play for another team when healthy. RB Jerome Ford was put on IR with a hamstring injury. WR River Cracraft was put on IR with an unspecified injury. Outside of the regular season and playoffs, NFL teams are not required to provide details about player health or injuries, though details will likely be reported by local media eventually. Both players were long shots to earn a roster spot in their respective crowded position groups, and with the move to IR, neither will don the burgundy & gold again in the 2026 season. Signed (4) RB Craig Reynolds With Jerome Ford headed to IR and Jeremy McNichols out for “weeks” according to Dan Quinn, the team needed depth at the running back position. Craig Reynolds entered the NFL initially as an undrafted player with the Washington Redskins in 2019. More relevant to his recent signing, however, is the five years he spent with the Detroit Lions, where he was teammates in 2021 and 2023 with the Commanders current offensive coordinator David Blough. TE Tre’ McKitty Tre’ McKitty recently won the UFL championship with the Louisville Kings. His performance over the spring season—including two crucial catches in the UFL championship game—reignited NFL interest and earned him a successful workout with Washington. McKitty was a highly touted third-round pick by the Los Angeles Chargers in 2021, and Washington is providing a “now or never” opportunity to see if his raw athletic traits can finally be unlocked at the NFL level. DT Maurice Hurst II Defensive lineman Johnny Newton will miss several months after having surgery to repair a torn pectoral muscle . Maurice Hurst II was signed to step directly into defensive rotations and absorb reps during padded and non-padded practices and the remaining preseason schedule. Hurst brings 65 games of NFL experience across his stints with the Raiders, 49ers, and Browns. Over the last three seasons in Cleveland, he proved to be an efficient rotational piece when healthy, accounting for 39 tackles, two sacks, and an interception. LB Krys Barnes Linebacker Jordan Magee has been dealing with a shoulder injury following the Dolphins game. Ale Kaho also got banged up against Miami but seems to be okay. Either way, the Commanders needed a reliable, healthy body to step into the second-team defensive rotations immediately. Unlike many late-preseason additions who are unproven, Barnes brings 75 games of NFL experience and 33 career starts across his time with the Packers, Cardinals, and Panthers. Having a veteran who has recorded multiple 80-plus tackle seasons ensures a higher floor for the defense if injuries linger. Accounting for Laremy Tunsil & Johnny Newton While Friday’s chart lists 91 players, we know already that two of those players, LT Laremy Tunsil and DL Johnny Newton , will not be on the active roster in Week 1. Timing counts for a lot with players who suffer major injuries in training camp. Here’s a quick explanation of the considerations for placing player on IR under the relevant NFL rules: 1. The Pre-Cutdown Rule (Season-Ending) As mentioned above, if the Commanders place Tunsil or Newton on IR during training camp before the final 53-man roster reduction deadline on Aug. 30, the player is automatically ruled out for the entire season . He would not be allowed to practice or play for Washington at any point during the year. While Tunsil and Newton have already undergone surgery, head coach Dan Quinn said that doctors have not yet determined his recovery timeline for either player. If doctors determine, in the coming days, that Tunsil and/or Newton will not be able to return to play prior to mid-February, then the Commanders might choose to exercise this option. 2. The Cutdown Day Exception (Designated to Return) NFL rules allow teams: a. to designate, on cutdown day (Aug. 30), up to two injured players to return from IR during the season b. alternatively, the team can carry a player onto the initial 53-man roster and move him to IR the following day (Aug. 31st) opening up a roster spot; the only reason to do this would be if the team needed to designate two other players to return at the time the initial roster was set on Aug. 30. (Option A is almost certainly the one that the Commanders would choose in Tunsil’s case, probably Newton as well) This approach (either option a or b) allows the player (Tunsil/Newton/both) to keep his season alive since it leaves the door open for him to return after sitting out a minimum of four games (obviously, in these two cases, it would be closer to four months than four games). If doctors determine that the player’s (Tunsil’s/Newton’s/both) return to play could happen prior to mid-February, then the Commanders might choose this option to keep all possibilities on the table. The only cost to the team is the opportunity to carry one or two more players on the training camp roster between now and Aug. 30. Not your typical depth chart The chart below is only a depth chart insofar as it assigns players to positions and stacks them in an order. The primary purpose of the chart is to keep track of the 91 guys that currently comprise the training camp roster, not to predict game-day alignments. You will note, for example, that I have 12 offensive position stacks and 13 defensive position stacks on the chart despite the fact that a team can only field 11 players at one time. You will also note that each player’s name appears only once regardless of the fact that he may play in multiple alignments or positions ( e.g., an interior offensive lineman who can play center and both guard spots will appear at only one of those positions, not all of them ). Again, this is by design, since the goal is to provide handy visual reference of the 91 individual players while also offering an overall snapshot of team strength and depth. The bias, though, is to provide a visual list of the full roster, not so much to create a game-ready depth chart. Finally, you will also note that, where players are capable of playing more than one position (and likely to do so on game days), my decision on where to align them may be very different from your idea of where they belong. A few recent changes in my presentation of the preseason 91-man depth chart Position consolidation At s ome position groups where players frequently change…

title: Joshua Josephs among top Commanders storylines as training camp continues
summary: The Washington Commanders conducted more back-to-back sessions of training camp this week. Receiver River Cracraft and running back Jerome Ford went on the team’s injured reserve […]
full_text: The Washington Commanders conducted more back-to-back sessions of training camp this week. Several players were out with injuries sustained during the team’s first preseason game versus the Miami Dolphins or the joint practice before it, while others returned from extended absences. Receiver River Cracraft and running back Jerome Ford went on the team’s injured reserve list while quarterback Marcus Mariota, defensive lineman Johnny Newton and linebackers Jordan Magee and Ale Kaho all sat out with new injuries. Edge rushers Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson also missed time with injuries this week. The team welcomed back starters Nick Allegretti and John Bates on Tuesday — more on Allegretti’s status in a bit — and several additional bodies were also added to the roster to conduct offseason activities. All the Commanders moves from this morning pic.twitter.com/Uepgvbz3ge — Martenzie Johnson (@10zJohnson) August 18, 2026 In seeming deference to the team’s injury status, head coach Dan Quinn opted to go shells only on Tuesday instead of full pads, but the injury news for the Commanders only got worse on Wednesday. Newton has undergone surgery for a torn pectoral muscle and will miss a good portion, if not all, of the regular season. Allegretti headed to the medical tent and was shut down early Wednesday and sat out Thursday. Running back Rachaad White was also revealed to have a hamstring injury, but returned on a limited basis Thursday. Both will miss Saturday’s preseason game in Detroit. Daron Payne also sat out Thursday’s session with a minor injury. There is plenty to cover, so here are the top associated storylines from the week. Jayden Daniels gets extended reps in camp, but is it enough? Marcus Mariota is sidelined with a sprained MCL , but the team is optimistic the veteran backup quarterback will be available for the season opener. On Tuesday, the coaching staff decided to give starter Jayden Daniels additional practice reps, which allowed the quarterback an opportunity to gel with the second-team wide receivers. Daniels threw his first interception of camp, a tipped ball to Amik Robertson, but bounced back to finish the day strong. First, he hit Jaylin Lane for a big completion, then Daniels shredded the defense in a one-minute drill, once again drawing the “surgical” tag. One-minute drill and Jayden Daniels was SURGICAL!! Found Diggs for a big gain on the right sideline, then hit Chig for a 40-yard TD on a Seam route. Perfect drive. #Commanders — Josh Taylor (@JoshTaylorFB) August 18, 2026 CHIGGGGGGG pic.twitter.com/q43xgAcID3 — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) August 18, 2026 While this is good news, the big storyline revolves around if Daniels should play in Saturday’s preseason game. On Thursday, the decision still hadn’t been made with Quinn simply stating a “good amount of starters” will get playing time on Saturday. Regardless of perceived necessity, Quinn may choose to keep Daniels on the bench all preseason given the team’s recent rash of injuries. The camp reports of Daniels’ performance have been glowing up until this point, but there are more than a few people that think Daniels could benefit from live competition. You can count Doc Walker among those who believe the Commanders should get Jayden Daniels and the starters time in preseason games. Here's what the Super Bowl champion with the Redskins had to say: pic.twitter.com/Db9vOIfxTQ — The Team 980 (@team980) August 19, 2026 Joshua Josephs continues to have a strong training camp Both Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson sat out this week’s sessions and fellow edge rusher Joshua Josephs used the additional reps to continue to build on his strong training camp. Joshua Josephs is ALLLLLL over the field today good lord — Josh Taylor (@JoshTaylorFB) August 18, 2026 Here’s a quick look at OLB Joshua Josephs in OL-DL 1-on-1s pic.twitter.com/7abX0sApRa — Skylar Nelson (@SkyMad03) August 18, 2026 Here’s a quick look at OL-DL 1-on-1s from today’s practice pic.twitter.com/m7Hba71rxk — Skylar Nelson (@SkyMad03) August 19, 2026 Josephs has looked good both in the pass rush and run defense while working with the first team. He played some SAM linebacker this week, which shows the team has faith in his off-the-ball ability. Josh’s potential role this season continues to grow. A roster battle is being waged at the defensive tackle position DJ Davidson abruptly retired last week, and since the announcement there has been no clarity regarding the identity of Tim Settle’s backup(Settle is also dealing with a calf strain). The loss of Johnny Newton late Wednesday creates further opportunity in the defensive tackle room. Shy Tuttle made some plays in the first preseason game and last year’s undrafted free agent addition Ricky Barber also had a good game. Barber even played some zero technique and looked good while doing it. Quinn praised both players in his pre-practice presser Tuesday. title: Washington Commanders have good options to fill in for Laremy Tunsil
summary: Rising optimism for the Commanders’ season was dealt a setback when Laremy Tunsil suffered a torn triceps in training-camp one-on-ones against edge rusher Odafe Oweh. The injury required surgery and is expected to sideline the team’s franchise left tackle for a large portion of the season. The announcement that Brandon Coleman would take Tunsil’s place […]
full_text: Rising optimism for the Commanders’ season was dealt a setback when Laremy Tunsil suffered a torn triceps in training-camp one-on-ones against edge rusher Odafe Oweh. The injury required surgery and is expected to sideline the team’s franchise left tackle for a large portion of the season. The announcement that Brandon Coleman would take Tunsil’s place during the rehab was met with mixed reactions within the fanbase. Many welcomed the opportunity for a young player who has shown growth in his first two seasons to step up and show what he can do, while gaining valuable starting experience. Others pointed to Coleman’s struggles while starting at left tackle in his rookie season and suggested that the team will need to find another replacement in free agency or elsewhere on the roster. A few panicked, and declared the season lost before it even started. Fortunately, with more than four weeks to go before the season opener and more than $37 million in cap space , the Commanders have time and resources to make sure they have a viable solution in place to protect quarterback Jayden Daniels’ blind side until Tunsil is ready to rejoin the starting lineup. In this article, I’ll use advanced stats from Pro Football Focus to review the main options which have been proposed to fill in for Tunsil from within the Commanders’ roster, or via free agency. The Baseline – Laremy Tunsil Let’s start by taking a look at Tunsil’s advanced blocking metrics. This sets the baseline against which we can measure the various options which the Commanders might try as temporary replacements. The following graph shows Tunsil’s pressure rate allowed in pass protection and run blocking grades throughout his 10 year NFL career. Pressure rate is the percentage of pressure opportunities on which he allowed a pressure (sack, QB hit or QB hurry). Pressure opportunities are pass blocking snaps, minus spikes and plays negated by penalties. Pressure rate is a well validated advanced stat, which is predictive of career outcomes at offensive tackle. Run blocking grades are PFF’s metric based on analyst ratings of a player’s contribution to play outcomes on every snap in a season. PFF grades are used here for want of any better validated metric for run blocking. The green line highlights 6% pressure rate. This is something of a magic number for offensive tackles. Tackles who achieve pressure rates below 6% by the end of their rookie contracts tend to get signed to long-term starting-level contracts. Those who don’t get below 7% tend to become backups, switch position or wash out of the league. Players in between have more variable outcomes, with some getting extended long-term and others getting short term contracts or going other directions. In 2025, 6% pressure rate fell between 9 th and 10 th place among primary starting left tackle (each team’s player with the most snaps at the position). That is a little high, because my sample includes a few backups filling in for starters. In most seasons, 6% is a little better than average among starters, if more care is taken to identify teams’ actual intended primary starters. (Regular readers might note I have previously set the threshold at 5%, using raw pass blocking snaps as the denominator. Switching to pressure opportunities provides greater accuracy, and inflates the figures by around 1%.) Tunsil is one of the rare offensive tackles who entered the league playing at a pro starter level in pass protection, and has improved over time. From 2020, he has been playing at an elite level, with the exception 2021, when he played through a torn ulnar collateral ligament in his thumb. That season, his pressure rate rose to normal starter level, while his run blocking grade took a dip in the opposite direction. This is a typical pattern – sudden spikes in blocking metrics are frequently associated with injuries. In 2025, Tunsil’s 3.4% pressure rate ranked third among primary starting left tackles. Only Denver’s Garrett Bolles (3.0%) and the Giants’ Andrew Thomas (3.1%) were better, and not by much. Tunsil is sometimes described as being just OK as a run blocker. His blocking grades have improved throughout the course of his career. In 2025, his 75.3 run block grade was 22nd highest among 94 OTs, which is not elite (Max: 96.6 – Penei Sewell; 2 nd place 92.0 – Trent Williams), but not too shabby either. He ranked 10th among tackles who played predominantly or exclusively on the left side. Right tackles were over-represented at the top of the run blocking rankings. To summarize, the player the Commanders are seeking to replace is an elite pass protector and a better than average run blocker at left tackle. That skillset is generally not available among street free agents in August, and would be an extremely lucky find on a team’s depth chart. Realistically, general manager Adam Peters’ challenge is to come as close as possible to prevent a significant drop off at protection on Jayden Daniels’ blindside. Quality run blocking to suit coordinator David Blough’s offense would be a bonus. Best Available Free Agent – Taylor Decker By happy coincidence, 2026 just happened to be one of the unusual instances when a starting-level left tackle was allowed to walk and not re-signed elsewhere. Earlier in the offseason, the Detroit Lions failed to reach agreement on a contract restructure with 10-year veteran left tackle, Taylor Decker , who was then granted a release. The Lions moved on, switching Penei Sewell to left tackle and drafting Clemson’s Blake Miller in the first round to play right tackle. Decker was drafted three picks after Tunsil in 2016 and has been well regarded as a starter for Detroit. However, he underwent multiple surgeries on his feet and ankles in 2024, followed by shoulder surgery in the 2025 offseason. It was reported that the request for release was prompted by the Lions’ asking him to take a pay cut . Could the Lions’ loss be the Commanders’ gain? Let’s have a look a look at Decker’s stats to get an idea of what he might have left in the tank. Decker’s early career progression in pass protection is more typical of offensive tackles than Tunsil’s. In his first two seasons, he allowed higher than desirable pressure and then progressively improved to starting level performance in the final three seasons of his rookie contract. However, his peak performance in 2020 fell well short of the numbers Tunsil has posted over the past six seasons. Furthermore, as the wear and tear has accumulated over the past three seasons, the pressure rates have creeped up above 6%. Nevertheless, in 2025, Decker’s pressure rate ranked 12th among primary starting left tackles. Unless he has a significant drop off this season, he should still be an average to above average starter. Decker’s average run blocking grades over the course of his career have been a little better than Tunsil’s, but it’s not a stark difference. Tunsil has been trending up over the past three seasons, while Decker’s curve is heading in the opposite direction. The numbers suggest that the wear and tear has been taking a toll on Decker’s performance. At age 33, he could well be entering the declining phase of his career. In that context, the Lions’ decision to move on makes sense. The Commanders don’t necessarily need someone to come in and play at Tunsil’s level. If he can maintain his level of play from 2025, Decker could provide a level of insurance as a solid veteran presence to back up and compete with the younger developing players on the roster. Decker’s availability has led many to wonder why the Commanders have not raced to sign him. To get a better handle on what they might be thinking, let’s have a look at the numbers of Tunsil’s chosen replacement. The Next Man Up – Brandon Coleman The Commanders’ response to Tunsil’s prognosis was quick and decisive, leaving many in the fanbase scratching their heads. Head coach Dan Quinn announced that Brandon Coleman would move back to left tackle —…

full_text: The Washington Commanders training camp rolls on for Day 14 in Ashburn, VA. Head coach Dan Quinn spoke to reporters before the start of today’s practice and provided updates on the growing list of injured players. CB Trey Amos suffered an ankle sprain when he returned to practice from last year’s broken fibula. The new ankle injury is on the same leg he had been rehabbing. Projected starting center Nick Allegretti was also quickly sidelined after returning to practice. He suffered a calf strain on the first day of camp, and felt some soreness during his return to the field. He won’t play against the Lions, leaving Julian Good-Jones and rookie Matt Gulbin to snap for whoever lines up under center on Saturday. It was reported last night that DT Jer’Zhan “Johnny” Newton had surgery in New York for a torn pectoral and Quinn confirmed that he will miss time. Some positive injury news was that RB Rachaad White’s hamstring injury isn’t serious, but he’s also not playing in Detroit this weekend. full_text: The Daily Slop – 20 August 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Sports Illustrated Albert Breer Empties His Commanders Notebook From Training Camp Dan Quinn is very much trying to instill a hard edge into his team after he felt like it lost a little bit of that in a come-back-to-earth 2025 season. So what does that mean? Longer practices, more time in pads, and conditioning and hardening a team under the sauna of the DMV summer. It has also meant more game-like conditions for everyone to sharpen their skills. More than anyone else, that’s applied to Quinn’s two new coordinators—David Blough on offense and Daronte Jones on defense. The Commanders are conducting mostly 11-on-11 periods, and most of that work’s been done in “call it” periods, where the coaches don’t have a script, are calling plays against each other and reacting to the circumstances in the moment. That’s great training, of course, for Blough and Jones as they build toward the season. This won’t be the Kliff Kingsbury offense he worked under the past two years. There are sprinkles of that, and the Sean McVay–influenced offense he played in under Kevin O’Connell. But there are more of Ben Johnson’s concepts than anyone else’s in what the Commanders are doing, if you had to drill down on the specifics. And that means a pretty significant change for Jayden Daniels. And, quietly, I get the sense that the staff can’t wait for the football world to see what Daniels is going to be in 2026—especially since a lot of that world seems to have forgotten 2024. The offensive line has questions, particularly after the loss of star left tackle Laremy Tunsil to a torn triceps. There’s a shot that he’ll make it back for the playoffs, but the Commanders won’t know for another 6–8 weeks , so they’re moving forward on the assumption that they’ll be without him this year. Javon Kinlaw’s shown an ability to line up all over the place, and hyper-athletic edge rushers Odafe Oweh and K’Lavon Chaisson, imported from the Chargers and Patriots, respectively, look like potential Swiss Army knives for Jones as he builds the scheme. And you can put No. 7 pick Sonny Styles in that category, too, as a guy who’s lived up to his reputation in just about every way and looks physically freakish, even among NFL players. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Bullock’s Film Room (subscription) Commanders Film Review: Matt Gulbin vs Dolphins Julian Good-Jones, the back up center, started in place of Allegretti which in turn elevated Gulbin to the second unit. Gulbin certainly didn’t look out of place with the second team offense. Granted, the Dolphins are a rebuilding team and lack depth across the roster, meaning he wasn’t facing the strongest opposition. So keep that in mind here as we work through the performance. But Gulbin can’t control who lines up across from him so it’s still worth seeing how he did. Let’s start with the run game. Undrafted free agent running back Robert Henry Jr. had an impressive outing against the Dolphins, but it was no coincidence that many of his explosive runs came on plays where Gulbin had some important blocks. Thought Commanders rookie center Matt Gulbin had a solid outing against the Dolphins in preseason. I broke down his performance: https://t.co/0Y27fjwnQU pic.twitter.com/uFRebtHhRf — Mark Bullock (@MarkBullockNFL) August 19, 2026 Sports Illustrated The Good and Not So Good From Commanders’ 13th Training Camp Practice Javon Kinlaw is one of the guys who could get more work if Johnny Newton is out for an extended amount of time. He looked like the wild man Washington needs more of this season, stopping Allen for a loss during team drills. Washington needs him to be the disrupter they paid for when they signed him. D.J. Davidson pulled off a play every guy looking to make the final 53 wishes they could by stripping Robert Henry Jr. and running it back for what would have been six points. Washington again struggled with pre-snap penalties, something that has plagued them all summer and has now stretched into preseason. Washington has now had enough practices with false starts/pre-snap mistakes that it can no longer be written off as one sloppy session. The offense can survive those mistakes on a training-camp field, but Quinn will want to see evidence in preseason game reps that the problem is being cleaned up. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Riggo’s Rag 7 supreme standouts from Washington Commanders 2026 training camp Day 13 Tyler Owens – Commanders DB Tyler Owens has always had elite-level athleticism. The Commanders have utilized him primarily on special teams over the first two years of his professional career, but there are growing signs that this could change under new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones. It’s been evident throughout training camp that Jones is trying to find ways to get Owens onto the field . He’s being used as a box safety, big nickel cornerback, and even across the linebacker positions within the new 3-4 front. This is bringing a positive response from the Texas Tech product, who looks ready to make a much bigger impact this season. Nick Cross – Commanders S There is an intriguing competition developing for the second starting safety position. But everyone already knows who the alpha on Washington’s defensive back end is. Nick Cross was an intriguing addition to the ranks this offseason. The Commanders believe he can be the tone-setting presence this team hasn’t had since Jeremy Chinn left town, and the impressive start made this summer only lends further weight to these claims. According to those in attendance, it was a good day for Cross. He blew up a couple of screen passes and always seemed to be around the action. The former Maryland standout has great vision and anticipation, which is key within the scheme new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones plans to run. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Last Man Standig (paywall) Commanders DT Johnny Newton undergoes pec surgery, expected to miss significant time Losing Newton is the latest depth subtraction since the start of camp. D.J. Davidson was expected to compete for a role before retiring. Daron Payne and Javon Kinlaw, the primary DT/3-4 ends, have been disruptive presences at the line of scrimmage in practice. Projected nose tackle Tim Settle missed the past week with a calf strain. Quinn suggested Settle could be close to returning to practice. Shy Tuttle has capably filled in at nose tackle. Second-year DT Ricky Barber, a roster candidate, and UDFA Jeffrey M’ba will receive additional work. Washington recently signed veteran free agents Byron Cowart and Maurice Hurst. K’Lavon Chaisson suffered a knee injury during the joint practice with the Miami Dolphins, and the team is being cautious with his recovery. Linebacker Jordan Magee suffered a shoulder injury and will be held out for the rest of the week. title: 2027 NFL quarterback predictions: 16 teams with questions
summary: We picked out teams with some level of QB1 questions for 2027 and projected two potential outcomes for each -- one likely and one not so likely.
full_text:
While everyone else is predicting who's going to start at quarterback for various teams next month, we're looking beyond this entire 2026 NFL season to figure out where the QB questions are going to be next year .

 Several of the NFL's teams are entering critical seasons with their quarterback situations. Some have no idea how they'll make it through this season with what they have on the roster. Some feel confident about this season but don't know how things will shake out for 2027. The smart teams are thinking ahead, even as they prepare for 2026. So every year, we try to pick a dozen or so teams whose long-term QB situations appear to be in flux and examine what's most likely to happen in the short and long terms.

 We try to stay away from situations in which contracts make change extremely unlikely. For example, you might say this is an important year for Dak Prescott to break through in the postseason for Dallas. And in some ways you might be right. But in terms of Prescott's long-term future with the team, that is not the case. He's signed through 2028, he has $45 million in fully guaranteed salary for 2027, and various restructures have created a dead-money situation that makes him virtually uncuttable or untradeable. He's not on this year's list.

 Lamar Jackson wasn't on last year's list , because at the time he had three years left on his contract with the Ravens, and there wasn't any doubt he'd be on the team in 2026. This year, however, he has two years left on his deal. And while the Ravens said they wanted to get him extended this offseason, they could not reach an agreement. That ratchets up the uncertainty on Jackson for 2027 and beyond, so we included him just to flag the circumstances and examine them a bit. If Jackson signs a new extension with the Ravens in the next few days, things change. But unless and until that extension gets done, we have license to wonder. That's just a fact.

 Last year we started with Arizona ... and we're starting there again.

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | CAR | CLE | DET 
 HOU | IND | LAR | MIA | MIN | NYJ 
 PHI | PIT | SEA | TB 

 
 

 

 Arizona Cardinals 
 Current starter:   Jacoby Brissett 
 Signed through:  2026

 The Cardinals have a new head coach in former Rams offensive coordinator Mike LaFleur. He inherits Brissett, who finished the 2025 season as Arizona's starter and played well under previous offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. But Brissett and the Cardinals spent the spring and summer in a contract standoff that resulted in a roughly $10 million raise over the roughly $5 million he had been scheduled to make this season under his previous deal.

 

 The team also signed seven-year NFL veteran  Gardner Minshew II  in free agency and drafted former Georgia/Miami quarterback Carson Beck with the first pick of the third round of this year's NFL draft. Of those three options, the only one under contract beyond 2026 is Beck, who played well in the Cardinals' first preseason game before sitting out the second because of a rib injury . The Cardinals have won four or fewer games in three of their past four seasons and are projected for the second-lowest win total (5) in ESPN's Football Power Index projections for 2026.

 Most likely outcome:  They start the season with Brissett and struggle. They switch to Beck at some point during the season to give him an audition and find out whether he can be part of the long-term solution. They secure a very high pick in the 2027 draft and use it on one of the highly touted quarterbacks in that class -- someone they believe can be a franchise cornerstone.

 Long-shot outcome:  Some combination of Brissett and Beck keeps the Cardinals competitive, even in a division where the other three teams each won at least 12 games last season (and one won the Super Bowl). They don't end up with a high draft pick, and they see enough from Beck to open 2027 with him as the starter.

 

 
 

 Atlanta Falcons 
 Current starter: Tua Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr . 
 Signed through: Tagovailoa, 2026; Penix, 2027 plus a team option for 2028

 The Falcons are ostensibly having a competition this summer for their starting job between Penix, who was the eighth pick in the 2024 draft, and Tagovailoa, who was released by the Dolphins this offseason. The Falcons were able to sign Tagovailoa for a veterans minimum salary because the Dolphins are on the hook for nearly $55 million in guaranteed salary for this year.

 Penix was their starter at the beginning of 2025 but is coming off a torn ACL . Because Penix hasn't been cleared for 11-on-11 team drills, this "competition" hasn't really gotten off the ground. And unless Penix gets out there soon, Tagovailoa will become the Week 1 starter by default. Tagovailoa wasn't good in the Falcons' first preseason game last weekend, but the new coaching staff under Kevin Stefanski likes his fit in the offense and believes Atlanta can get him ready in time for Week 1.

 No matter what happens, though, there's uncertainty beyond this season. Tagovailoa signed for only one year. Unlike Kyler Murray , who was in a similar situation when Arizona cut him with guaranteed money left on his deal and signed with Minnesota, Tagovailoa doesn't have a clause in his contract prohibiting his new team from using its franchise tag on him after this season. So if Tagovailoa played well and the Falcons wanted to keep him, they could -- but they aren't committed to it.

 

 As for Penix, the Falcons have to decide by the first week of May 2027 whether to pick up (and fully guarantee) his option for 2028. They'll need more information than they currently have on him before making that decision. Ideally, they'll see him play at some point this season. It's also worth noting that both of these players have significant injury histories. Tagovailoa has missed 20 games because of injury over the course of his six-year NFL career, and Penix suffered four season-ending injuries during his college career and then another last year in the NFL.

 Most likely outcome: Tagovailoa starts the season but struggles with health and/or performance, and the Falcons turn to Penix once he is healthy to continue their assessment of whether he can be their long-term answer. The new front office and coaching staff that took over following the 2025 season selects a QB early in the 2027 draft, either to develop behind Penix or to replace him if Atlanta has decided he isn't the answer.

 Long-shot outcome: Tagovailoa turns out to be an excellent fit for Stefanski's offense and has a good year. The Falcons win the NFC South for the first time since 2016 and make the playoffs for the first time since 2017. After the season, the Falcons and Tagovailoa agree on a Daniel Jones - or Baker Mayfield -style contract extension that keeps him there a couple of years more.

 

 
 

 Baltimore Ravens 
 Current starter:   Lamar Jackson 
 Signed through: 2027

 Two-time league MVP Jackson is making $52 million this year and $52 million in 2027, though none of the 2027 money is guaranteed. His contract contains void years in 2028 through 2030 for cap accounting purposes, but it voids after the 2027 season. It also includes a no-trade clause and a clause prohibiting the team from designating him its franchise or transition player. So if Jackson plays out the current deal and doesn't extend it, he'll hit free agency in March 2028, and the Ravens wouldn't be able to do a thing about it.

 Baltimore tried to do an extension with Jackson this spring in an effort to lower his 2026 cap hit, but it was unable to get a deal done. So it ended up lowering that cap hit by about $40 million through a simple restructure . As a result, his cap hit for 2027 is now projected to be $84.3 million, which means the Ravens have to either extend him or restructure the contract again next spring in order to save cap room.

 

 Jackson is coming off a down year by his own lofty standards, as he missed four games…

The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action.  Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Bills camp 
 
 New grass field held up well in opener, Bills president says 
 Bills' Phidarian Mathis banned 3 games for substance abuse violation 
 Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson carted off with leg injury 
 Josh Allen on Bills' alternate uniforms: 'Stop hating on the jerseys' 
 
 
 Thursday, Aug. 20 
 BEREA, Ohio -- The Bills' joint practice with the  Cleveland Browns Thursday turned into a display of tight ends for the offense. The big play of the day came on a 50-plus yard throw from quarterback Josh Allen to Dalton Kincaid with no defenders around the tight end. Kincaid described the play as "the most open I've ever been in the NFL."

 While an issue in coverage might have been involved, the play was an example of what Kincaid can contribute, especially when healthy (he played on limited snaps most of the 2025 season because of a left knee injury).

 "It's no secret that we're a better offense when [Kincaid's] on the field for us," Allen said. "... I feel like we're really clicking on the same page right now. And yeah, he opens up so much."

 Second-year tight end Jackson Hawes also had a big day, catching two touchdowns -- one from Allen and the other from backup QB  Kyle Allen .

 "[Hawes'] got some real nuance to his receiving game," Allen said.

 

 More observations: 

 
 The Bills continue to deal with lingering injuries as DT Ed Oliver and rookie WR Skyler Bell were not seen at practice. Several players were present, but not participating, including C Connor McGovern (right leg), RB Ty Johnson , WR Keon Coleman (right foot), WR Khalil Shakir (right leg), WR Dante Pettis , S C.J. Gardner-Johnson and rookie S Jalon Kilgore (right leg). 
 S Jordan Hancock took advantage of a Deshaun Watson pass thrown right to him in the red zone and picked it off, making sure to run all the way to the other end zone. 
 RB Ian Wheeler trucked a Browns defender on a red zone play, getting a big reaction from the Bills offense. 
 Despite not practicing, Gardner-Johnson was a consistent vocal presence, including chirping at the Browns offense. 
 Coach Joe Brady said before practice that he wanted to see how the session went before deciding if the first-team would play in Saturday's preseason game in Cleveland. Allen and the other starters saw extensive work in practice. 
 
 
 Tuesday, Aug. 18 
 The Bills took to the field for the team's second open practice in the new Highmark Stadium early Tuesday morning, and the practice featured some developments on the injury front.

 Two expected starters -- safety Cole Bishop and cornerback Maxwell Hairston (groin) -- returned to practice after missing time over the past week. Hairston hadn't practiced since Aug. 6. Wide receiver DJ Moore also participated in practice after being looked at by athletic trainers during Saturday's preseason game against the  Carolina Panthers . He did not, however, participate in team drills.

 Players to keep an eye on in the wide receiver room include: Rookie Skyler Bell continues to miss time, while Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman did not practice for the first time this camp. Coleman was wearing a walking boot on his right foot. The team is not sharing injury designations in the preseason.

 Other players not practicing include defensive tackle Ed Oliver , rookie safety Jalon Kilgore (wrap on right leg), safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson , running back Ty Johnson and center Connor McGovern  (McGovern said Saturday that his goal is to be back for the regular season).

 Next up for Buffalo is a joint practice at the  Cleveland Browns  on Thursday, which should serve as an extensive look at the first-team offense and defense.

 A couple fights broke out late in practice among linemen. Overall, though, fights have been limited during camp and the skirmishes on Tuesday were relatively brief. 
 Rookie linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr almost intercepted a Josh Allen  pass and was visibly frustrated when he couldn't bring it in. He is competing with Dorian Williams for a starting inside linebacker job. 
 

 
 Thursday, Aug. 13 
 One key player the Bills are looking forward to having back on the field for the regular season is edge rusher  Michael Hoecht . Hoecht has been a full participant for much of training camp while working back from a torn right Achilles suffered in November.

 Coach Joe Brady said that the plan is for Hoecht to play in a preseason game, but did not want to disclose if that would be this week or in the future. Hoecht also said after practice that he believes it's a game-time decision.

 "[Hoecht's] way ahead of schedule, seeing what he's able to do," Brady said. "And so, if it's not this week, I do want to get him preseason football. Shoot, he's gonna want to do preseason season football."

 Other observations:  

 
 C Connor McGovern , RB Ty Johnson , WR Skyler Bell . CB Maxwell Hairston .and CB Kani Walker are all facing injuries, while S Cole Bishop and S C.J. Gardner-Johnson did not participate in practice. Hairston and Bishop did do some work inside the team's fieldhouse while the rest of the team was outside. 
 Offensive coordinator Pete Carmichael will be in the coaching booth instead of the sideline for Saturday's preseason game. Carmichael has traditionally coached on the sideline, but Brady wants to experiment with him in each place during the preseason. 
 Quarterback Shane Buechele threw interceptions on back-to-back plays during 11-on-11 drills. The first was a pick-six by defensive back Te'Cory Couch and the second was on an errant throw taken away by linebacker Jimmy Ciarlo . 
 

 

 Who is the Bills' top performer so far at camp? 
 Nickel corner Dee Alford . Quarterback Josh Allen put it best, "Dee Alford's been making a lot of plays." This could go to a couple of players, including receiver DJ Moore , but Alford has stood out on a defense that is undergoing major change. His training camp performance featured three interceptions off Allen.

 

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Where does this defense stand? This is the part of the team that underwent the biggest change this offseason, going from a 4-3 base under Sean McDermott the last nine seasons to a 3-4 with new coordinator Jim Leonhard. Getting a look at this unit in game action will continue to help in seeing more and more of what to expect. Keep in mind, however, that multiple defensive secondary starters are dealing with injuries, including safeties Bishop and Gardner-Johnson and CB Hairston.

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 The Bills wide receivers room is a popular topic of conversation. While DJ Moore 's connection with quarterback Josh Allen has been a camp highlight, it was Joshua Palmer who stood out with a couple of nice grabs in Tuesday's practice.

 Palmer's first season with the Bills was disrupted by injuries, especially a left ankle injury, but the receiver said he is now feeling much more comfortable. Getting significant, and reliable, contributions from players such as Palmer would be big for Joe Brady's offense.

 "I don't have to question any of my movements," Palmer said. "I don't have to think before the route. I don't have to ... I'm not stressed before I go on the field. I just go out and play."

title: 'This is it': Bengals' Joe Burrow tired of waiting, targets Super Bowl
summary: The Bengals improved their defense after missing the playoffs a third straight year. Will it be enough?
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- There are a couple of reasons Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow isn't backing down from the championship chatter before the start of the new season.

 For starters, Burrow is hopeful that by talking about it enough, he can will a potential run to the Super Bowl into existence.

 The other reason? After two seasons of falling short after deep playoff runs, followed by three years of missing the postseason, enough is enough. Burrow is treating this season as a now-or-never year for Cincinnati.

 "You can keep pushing it down the road or you can talk about it now and say this is the year," Burrow said Thursday. "You know, I'm tired of saying, 'Next year, next year, next year.' This is it.

 "Your life is too short to keep pushing things down the road. I'm trying to instill some urgency and some intensity in everybody to go and be great every day and try to make it happen."

 

 That urgency has been a theme throughout the offseason and on Thursday following the team's joint practice against the Chicago Bears . While both first-team offenses had their fair share of good moments during team drills, Cincinnati closed the day with a clean victory.

 In the final two periods that mimicked the last 3:30 of a game, the Bengals' starters won both of them. Following a defensive stop, the offense moved the ball just enough to put kicker Evan McPherson in position for a field goal that won the period.

 In the second period, Cincinnati's defense dominated. First, newly acquired defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II picked off a ball he batted into the air. Then, defensive end Myles Murphy got two sacks, including one safety, before cornerback Jalen Davis intercepted Chicago's Caleb Williams as Williams remained under pressure a few yards away from his own goal line.

 It was exactly the type of showing the Bengals were hoping for when Cincinnati revamped the team after a 6-11 campaign last year. It was the first losing season since Burrow's rookie year in 2020 and a far cry from the team that lost in Super Bowl LVI in Jan. 2022 and lost in the AFC Championship Game a year later.

 In recent months, Burrow has spoken about his title aspirations, even drawing comparisons between this year's Bengals roster and the 2019 LSU team he led to an undefeated season and College Football Playoff title.

 That talk has been intentional.

 

 "I'm trying to put it out into the world," Burrow said. "I'm trying to manifest it. I'm trying to show our guys the urgency that I have and that I want us to have as an organization to go and make it happen."

 Since the end of last season, Cincinnati has operated as aggressively as it ever has. It signed linebacker  Boye Mafe  to a three-year, $60 million deal, and traded for Lawrence, which has already provided promising returns. After beating up on Cincinnati's offensive line throughout training camp, he caused havoc against the Bears.

 "He's an All-Pro guy," said Williams, adding that Lawrence is in the same category as Kansas City's Chris Jones . "He's a force to be reckoned with, and that's something that you go into a game week that you plan for him, that you plan to execute against him and doing things that aren't necessarily in his favor."

 Cincinnati's front office held up its end of the bargain when it came to producing a championship-level defense. Burrow said on Thursday that he believes the side of the ball that struggled so much over the past two seasons is good enough to push the Bengals back to the Super Bowl.

 However, an offense that is tinkering with a more varied attack is still trying to find its footing as the preseason winds down. Burrow acknowledged as much on Thursday.

 "We have to be more consistent on offense," Burrow said. "Our standard is so high, but it's so high because of what we've done and what we can do."

 Cincinnati still has three weeks until the season opener against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

 That's when the Bengals will start to find out if it will finally be the year it all comes together -- or what might happen if it doesn't.

 Thursday, Aug. 20 
 After a spirited joint practice with the Buffalo Bills on Thursday, Browns coach Todd Monken said he doesn't anticipate seeing the team's older starters play in Saturday's preseason game.

 Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson split first-team reps in the practice. Watson delivered one of his best throws of camp early in practice, when he found rookie wide receiver KC Concepcion downfield in between a pair of Bills defenders. Watson, though, had a poor stretch in red zone drills, sailing a pass to a wide-open Harold Fannin Jr . and then throwing an interception to defensive back Jordan Hancock a couple of plays later.

 One of Sanders' best moments came during a third-down session. On one play, Sanders used his cadence to draw the Bills defense offside and threw a downfield pass to wide receiver Isaiah Bond , who drew a defensive pass interference penalty. On the next play, Sanders found wideout Malachi Corley downfield for a big gain in the middle of the field.

 Sanders led Cleveland's only two-minute drill in practice and drove the offense the length of the field, but he was "sacked" on the penultimate play, and then his last-second pass to rookie wide receiver Denzel Boston in the end zone was broken up by corner Maxwell Hairston .

 "It didn't look like we were out of place. It looked like we belonged," Monken said after the practice.

 

 More observations: 

 
 On the second play of a two-minute drill, the Browns defense allowed a 50-yard touchdown pass from Josh Allen to Dalton Kincaid on an apparent coverage bust. 
 Running back Quinshon Judkins missed his second day of practice with what Monken called a "nagging" injury. 
 Defensive end Alex Wright left practice on a cart after sustaining an apparent injury in defensive line-offensive line 1-on-1s. 
 Defensive tackle Travis Bell left practice early with a member of the medical staff. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 17 

 Shedeur Sanders is slated to start at quarterback in the Browns' second preseason game against the Bills on Saturday, but he could be playing without Cleveland's starting offense.

 Coach Todd Monken said he and Bills coach Joe Brady agreed to hold out starters if their No. 1 units get enough work in during joint practices on Thursday.

 "Would I like to have a decision today? Of course," Monken said. "Would I like a decision by next Monday? Of course. I'd love to have that decision. And we'll see. We've got a lot of football this week. We've already had a lot of football. We've got four days of practice and a game. That all adds into any decision with the roster and who the starters are.

 "Some are further along than others, right? We already know. That's part of it. And I'm OK. By the time we get to next week, that'd be great. We can start planning that way, have some practices, and here we go."

 More observations: 

 
 Michael Coats Jr . and Nate Evans practiced after leaving the preseason opener with injuries. 
 Zak Zinter , Myles Bryant , and Elijah Chatman returned to practice after missing multiple sessions, as well as the preseason opener.

 Monken said the Browns are being "overly cautious" with Schwesinger, who hasn't practiced since July 31. The team is hopeful he will return to practice next week. 
 The Browns signed tight end Jermaine Terry II and waived tight end Brenden Bates with an injury designation. 
 

 

 Who has been the Browns' top performer so far at camp? 
 WR Denzel Boston . The No. 39 overall pick is trending to be Cleveland's No. 1 receiver sooner rather than later. Boston has dazzled with plenty of highlights, using his 6-foot-4, 215-pound frame to make contested catches almost daily. He's also made himself a friendly target for quarterbacks as a smooth route runner. Boston recently got promoted to the No. 1 offense as Cleveland's boundary receiver.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Who will be the Browns' starting quarterback? Deshaun Watson will start the preseason opener;  Shedeur Sanders will start the second preseason game. The exhibition matches will allow Todd Monken to evaluate the quarterbacks in a bevy of game-like situations. The first-year head coach is placing an importance on pre-snap operation and playmaking ability.

 
 Wednesday, Aug. 12 
 The Browns are hoping quarterback  Deshaun Watson 's return to health will mean a return to the Pro Bowl form he displayed with the Texans, but Watson said Wednesday that "my game has definitely changed."

 "I'm different, man," Watson said before practice. "I think ever since I've been here early on, bringing up Houston was cool, but I'm 30 now. I had some injuries and things like that. So, my game has definitely changed. But the mentality in how I play and how I approach it doesn't."

 Watson was one of the NFL's top dual-threat passers in Houston, but suspension and injuries have limited him to just 19 games since Cleveland traded for him in March 2022.

 "I think you have to be who you are because if you try to be something you're not, you're not going to play at the highest level of your skill set," coach Todd Monken said. "So it's just the way it is with him; he's going to have to play or utilize his athleticism in order to play at the top of his skill set. ... But one of the superpowers is his athleticism. I mean, that always has been. So you can't take that away or you've basically taken away a part of what made him special."

 In a lighter practice ahead of the team's preseason opener against the Bears, Watson and Shedeur Sanders led successful two-minute drills to cap the session. Both quarterbacks connected on deep passes during their possession. Sanders had a deep completion to wide receiver Isaiah Bond , who made a diving catch. title: 2026 Dallas Cowboys training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Cowboys training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Cowboys reporter Todd Archer has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at the Cowboys' camp. Will Dallas turn around the NFL's worst defense from 2025? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Cowboys' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Cowboys camp 
 
 Cowboys, Saints fined $500K each for brawls in joint practice 
 Is Cowboys' DaRon Bland finally over his nagging foot issue? 
 Miller to play 15th season after getting 1-year deal from Cowboys 
 Sources: Cowboys, Quinnen Williams reach 3-year, $105.9M deal 
 Cowboys' Dak Prescott not shying away from setting lofty goals 
 Jones optimistic about Cowboys, likes 'what we put together' 
 Source: Ex-Cowboys QB Will Grier returns as offensive assistant 
 Quieter offseason has Cowboys focused on the right things 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 20 

 Coach Brian Schottenheimer was clear: training camp for the Dallas Cowboys is not over. But Thursday marked the final full practice in Oxnard, California.

 The two-hour session was conducted in full pads, two days before the Cowboys' second preseason game against the Arizona Cardinals . The Cowboys will have an hour workout Friday before flying to Phoenix.

 Owner and general manager Jerry Jones liked what he saw in the 13 practices.

 Jones was asked about which individual players stood out, but he went with position groups instead, mentioning the wide receivers, quarterbacks and the secondary.

 "We've gotten a lot of reps and within those reps we've seen some young players that didn't disappoint," Jones said. "And we also saw some veteran players that are new to the team that are fitting right in with the coaching they're getting. So when you weigh all of that, I really am excited about where we are."

 More observations: 

 
 Von Miller got some work in team drills for the first time since signing this week. He was able to work the edge on both right tackles, Terence Steele and Nate Thomas , to pressure Dak Prescott . 
 After going through a relatively quiet camp in terms of injuries, a number of players were unable to finish practice Thursday. Nose tackle Jay Toia (elbow) and tight end DJ Rogers (knee) were scheduled to have MRIs. Edge rusher James Houston also left practice early. 
 It was a strong finish for rookie defensive back  Caleb Downs , covering wide receivers and tight ends. He broke up a Prescott pass to Luke Schoonmaker over the middle and had blanket coverage later on Jake Ferguson . 
 Ferguson and DeMarvion Overshown were in a brief tussle after Ferguson tossed the ball at him after a catch. Neither was ejected from practice. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 19 
 Training camp opened with the Cowboys wanting a competition at left tackle between Tyler Guyton and Nate Thomas , but it never really materialized in part because of how well Guyton has performed.

 In the past two days, coach Brian Schottenheimer and offensive coordinator Klayton Adams spoke about the other side of the line and the right tackle situation, where Terence Steele is the starter.

 "T-Steele's got to play a little bit more consistent," Schottenheimer said. "He has had a couple days where he's been a little bit dropping his pads and getting edged a little bit. He needs to be better."

 Adams wonders if by working less, Steele will benefit. Steele, entering his seventh season, has played 2,333 of a possible 2,357 snaps the past two seasons.

 "He and I had a good conversation about that this morning of how we continue to try to find consistency," Adams said. "He's a guy that's going into Year 7, and he's never going to ask for a day off. He's never going to ask for a break. So we're just searching for ways to help him and help him play at his best and most consistently."

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 18 

 Amid the fights and skirmishes between the Cowboys and Saints, there was actually some practice, but not enough for coach Brian Schottenheimer's liking.

 On the first play between the offense and defense, there was a shoving match. On the fifth snap between the first-teamers, there was a fight. But let's stick to football, specifically the Cowboys' first-team offense against the Saints' defense.

 Unofficially,  Dak Prescott was 20-of-25 with one interception. On a crosser to CeeDee Lamb , the pass sailed over Lamb and right into the arms of safety Julian Blackmon . Prescott had a deep completion near the sideline to George Pickens that drew loud cheers from the fans.

 In red zone work, Prescott had touchdown passes to tight end  Jake Ferguson on a shovel pass, a quick throw to Pickens on a slant and a perfectly placed ball to the post that was high enough that only receiver  Ryan Flournoy could come down with the catch. Pickens was flagged for a celebration penalty by the officials when he flipped the ball in the direction of Saints cornerback  Kool-Aid McKinstry .

 "I think we're finding our rhythm," Schottenheimer said. "I'll go back to the preseason game. I think we kind of found our rhythm even in the second half against Seattle. And that's what training camp is for."

 

 Who is the Cowboys' top performer so far at camp? 

 George Pickens . He has essentially made a big play in every practice as he gets set to play on the $27.3 million franchise tag. Whatever disenchantment some might have expected from Pickens without a long-term deal has not materialized. Coaches have noted his attention in the meeting rooms since the start of training camp.

 He and Dak Prescott have picked up where they left off in 2025 when the receiver had career highs in catches, yards and touchdowns. Does that mean he will surpass those figures again in 2026? Not necessarily, but his performance so far has shown a focused player as the season inches closer.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 Because the Cowboys aren't going to play their starters in the preseason, it's impossible to completely answer anything about the defense. There have been encouraging signs there, but let's look to the offense for what can be answered in the preseason games: Who will back up Prescott?

 Joe Milton III and Sam Howell have alternated as Prescott's backup in practice and both have had good moments and not-so-good ones. The Cowboys believe they have line play and skill players to give both QBs a fair shot to perform in the preseason and not have them running for their lives. Read more below:

 

 Monday, Aug. 17 

 For the second time this month, the Cowboys will hold a joint practice, hosting the New Orleans Saints  on Tuesday after traveling to the Los Angeles Rams a week ago.

 The importance of the work isn't lost on tight end Jake Ferguson , who, like the rest of the Cowboys' starters and regulars, will not play in any of the three preseason games.

 "It's usually their starting defense going against our starting offense," Ferguson said. "That's where we get a good read of what we're looking like, what we're feeling like, what we need to clean up. We had that one against the Rams and came out firing. It was a lot of things we needed to clean up, but this is a good tell."

 The Saints will bring a familiar face with coach Kellen Moore. Ten years ago, Moore was Tony Romo 's backup for Dallas before breaking his ankle early in training camp. It helped pave the way for Dak Prescott to become the starter. Moore became a Cowboys assistant coach and served as offensive coordinator from 2019 to 2022. Moore also interviewed for the Cowboys head coaching vacancy that…
