title: Is Cowboys' DaRon Bland finally over his nagging foot issue?
summary: Bland set an NFL record in 2023 with five pick-sixes and hopes to get back to form in 2026, boosted by some new shoes.
full_text:
OXNARD, Calif. --  DaRon Bland 's feet tell his story.

 A cornerback's success has more to do with feet than anything else. Backpedaling at the snap. Driving on a throw from the quarterback. Sprinting stride-for-stride with a wide receiver.

 If the footwork isn't good, then a cornerback will be in trouble.

 But what about when a foot isn't healthy? What then?

 Late in the 2024 training camp, Bland had surgery on his left foot to repair a fifth metatarsal stress fracture and missed the first 10 games of the season. He never felt quite the same as he had his first two years when he intercepted 14 passes and set an NFL record with five pick-sixes in 2023.

 

 Last season, the 2022 fifth-round pick was placed on injured reserve with three games remaining and had his second left foot surgery in as many years. In January, Dr. David Porter, a consultant for the Indianapolis Colts , replaced the screw in Bland's foot. He rehabbed throughout the offseason with the idea of being 100% ready for training camp.

 "It's a lot better," Bland said. "I mean I don't really feel no aches or pains that much. Little soreness here and there, but nothing major."

 Bland's movements appear sharper than last year. His quickness is better. He looks more confident.

 "I'm definitely getting a lot more push now getting out of my breaks," Bland said. "Not worried about it."

 

 Bland has made one change that he believes has helped his foot. He is wearing size 15 cleats instead of a size 14.

 "It's just us trying different things and trying to see what's best," Bland said. "So far this has felt the best right now."

 It doesn't matter to the Cowboys whether it's comfort or confidence. They need Bland, who signed a four-year, $90 million extension in 2025, to find the form of his first two seasons in new coordinator Christian Parker's scheme.

 As much as Bland's foot has been rebuilt, Schottenheimer does not believe there is a need to rebuild Bland's confidence because he showed his capability with 14 interceptions in his first two seasons.

 During that same stretch, he allowed seven touchdowns and a 60% completion rate in 877 coverage snaps, per ESPN Research. In his past two seasons with the foot injury, he allowed 10 touchdowns and a 65% completion rate in 687 coverage snaps.

 Bland returned his lone interception last season 68 yards for a touchdown.

 "DaRon doesn't say much, but he's extremely confident," Schottenheimer said. "He can't do what he's done in this league, even as a young, young player and not be pretty confident."

 

 This year, Bland has a third different position coach in as many seasons with Derrick Ansley, who came over from the Green Bay Packers . Given Parker's background with defensive backs -- coaching Pat Surtain II with the Denver Broncos , and Quinyon Mitchell and Cooper DeJean with the Philadelphia Eagles , plus Ansley -- Schottenheimer sees technical improvement in Bland.

 "I think he's really taken to the fundamentals in the scheme," Schottenheimer said. "But just really the way DA and those guys are coaching him, you see him flashing with the quick decisions and the quick breaks and the PBUs [pass breakups]. But I really like watching him too with the crack replaces, coming up and filling on runs, and things like that."

 While some cornerbacks can be loud and brash, Bland is reserved and quiet. When asked what he liked about Bland's camp, Ansley first mentioned his leadership and the tutoring he is doing with second-year cornerback Shavon Revel Jr.  Ansley said Bland is a "relationship guy" and an "observer."

 "You can tell why he's been All-Pro," Ansley said, "because he doesn't get rattled. He makes a play, he's the same guy. He gives up a play, he's the same guy. That's a characteristic that you need at corner because your life out there, you're walking on landmines, and at some point you're going to step on one and it explodes. You've got to be able to come back to life."

 Teammates, coaches and front office personnel have told him they see a difference between this year and last year. More importantly, he feels a difference.

 "Definitely sometimes you be in your head about this," Bland said.

title: Why Lions, NFL coaches believe Super Bowl chances are possible
summary: If you don't believe Campbell & Co. that the Lions will be contenders, ask Sean McVay, Matt LaFleur and others.
full_text:
DETROIT -- When Dan Campbell arrived for the NFL's annual league meeting in March, no one would have guessed he was three months removed from one of his most disappointing seasons as the  Detroit Lions ' coach.

 Instead, those who saw him at the Arizona Biltmore in Phoenix were more preoccupied with his hair, which along with his goatee was considerably longer than anyone covering the team since 2021 could remember.

 "You know what? I just haven't cut it," Campbell joked. "I haven't cut it. I cut the sides, but I haven't."

 

 His relaxed look mirrored the calm confidence with which he discussed his team while answering questions from reporters alongside his coaching peers. He talked about his team heading into the 2026 season -- expressing his belief in the staff and the roster that he and general manager Brad Holmes had built.

 "We've been going. It's been fun. Been fun. Brad and I have been -- we've been back in the bunker just going at it," Campbell said. "It's been fun. It really has. Kind of a little bit of a rebirth, actually."

 His Lions were in need of the mini reset. They had won 15 games in 2024 and 12 the season before that, cementing themselves as one of the NFC's top contenders along the way. But in 2025, after losing both coordinators and eight coaches overall, they won just nine games and missed the playoffs for the first time since 2022.

 This offseason, some change was inevitable. The biggest: Campbell brought in former Arizona Cardinals offensive coordinator Drew Petzing to replace John Morton, whom the Lions fired in January after the first-time OC struggled to give Detroit an offensive identity. Detroit also put the finishing touches on a two-year renovation of the offensive line by moving All-Pro Penei Sewell from right tackle to left, adding Cade Mays in free agency and drafting tackle  Blake Miller  with the No. 17 selection.

 

 Otherwise, the team that enters the 2026 campaign is largely made up of the same nucleus that helped push the Lions to so much success. And Detroit has doubled down by locking down two of its young stars in running back Jahmyr Gibbs and linebacker Jack Campbell  with lucrative contract extensions. Those signings followed new deals they've given to other homegrown talents over the past three years and raised their overall investment in extensions to more than $1 billion over that span.

 Dan Campbell said the commitment to the current roster, combined with the organization's recent track record of success, is why he and the Lions remain confident their championship window remains open despite last season's setback.

 "Our window is not closed. It's not closed. That was the whole reason why we did this. We fell short last year. But needed to get in [the playoffs], and now it's about the matchups, where you're playing and who you're playing," Campbell told ESPN of his team, which is  favored by DraftKings to win the NFC North and have the fifth-best odds to win the conference . "We want to be able to do that every year, and sometimes, I'm just saying is what happens is, you want to go all-in for one player, well how do you know that one player doesn't get hurt?

 "Or how do you know the three players behind him don't get hurt and now you've got no depth. Whereas, let's just get a unit together that we feel like can compete every year and then it's about in that moment, we're making those plays and finding a way to win that game."

 And they are not alone in their assessment of the team. Asking about the Lions' prospects revealed a consensus from top coaches around the NFL -- from the  Los Angeles Rams ' Sean McVay to the  Green Bay Packers ' Matt LaFleur -- that the 2026 Lions are not the 9-8 team the league saw last season.

 Here's what the Lions and others around the league are saying about Detroit's Super Bowl worthiness in 2026.

 

 

 Part of the reason for Detroit's uncharacteristic 2025 campaign was the turnover on the coaching staff. After finishing 15-2 in 2024, the Lions most notably lost offensive coordinator Ben Johnson and defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn, who took head coaching jobs with the Chicago Bears and the  New York Jets , respectively. Those two departures were big losses for the team. But an underappreciated aspect that contributed to its struggles last season was the sheer number of coaches Campbell had to replace. 

 Campbell: "Well, you learn. But I don't think anybody necessarily tells you, 'Hey, be ready to lose [eight] coaches in one year.' Of course, that's the plan. You're going to lose some guys, you do it right and then the next guy, you can promote or you can go find guys. But when you're talking about [eight coaches], that's a tall task. But you owe it to the players, you owe it to the organization to find the best guy.

 

 "So, I feel like those pieces we added last year, for the most part, really fit what we're about and are good for us."

 McVay: "I think it's a champagne problem. When you end up losing coaches for the reasons that you're talking about with Dan, that means you're doing really well. People want to try to replicate. Or people in your building that are in leadership roles, they want to have them lead or take elevated steps in their career.

 "What I would say is it's a blessing. What I've really leaned into for us is what's been really fortunate is you get exposure to new people. New ideas."

 Glenn: "It's a really good problem to have because usually when you're losing coaches like that, that means you're doing well."

 LaFleur: "I do think that is a challenge, obviously. [Campbell] lost both of his coordinators, and there's a little bit of learning curve there and sometimes you have some growing pains, but I still think they're an elite team."

 

 In Johnson's three years as OC, the Lions established one of the NFL's most dangerous and prolific offenses. In 2024, his unit scored a franchise-record 564 points and led the league in scoring for the first time since 1954. Since 2022 -- the year Johnson took over playcalling duties midseason -- the Lions are tops in the NFL in scoring and total offense. While they still managed 481 points last season, they failed to establish an offensive identity outside of home run plays, and Morton, who replaced Johnson, was relieved of playcalling duties in November. In January, the Lions fired Morton and hired Petzing, who'd spent the previous three seasons as OC of the Cardinals. 

 Campbell: "I feel like the addition with Drew Petzing is going to be great for us. I think it's going to get us centralized. Back to being centralized more on offense."

 McVay: "This league is so volatile, great coaches get let go every year and great coaches become available. And I think when you show your place is a developmental staff that'll invest in the human being and help them get to places that Dan and I were fortunate enough to get to, you attract high-caliber people and you've got to lean into it."

 

 

 The Cardinals ranked second in the NFL in rushing yards per attempt (4.92) and ninth in total rushing yards (6,399) during Petzing's three years of calling plays in Arizona. And while Detroit's average yards per carry remained steady from 2024 to 2025 (4.7 to 4.6), the team's attempts, rushes per game and rushes of 10 or more yards per game all dipped last season. 

 Petzing, on what he wants from his offense in Detroit: "It needs to be physical, it needs to be tough, it needs to be difficult to defend and it needs to be multiple at times.

 "It's not going to all run through one person, it's not going to run through one personnel, it's going to change week to week. I think that's important in this league. Defensive coordinators, I think, do things at a really high level. They watch tape, they understand scheme. So, I think that's a big part of what we need to be on offense."

title: 2026 NFL preseason Week 2: Game takeaways, analysis
summary: Week 2 of the NFL preseason is underway, and our NFL Nation reporters are tackling the biggest looming roster questions coming off each game.
full_text:
Week 2 of the  2026 NFL preseason kicked off Thursday, giving us more insight into position battles and the push to make 53-man rosters before the cut-down deadline Aug. 30. Action began with two games Thursday, and that will be followed by three games Friday, 10 on Saturday and the first Sunday night game of the season to wrap things up.

 What are the biggest questions for the teams after each game? What have we learned about how depth charts are shaping up? And what solutions could present themselves based on preseason play in Week 2?

 Our NFL Nation reporters picked out what you need to know about big roster decisions and more coming off Week 2 of the preseason.

 
 Quick links: 
 Full schedule | Where to watch 
 Depth charts  | Sign up to play fantasy 

 
 

 Thursday's games 

 49ers 41, Chargers 17 
 

 49ers:  What is the state of the receiver and guard depth charts?  The battle for receiver roster spots has been hard to decipher, but Jacob Cowing helped his cause significantly Thursday night due to his special teams contributions. Cowing returned a punt 83 yards for a score and is the most reliable punt return option on the roster. That should help him land on the initial 53-man roster, even if it means saying goodbye to a more proven veteran.

 Elsewhere, it's still unclear whether the Niners have a starting-caliber left guard, with rookie Carver Willis getting the start against the Chargers. Willis, Connor Colby and Robert Jones have been competing for that spot, but none of them has done enough to separate from the others. Austen Pleasants also entered the mix Thursday, creating more questions at the position.  -- Nick Wagoner 

 Next game: at  Las Vegas Raiders  (Aug. 27, 8 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited)

 

 Chargers:  Is Jake Slaughter ready to be the starting center?  The biggest news of the week for the Chargers was the injury to center Tyler Biadasz , who suffered an ACL injury to his left knee Tuesday and is out indefinitely.

 Slaughter, a second-round rookie, will likely begin the season as the Chargers' starting center, where he played all his college snaps. He got his first shot at that job Thursday night, playing nine snaps. He allowed zero pressures, according to NFL Next Gen Stats.  -- Kris Rhim 

 Next game: vs.  Los Angeles Rams  (Aug. 27, 10 p.m. ET, NFL Network)

 

 Raiders 22, Texans 20 
 

 Raiders:  How much confidence do the Raiders have in their secondary?  Las Vegas' secondary has potential, but will that lead to success in 2026? Second-year cornerback Darien Porter is still learning the position after spending most of his college career as a wide receiver. He started 10 games as a rookie, but he has a lot more growing to do. Fourth-round rookie corner Jermod McCoy hasn't played football in more than a year because of a knee injury, so it will take time before he feels like his true self. Fifth-round rookie corner  Hezekiah Masses  is also learning. Second-round safety Treydan Stukes has the best chance of making a positive impact as a rookie, but the Raiders are taking his development slowly because they are asking him to play deep safety and nickel.

 The Raiders have struggled in coverage in two preseason games. Cardinals quarterbacks Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew II combined for 16 straight completions in the first half last week, and Texans backup Davis Mills completed 11 of 15 passes for 93 yards in the first half Thursday night. The Raiders' young secondary could be quite good in a season or two, but asking it to fix last season's pass-coverage issues immediately might be too tall a task.  -- Ryan McFadden 

 Next game: vs.  San Francisco 49ers  (Aug. 27, 8 p.m. ET, ESPN Unlimited)

 

 

 Texans:  What will Houston's offensive line eventually look like?  Houston's starting tackles Thursday were Trent Brown and Aireontae Ersery . First-round pick Keylan Rutledge started at left guard instead of center, where he has played for most of training camp, and  Evan Brown took first-team snaps instead. Ed Ingram started at right guard, leaving two free agent signees (right tackle Braden Smith and guard Wyatt Teller ) running with the second unit.

 The Texans signed Smith to a two-year, $20 million deal and Teller to a two-year, $16 million contract, with the expectation that both would start and boost the team's frequently problematic offensive line. So how will Houston decide which linemen to start Week 1? And do the Texans want $36 million worth of offseason signings on their backup unit?  -- DJ Bien-Aime 

 Next game: at  Carolina Panthers  (Aug. 28, 7 p.m. ET)

title: 2026 Kansas City Chiefs training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our updates from Chiefs training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Chiefs reporter Nate Taylor has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Chiefs camp. Can coach Andy Reid get the Chiefs back into the playoffs? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Chiefs' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Chiefs stories 
 
 Chiefs' Bieniemy: Wife to make full recovery after being shot 
 Rookie Benson earns shot to start at RT for Chiefs 
 Tight end Travis Kelce says he can still 'play at a high level' 
 Reid: Mahomes unlikely to play in preseason opener 
 Rookie wideout Cyrus Allen an early star of Chiefs training camp 
 
 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 20 

 At the end of the Chiefs' final training camp practice on Thursday, a ceremonial on-field session that was less than 90 minutes for fans and military members, quarterback Patrick Mahomes did something rare: He led the scout-team offense in the final 11-on-11 period to close his 10th camp.

 The final reps were run while Semisonic's classic 1998 song "Closing Time" played on the speakers, which is an annual tradition for coach Andy Reid.

 "They worked hard and I appreciate that," Reid said of his players. "I thought we made progress. It's the young guys that you're looking at here. We have a number of them. How they progress -- and continue to progress -- will be a big part of how this team does."

 Reid said Mahomes will not play in Saturday's exhibition against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . Other veterans, such as right guard Trey Smith (hip), left tackle Josh Simmons (back) and defensive end Ashton Gillotte (ruptured plantar fascia) will not play, either.

 Backup quarterback Justin Fields is expected to play into the second quarter for Saturday's exhibition. Reid was unsure if he would let Mahomes play a few snaps in the preseason finale next week against the Seattle Seahawks .

 "We'll see how that goes," Reid said. "We'll see."

 Additional notes: 

 
 In their initial evaluation, the Chiefs are optimistic that Gillotte could return in about three weeks. If his rehab goes well, Gillotte would have a chance to be available Sept. 14 to play on opening night against the Denver Broncos . 
 

 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 19 

 Mansoor Delane , the Chiefs' rookie cornerback and their top draft pick, is expected to make his preseason debut Saturday night against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

 In three consecutive padded practices, Delane has been competitive during man-to-man coverage reps against the Chiefs' top receivers -- such as Rashee Rice , Tyquan Thornton and rookie Cyrus Allen . Before Wednesday's practice, coach Andy Reid expressed how pleased he has been with Delane, who is a projected starter for longtime defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo.

 "You can see the talent," Reid said of Delane. "These next couple of weeks will be good for him. I like what I see. He's definitely not afraid out there -- or hesitant. If anything, you've got to tell him, 'OK, slow down and get those hands off of [the receiver].' He wants to snatch everybody. I mean, we play man [coverage]."

 One change the Chiefs made Wednesday was to have Delane wear mitts on his hands to prevent him from holding receivers during the one-on-one drill. Delane did well in those reps, although Allen was able to make a contested catch on a deep throw from backup quarterback Justin Fields . A few minutes later, Delane had a pass breakup on a shorter route in a rep against Allen.

 "He's a guy who has sticky coverage," defensive backs coach Dave Merritt said of Delane. "Getting him back in pads and seeing that he can actually tackle people now, hopefully that's going to show up this weekend."

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 18 

 Day after day, the Chiefs' injuries continue to pile up. For the first time in camp, left tackle Josh Simmons missed Tuesday's practice because of a back injury.

 Receivers Tyquan Thornton (strained hamstring) and Jimmy Holiday (quad) left practice early as well. Earlier during Tuesday's on-field work, defensive end Ashton Gillotte , who returned just two days ago following a strained hamstring, sustained a right foot injury while covering tight end Jared Wiley . Linebacker Jack Cochrane missed Tuesday's work with a right knee injury.

 Those players were added to a list that already includes safety Chamarri Conner (sore knee), right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerbacks L'Jarius Sneed (knee) and Kader Kohou (sore ankle), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee) who have been held out of practice for much of the past week.

 

 

 Monday, Aug. 17 

 Wearing the usual white jersey for defenders, Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane fully participated in Monday's practice for the first time since camp started.

 Delane missed Saturday's preseason opener as the Chiefs held him out while he continued to let his right shoulder heal, an injury that had led him to wear a noncontact yellow jersey and miss the 11-on-11 reps. In Monday's work, Delane did well to cover receivers such as Rashee Rice , Nikko Remigio and rookie Cyrus Allen . If Delane continues progressing this week, he should make his preseason debut Saturday when the Chiefs face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

 "He did everything and was in all the drills," coach Andy Reid said of Delane. "[He] looked good, so that's good work for him as he goes through that. We'll just monitor him and see how he does with the extended play."

 More observations: 

 
 Monday's practice was the Chiefs' longest of camp -- a session that lasted two hours and 15 minutes. Reid said backup left tackle Esa Pole left practice early because he was dehydrated. Receiver Andrew Armstrong sustained a strained hamstring, linebacker Jack Cochrane left early with a knee injury, and undrafted rookie safety DeShon Singleton tweaked a hamstring. 
 Missing practice were right guard Trey Smith (hip), cornerback  L'Jarius Sneed  (rest), linebacker Drue Tranquill (lower back spasms), safety Chamarri Conner (knee) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (right knee). "Trey is doing [well]," Reid said. "He's getting close. We'll see where it goes. I don't know if you'll see him this week, but he's getting close. 
 The lone major lineup change among the projected starters was along the offensive line. Kahlil Benson , the undrafted rookie from Indiana, switched from right guard -- the position he played in Saturday's preseason loss to the Los Angeles Rams -- to right tackle. Jaylon Moore , a five-year veteran, switched from right tackle to right guard, the spot where Smith starts. Reid suggested that Benson was moved to get him ready to play the right tackle position in Saturday's exhibition against the Buccaneers. "Moore has been doing a great job in there for us," Reid said. "With that, Benson doesn't get any reps at [right tackle]. We want him to go against the better players and have a chance to continue to grow there. We just flopped them over and let Moore get some reps at guard and Benson gets some reps at the tackle spot. Benson held his own at the guard spot in the game. They need to be able to play both [positions]. It's good experience for them." 
 

 

 

 Who has been the Chiefs' top performer so far at camp? 
 Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods has been a revelation. Not only has the first-round pick made an impact in each practice, but Woods has quickly shown that he has the quickness and strength to be a potential impact player next to pass rusher Chris Jones . Veterans including center Creed Humphrey ,…

title: Inside Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza's game preparation
summary: The rookie QB's studious history shows he'll be ready for Thursday's preseason game at Houston (8 p.m. ET, ESPN).
full_text:
HENDERSON, Nev. -- Quarterback Fernando Mendoza is a football nerd, but in a good way. Just ask his former high school coach, Dave Dunn.

 As a 15-year-old quarterback at Christopher Columbus High School in Miami, Mendoza would skip eating lunch with his classmates in the cafeteria and take his food to Dunn's office, where he would have a notebook and pen in hand to go over the practice plan.

 Their routine meetings continued throughout Mendoza's time at Christopher Columbus. Even in the offseason, Mendoza would go over what defenses are doing and come up with ideas for the Explorers to implement into their game plan.

 

 "How many 15-year-old kids are wired that way?" Dunn told ESPN.

 Mendoza's meticulous preparation and dedication to his craft propelled him from being a three-star recruit in high school to becoming a Heisman Trophy winner and national champion at Indiana in 2025.

 It is with these traits that the Las Vegas Raiders hope Mendoza can develop into the face of the franchise and help the organization achieve sustained success whenever the 2026 NFL draft's No. 1 pick is called to be the starting quarterback. For now, Mendoza will look to use his studious techniques for Thursday's preseason game against the Houston Texans ( 8 p.m. ET, ESPN ).

 "[At quarterback], the expectation is to be the most prepared guy in the building," Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said. "Out of the young quarterbacks that I have been around, I think he has the upper hand on them in that area."

 Dunn, who has been at Christopher Columbus since 2019 and even coached Mendoza's brother Alberto, said Fernando doesn't like to leave any stone unturned. In Dunn's experience with Mendoza, nothing rarely caught the South Florida native off guard.

 The coach attributed that to Mendoza studying and mentally preparing himself so that he could put the team in the best position to win games. Dunn recalled a moment during a regional final game in which Mendoza didn't see anyone open so he had to improvise and scramble for a touchdown on the first drive.

 

 Mendoza came back to the sideline, breaking down the play, step-by-step.

 "Every once in a while, somebody's going to throw something at you you've never seen before," Dunn said. "... [Mendoza] knew nothing was open, and he knew where the pressure was coming from. He goes, 'All right, I knew I had to move to my left. I had the X receiver as a possibility. Saw that he wasn't going to get open [and] my only option was to scramble.'"

 Dunn admired Mendoza's attention to detail and studious habits. Whenever he saw Mendoza in his office or in team meetings with a notebook, Dunn loved it even if he thought it was out of the norm for younger players.

 Mendoza was even preparing for Kubiak's offensive scheme before he heard his name called in April's draft. Last year in college, he watched a lot of NFL football on Sundays and film breakdowns of how Kubiak utilized the  Seattle Seahawks ' offense.

 Since Mendoza has been a Raider, his notebook is still one of his biggest assets. During Raiders OTAs, quarterbacks coach Mike Sullivan said Mendoza wrote out every pass play, detailing the progression and his footwork. Mendoza even gave his own critique of when he fell short or when he felt he did well.

 

 It was one of the examples Sullivan used to describe Mendoza's tireless work ethic and old-school approach.

 "[Mendoza] didn't have the neatest handwriting, but I appreciated him doing that. I said, 'Maybe you could type this next time,'" Sullivan said. "But he went through that process, and he's someone that I think a lot of his confidence comes from the preparation and the type of time and effort that he puts in."

 Mendoza understands he is behind the curve. Since the start of training camp, Mendoza has mostly played with the second-team offense, while Kirk Cousins has played solely with the starters.

 Last week, Mendoza watched Cousins orchestrate a scoring drive at the beginning of the Raiders' 27-14 preseason loss to the Arizona Cardinals . And he still saw a significant gap between the 15-year veteran signal-caller and himself.

 Still, Mendoza's performance was good enough for Kubiak to call him an "ascending player." He threw for 97 yards and a touchdown, showcasing that progress has been made. Mendoza, however, is a perfectionist, so he harped on his jitters during his first drive, the misthrows and misreads. Mendoza repeatedly mentioned what needs fine-tuning.

 "Like you see Kirk has this time [and] anticipation. ... That's an area I've got to grow in," Mendoza said.

 Mendoza has been putting in extra work outside of the team's training camp practices. He occasionally spends time with the centers on the roster to strengthen his comfort level with playing under center.

 

 He has spent late nights in the indoor practice field, going through the team's offensive script with some of his teammates. And following his preseason debut, Mendoza said he immediately began watching the film of his performance.

 Mendoza continues to be an avid listener, soaking in the advice he receives from Cousins, his coaches and minority owner and NFL legend Tom Brady.

 "You have to do everything that you possibly can to get that mental edge over your opponent, and that's what he's doing," Raiders wide receiver Jalen Nailor said. "He still has a long way to go, but having Kirk as a mentor to him, Tom [Brady] as well, is really going to help his game grow."

 Fullback Connor Heyward said: "He wants to earn everything, which is that much more special. ... When you have a quarterback like that, you know the future is very bright."

 

 Mendoza's short-term memory has also been essential for his development. He tries not to dwell on the mistakes, such as the interception he threw in the red zone to Texans safety Jalen Pitre during the Raiders' joint practice in Houston on Tuesday.

 Instead, he views those moments as learning experiences and maintains an optimistic mindset.

 "It would be letting my teammates down if I let that burden me throughout the next couple of series, because I wouldn't be able to play on time and they wouldn't be able to rely on me," Mendoza said. "Tranquilo, which means 'calm' in Spanish. I say 'tranquilo' and move forward. You know, it's all good."

 Dunn said it has been "surreal" to see Mendoza's rise over time. When Mendoza was an unheralded high school recruit with just one Power 5 offer from Cal, Dunn knew all Mendoza needed was a chance, and his former star player would shine.

 Cal gave Mendoza an opportunity from 2022 to 2024, and then the Hoosiers did in 2025. When the Raiders eventually hand him the keys to the offense, Dunn knows Mendoza will be ready because of the work he puts in.

 "He is a lifelong learner when it comes to football," Dunn said.

title: 2026 Minnesota Vikings training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Vikings training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Vikings reporter Kevin Seifert has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and of course the quarterback room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Vikings camp. Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Vikings' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Vikings stories 

 
 What Kyler Murray as QB1 means for Vikings, J.J. McCarthy 
 Vikings, O'Neill reach $96M extension 
 Top Vikings storylines after minicamp, from QBs to new GM 
 Will Vikings start Caleb Banks, other rookies on defense? 
 Jefferson says decision on Vikings starting QB 'coach's call' 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 20 

 The Minnesota Vikings defense put on a dominant performance over two days of joint practices with the Baltimore Ravens .

 That has often been the case in recent years, when defensive coordinator Brian Flores' blitz schemes overwhelm offenses that are still learning their protection schemes. Linebacker Dallas Turner repeatedly broke into the backfield on pass rushers, and on the few occasions when the Ravens got the ball into the end zone, they celebrated wildly. Rookie receiver Ja'Kobi Lane spiked the ball with fury, for example, after catching a pass in the back of the end zone.

 The Vikings' offense, meanwhile, showed it is still catching up after spending the first two weeks of camp in a quarterback competition. Most notably, cornerbacks Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins did strong work against Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson , who beat a double team for a touchdown Wednesday but had roughly a half dozen passes broken up as he tried to muscle for position.

 Jefferson said afterwards that the offense is making progress and acknowledged what quarterback Kyler Murray said this spring: Splitting reps was an added challenge.

 "Obviously [Murray] taking all of the 'ones' reps kind of allows us to get in the rhythm and get into the groove of things," Jefferson said. "And you don't really have to rely on having a catch on both footballs from two different people. So I mean, just like he said, he felt that the reps was a little short and he felt more comfortable having more reps.

 "So now he has it and the connection is definitely growing. Work needs to be done, but it comes with time and comes with just coming out here and just working together."

 
 Kicker Will Reichard converted four of six attempts during live kicking Thursday, with misses from 43 and 52 yards. The Vikings continued to split the holding duties between punters Johnny Hekker and Brett Thorson . 
 Safety Theo Jackson left practice with members of the Vikings medical staff after suffering what appeared to be a lower body injury. The team is relatively thin at safety and it has been notable that, even before Jackson departed, undrafted rookie Jacob Thomas was getting extensive first-team snaps. 
 Pro Football Hall of Fame receiver Randy Moss spent both days of joint practices with the Vikings, watching from the sidelines and sitting in on receiver meetings. "The information that he has is endless," Jefferson said. 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 19 

 J.J. McCarthy took every second-team rep Wednesday in the Vikings' joint practice with the Baltimore Ravens , shortly after coach Kevin O'Connell reiterated with reporters that he considers McCarthy the No. 2 quarterback behind starter Kyler Murray .

 O'Connell, however, said he wants the quarterback position to remain competitive and did not rule out the possibility of  Carson Wentz  challenging McCarthy for the spot.

 
"We want Carson feeling like he can do the things consistently that he can do," O'Connell said, "and that we know exactly who and what he is. And we want J.J. feeling like, 'I'm one snap away, so I've got to prepare like I'm the starter anyway.' It's easy to say those things, but we wanted to have a room that forced it.

 "So we'll see how these next couple of weeks play out, and we're going to do what's best for our team, and proud of the way J.J.'s handled the last few days."

 McCarthy and Murray finished out the team portion of Wednesday's practices with big throws. Murray arced a pass roughly 40 yards into the corner of the end zone, allowing receiver Justin Jefferson to run past a double team and grab the ball for a touchdown. McCarthy then threw about a 30-yard pass over the middle to receiver Myles Price for a score.

 Other observations: 

 
 O'Connell acknowledged there have been some inconsistent snaps from center Blake Brandel to Murray during camp. He indicated it is largely an issue of Brandel anticipating where he is going to step first, triggering an inaccurate snap -- an unsurprising development for a player who hadn't played center before last season. "We have time," O'Connell said, "but not that much time, as I like to say." 
 Quarterback Max Brosmer (right wrist) did some light throwing Tuesday but did not participate in team drills. O'Connell said the Vikings are hoping Brosmer will be ready to play in Saturday's preseason game. 
 Rookie Caleb Tiernan , a third-round draft pick this spring who has been the second-team right tackle during training camp, is week-to-week because of an ankle injury, O'Connell said. 
 

 

 Who is the Vikings' top performer so far at camp? 

 Receiver Tai Felton has demonstrated remarkable improvement from his rookie year, when he struggled to catch the ball consistently in training camp and wound up with a near-exclusive special teams role during the season. He has made one-handed catches in the end zone, demonstrated soft hands at the end of deep routes and displayed his top-end speed while running quick hitters. Coach Kevin O'Connell said he has noted exceptional route running at times as well.

 Is Felton the Vikings' best player? Of course not. But no one has opened more eyes since camp began. He'll push veteran No. 3 receiver Jauan Jennings for playing time.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 

 The entire NFL world wants to know how quarterback Kyler Murray , who was named the starter after a two-week competition with J.J. McCarthy , will perform in the Vikings' offense. But Murray isn't likely to play nearly enough during the preseason to answer that question.

 The most important question the Vikings can realistically answer is how much of their talented draft class will truly be ready to contribute in Week 1.

 That list most notably includes defensive linemen Caleb Banks and Domonique Orange , linebacker Jake Golday , safety Jakobe Thomas , cornerback Charles Demmings and running back Demond Claiborne .

 

 Monday, Aug. 17 

 Second-year quarterback Max Brosmer did not participate in a relatively light practice Monday because of an injured right wrist, a development to keep an eye on as the Vikings prepare for their second preseason game Saturday against the Baltimore Ravens .

 
The Vikings and Ravens are scheduled for two days of joint practices Wednesday and Thursday, and historically coach Kevin O'Connell has not played starters in the preseason game that immediately follows. O'Connell has not revealed his plans for Saturday's game. But assuming that starter Kyler Murray doesn't play, and if Brosmer isn't available, that would leave all the snaps for J.J. McCarthy and Carson Wentz .

 
In 2025, Brosmer played 58% of the Vikings' offensive snaps in the second preseason game following joint practices with the New England Patriots .

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell said earlier this week that both of the quarterbacks who took part in their two-week competition for the starting job would play…

title: 2026 New England Patriots training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our daily updates from Patriots training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Patriots reporter Mike Reiss has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Patriots camp. Will Drake Maye  start another MVP-like campaign in Year 3? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, concluding with the Patriots' top camp performer and biggest lingering question as preseason games begin.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Patriots camp 
 
 Patriots TE Hunter Henry signs extension worth up to $20M 
 Has Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez found his voice? 
 A.J. Brown on injury: 'Thumb out of place, you keep going' 
 Patriots' Brown knows Vrabel's rip comes from 'great place' 
 Kraft: Patriots' Gonzalez has offer to be 'highest-paid' CB ever 
 Too many receivers? A look at the Patriots' crowded WR room 
 
 
 

 Thursday, Aug. 20 
 Quarterback Drake Maye has said that wide receiver A.J. Brown is "open even when he's covered," and Thursday's practice with the Eagles highlighted the fine line Maye walks with that thought.

 Maye was intercepted twice when targeting Brown, the first of which came in front of the right pylon in red zone work as cornerback Riq Woolen stepped in front of the pass and returned it for a would-be pick-six.

 "I was just late with the football. You can't be late in the red zone," Maye explained. "It's tight, and it's a concept that we probably need to get some more work on and just find some timing."

 The second pick came closer to midfield, with Maye firing a pass to Brown on an in-breaking route. It was unclear in real-time if Brown caught the ball and had it jarred loose from his grasp by Woolen, or if the ball simply popped up in the air. Nonetheless, outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt showed impressive awareness and quickness to dive and haul it in.

 Overall, Maye was pleased with the two days of practices with the Eagles. The teams play Saturday night but it's possible Maye won't see any action based on the extensive reps he received in practice.

 "I think we had a lot of great work," he said. "You got to string some plays together in a row, and I felt like we did that more [Wednesday] than we did today."

 More observations: 

 
 CB Marcus Jones had two interceptions. That gave the Patriots a total of seven INTs over the two days of practice with the Eagles. 
 With starting right tackle Morgan Moses having his reps managed, first-round pick Caleb Lomu elevated to the top unit in his place. 
 In one-on-one red zone work, Brown had what looked like a highlight-reel catch in the back left corner of the end zone on CB Quinyon Mitchell , but the official ruled him out of bounds. If there was instant replay, it might have been overturned. 
 Former teammates Brown and Jalen Hurts shared time together after practice, as did Drake Maye and Hurts. 
 More than an hour after the final open-to-the-public practice ended, two players remained signing autographs for fans -- WRs Efton Chism III and Mack Hollins . 
 

 

 Wednesday, Aug. 19 
 On the first snap the Patriots and Eagles were on the field together, wide receiver A.J. Brown ran a go route against cornerback Quinyon Mitchell and had a chance to electrify the estimated crowd of 12,000-plus.

 Brown created separation, fought through a potential penalty, but then failed to secure the catch.

 It was the only blemish on a productive day in which Brown totaled six receptions against his former team.

 "Q got away with a little holding," Brown said with a laugh, when asked to describe the play against Mitchell. "I won, he pulled himself back into the play, and I just have to finish the play. My right hand didn't get to the ball quick enough. My left hand got on the ball. That's on me. Attention to detail -- catching the ball high, not letting it get low.

 "... It's never about who I'm going against, it's the little things; that could have been a 40-yard bomb, but now it's a long foul ball. Those are the things I'm focusing on."

 Brown met with reporters after practice and upon his arrival he took note of seeing "old friends" in the media from spending four seasons in Philadelphia. He said he hasn't spoken with Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts since the trade, but he had "all love" for his time in Philadelphia.

 As for how he feels things are going learning to work with a new quarterback in Drake Maye , he said: "There have definitely been some challenges but he's very special. He makes my job a lot easier. There's a learning curve and we'll continue to keep working at it."

 

 More observations: 

 
 One area of improvement from last week's practice with the Colts came in the two-minute drill. The Patriots' top offense rushed Andy Borregales on for a successful field goal, while the top defense held the Eagles without points. The backup units also were successful, with the D capping off a turnover-laden day as CB Kindle Vildor registered an INT. 
 The Patriots totaled five interceptions from safeties Craig Woodson (2) and John Saunders Jr ., and CBs Vildor and Marcus Jones . 
 Although not facing a pass rush that can tackle him, Maye was accurate and in rhythm for the most part. One charting of his day had him 16-of-19 in 11-on-11 work. 
 Rookie OLB Gabe Jacas was elevated to the first unit on punt protection, and said after practice he has never executed those responsibilities prior to coming to New England. Coach Mike Vrabel has been spending one-on-one time with him. 
 Newly signed veteran G/C Greg Van Roten initially worked at center with the second unit in warmups. 
 Starting CB Christian Gonzalez has remained out of practice since Aug. 11. 
 There were no fights, as the professionalism of both teams showed up. The lone dust-up came after a snap in a FG drill and Vrabel got right in the middle of it to help extinguish things quickly. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 18 
 Former Patriots wide receiver Julian Edelman was a guest of the team's light, low-tempo practice. Edelman watched from the sideline and at one point was chatting with owner Robert Kraft.

 "It's always good to have Patriots legends around here," veteran tight end Hunter Henry said. "The more the merrier. Those guys set the standard here, so it's always good to have them back."

 Edelman also caught up with wide receiver A.J. Brown , who will be under the spotlight the next two days with the Eagles coming to town for two practices. Edelman had given Brown his blessing to wear his old No. 11, but Brown previously said he wanted to honor Edelman's legacy and create his own by wearing No. 1 (his old college number).

 

 More observations: 

 
 The Patriots officially signed veteran G/C Greg Van Roten to a one-year deal and released TE Mitch Van Vooren . The 36-year-old Van Roten, who projects as the top interior backup with Ben Brown sidelined multiple weeks due to injury, has been assigned jersey No. 70. 
 Veteran LB Robert Spillane was one of the last players on the field after practice, as he spent time working with 2026 second-round draft pick Gabe Jacas on punt protection and punt-rush technique. 
 As for what to expect in Wednesday and Thursday practices with the Eagles, coach Mike Vrabel said: "I think upwards of probably 28 reps, 30 reps for the first group on each day is a good number ... we'll be able to do a lot more field work on the first day and then probably focus on the red zone the next day." 
 The Patriots had veteran free agent DT DaQuan Jones and veteran free agent LB Shaq Thompson in for visits (different from tryouts).

 Quarterback Drake Maye  delivered a beautiful deep pass to receiver A.J. Brown for a 65-yard(ish) touchdown over the…

title: 2026 New York Giants training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our updates from Giants training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Giants reporter Jordan Raanan has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and, of course, the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Giants camp. How will the Giants handle increased expectations and a new coach? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Catch up on all the updates, including the Giants' top camp performer and biggest lingering question.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest news from Giants camp 
 
 Players pulled from fight-filled Giants-Dolphins practice 
 Giants trade Daniel Faalele to Jaguars for 6th-round draft pick 
 Giants' Malik Nabers 'felt good' in 1st full-speed live drills 
 Giants QB Jaxson Dart 'puzzled' by latest concussion test request 
 A Harbaugh team meeting during training camp -- an inside look 
 

 
 Thursday, Aug. 20 
 MIAMI GARDENS, Fla. -- This was the kind of practice you wanted to see from the Giants' offense -- and from quarterback Jaxson Dart .

 Dart had perhaps his best performances of the summer, going 17-of-23 passing in a joint practice against the Miami Dolphins that included several deep and intermediate gains. Six went to his favorite target, tight end Isaiah Likely .

 "I felt like I played clean," Dart said.

 This was an important day for Dart and the Giants' offense, which has been up and down most of the summer while learning a new system. They hadn't been able to hit many plays downfield.

 This was sort of a validation that this new offense can work.

 "We had a number of chunk gains off play-action, which was good to see," Giants coach John Harbaugh said. "It's one thing in theory, it's another thing in practice. You want to see it work. At the end of the day, did the play work? It could be a great play, but if it doesn't work, then there's a lot of things that go into making it work, including executing it well, then it's not a good play. I agree [it's validating]."

 

 More observations: 

 
 The Giants' offense probably wasn't even the team's best unit in the joint practice against the Dolphins. Outside linebacker Brian Burns said the defense was "dominant." When asked by a reporter if they had six sacks, Burns said no. In his estimation, they got to Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis even more than that. 
 How about this for a quick integration? Running back Najee Harris participated in live drills after just three days with the team. He even got a couple carries, including one on the goal line where he made an impressive cut and reached the end zone. Harris looked good for a player that supposedly wasn't going to be in football shape for a "couple weeks." 
 Another perfect practice for undrafted rookie kicker Dominic Zvada , who went 6-for-6, including one to end practice after the Giants drove the field on a two-minute drill. 
 Rookie guard Francis Mauigoa left practice with what Harbaugh called a "stinger." He didn't expect it to be serious. Josh Ezeudu was next in line at guard. 
 

 

 Tuesday, Aug. 18 

 Malik Nabers participated in full live-speed team drills for the second straight day in a red jersey. And he looked even better than he did on Monday.

 Nabers saw a slightly increased workload. He ran eight routes and caught four passes from quarterback Jaxson Dart in 11-on-11 and 7-on-7 drills. Of course, it helped that the defense couldn't touch him.

 On one deep pass, safeties Jevon Holland and Tyler Nubin had to pull up on the play to avoid any contact.

 Coach John Harbaugh said that Nabers "handled it well" bouncing back after his first day of live drills. The next step is adding reps, getting bumped around, shedding the red jersey and feeling contact. That could come as early as next week.

 In the meantime, Nabers' workload will be light during Thursday's joint practice with the Dolphins. Barring a setback, the expectation seems to be that Nabers will be ready for Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys .

 

 More observations: 

 
 Running back Tyrone Tracy Jr . was first up at running back on Tuesday. He's still squarely in the Giants plans even with the signing of Najee Harris . Tracy and Cam Skattebo have both been the first running back up throughout training camp. 
 Harbaugh seemed to indicate he expects it to take a "couple weeks" before Harris gets into football shape. The veteran running back did only individual drills on Tuesday. 
 The Giants worked on a lot of red zone and short-yardage situations on Tuesday. Dart's running was a big part of the practice. 
 

 

 Monday, Aug. 17 
 The referee at practice threw a flag on Colton Hood after he cut off wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr . in the end zone. The rookie cornerback didn't like the call and made it known.

 Coach John Harbaugh saw it unfold. He didn't agree with Hood's assessment and sent him to the sideline. But not until they had a quick chat.

 "I wasn't angry. I just wanted to make the point that, you know, what are you arguing about?" Harbaugh said. "The ball was in the air and you pushed the receiver and redirected him. It was a restriction. That's going to be pass interference. But he's competitive. He's competitive. He wants to win every snap. And I think [that's] part of the journey for the young corners."

 Hood had his ups and downs in the preseason opener -- a 13-10 loss against the Minnesota Vikings . And again at Monday's practice. Harbaugh said Hood was going to be playing plenty and just wanted to accelerate the learning curve.

 Hopefully this was a lesson learned.

 

 Who is the Giants' top performer so far at camp? 
 TE Isaiah Likely  The offseason acquisition has been the Giants' No. 1 receiver with Malik Nabers not participating in team drills. He's been quarterback  Jaxson Dart 's safety net, leading all first-team receivers in catches by a wide margin.

 "Zay's done a great job," offensive coordinator Matt Nagy said.

 The way Likely smoothly gets in and out of breaks has just looked different from incumbent starter Theo Johnson . He also seems to have the best handle on the new offense given his familiarity with coach John Harbaugh and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman from Baltimore. Given the way Dart likes to throw to his tight ends, it suggests that Likely is in for a breakout season given the chemistry they already have developed.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 Can the offense put it together? There are a lot of things working against Dart early in camp. He's learning a new offense, doesn't have Nabers in live drills and the structure of practice prohibits endless freelancing, which is perhaps what he does best. So it has been a struggle.

 The offense has failed to put together many big days in practice throughout the summer. Nagy said they expected there to be "highs and lows through this process" for their young quarterback. To see Dart and the first-team offense have some success in the preseason, even if it's just flashes, would be a welcome sight and could provide a confidence boost entering the season.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 

 The Giants are working hard at training camp. There is no doubt about that. Even on a rare day when they weren't in pads and ran a mental-rep practice that resembled a walk-through, coach John Harbaugh had the Giants on the field for two-plus hours.

 The practice concluded with them going over pregame introductions and the new routine for warmups. Every detail is important at the difficult Camp Harbaugh, which had players in full pads at seven of the past 10 practices.

 "My toughest training camp in 10 years," said fullback Patrick Ricard , who came over from Baltimore with Harbaugh.

 In a way, this has reminded some Giants of a college camp. With fewer…

title: From Knicks to Yankees, Nick Jonas finds the perfect song
summary: The Jonas Brothers are longtime New York sports fans and have a song that can speak to their favorite teams.
full_text:
First, it was the New York Knicks ' first NBA title in 53 years. Then it was the "American royal wedding" between pop star Taylor Swift and Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce  keeping the historic Madison Square Garden busy this summer. However, summer at the world's most famous arena isn't over yet. 
 
 

 The Jonas Brothers' three-night stint at MSG for the "Burnin' Up Tour All Over Again" kicks off Aug. 20. Raised in New Jersey, the three brothers, who are featured in the new Disney film "Camp Rock 3," are New York sports fans and have been unwavering supporters of the Knicks, so the venue just seems fitting, especially during a summer like this. 
 
 

 "Going back to last year, the run [the Knicks] made in the playoffs, I was in New York at the time doing a show on Broadway and was around it every day, feeling the energy in the city. It was electric," Jonas told ESPN. "Cut to this year, and just to see them complete the journey during the finals and what that meant to the city as a whole ... it was pretty incredible to see."

 On the cusp of a historic New York summer and ahead of performing at halftime of the NFL Week 1 game between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams  in Melbourne, Australia, ESPN sat down with Nick Jonas to assign Jonas Brothers songs to his favorite New York team from each league.

 

 

 New York Knicks: 'Love Bug' 

 Again, the Knicks are still the moment after winning their first NBA championship in more than 50 years. This sweet ballad from the Jonas Brothers, released in 2008, perfectly sums up how Nick Jonas feels about his team.

 "It just feels right for them," he said.

 

 

 New York Giants : 'Sucker' 

 The NFL regular season is right around the corner, and many New York sports fans are loyal to "Big Blue." The Giants also have a humongous fanbase, just like "Sucker." In 2019, the group's comeback single struck the top of the Billboard charts -- the Jonas Brothers'  first-ever No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 .

 "I'm probably going to go with 'Sucker' because it's the biggest one, the most important [song], to some," Jonas told ESPN.

 

 

 New York Yankees : 'Burnin' Up' 

 Just like the Yankees, there's so much nostalgia that comes with "Burnin' Up." The song, released in 2008, was one of the first smash hits for the Jonas Brothers. As for the Yankees, they are one of the most revered franchises in sports. 

 "[The Yankees are] more like legacy," Jonas said.

title: Can Adonai Mitchell be 'Robin' that Jets are searching for?
summary: New York has struggled to find a complement to Garrett Wilson since drafting him in 2022.
full_text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- In  Garrett Wilson 's first four seasons with the New York Jets , his opening-day sidekicks at wide receiver were, chronologically:

 Corey Davis , Allen Lazard, Mike Williams and Josh Reynolds .

 One got benched (Lazard), one got traded (Williams) and one got injured (Reynolds). None of them caught more than 32 passes.

 Next tag-team partner up: Adonai Mitchell .

 

 "If he continues on this trajectory right here," receivers coach Shawn Jefferson said of Mitchell, "he will be a really good Robin for our Batman. Big time."

 Except for an 11-game stretch in 2024, when Davante Adams was acquired in a trade that reunited him and Aaron Rodgers , Gotham City has lacked a dynamic duo at receiver in recent years. The franchise that produced star tandems such as Wayne Chrebet-Keyshawn Johnson (1990s) and Al Toon-Wesley Walker (1980s) has fielded its share of jokers.

 In Mitchell, the Jets believe they have an ascending talent, ready to pop in his third year in the NFL -- a player whose outside vertical speed should complement Wilson's slipperiness in the short and intermediate areas.

 Since 2022, the Jets have relied on Wilson and running back Breece Hall as their offensive staples, hoping each season to uncover a third option -- either a No. 2 wide receiver or a pass-catching tight end.

 Hall said he and Wilson have a friendly competition, trying to outdo each other for the unofficial title of "best player on offense." They'd love it if their two-man show turned into a three-man battle. Did someone say four?

 "I believe we have the pieces in place that will get us to playing meaningful football in December, something I've dreamed about doing for a long time," said Wilson, who, like Hall, has yet to experience a winning season in the green and white.

 Hall believes this is the best and most cohesive skill-position group they've had during their tenure, saying, "We feel we finally have a team around us for us to really flourish and do what we know we can do."

 To be fair, the Wilson-Adams-Hall troika produced solid numbers, if not victories, in 2024 -- a 5-12 season. In fact, Wilson set career highs in catches (101), receiving yards (1,104) and touchdowns (seven), in part, because Adams was able to draw coverage away from him. That they got competent quarterback play from Rodgers also was a factor.

 

 Adams was productive (67 catches for 854 yards in 11 games), but he was perceived as a hired gun, just passing through to satisfy Rodgers' desire for another weapon. The Mike Williams experiment backfired, leading to the Adams trade.

 This time, the candidates for the "Robin" role have a chance to stick around for a while. Mitchell, acquired from the Indianapolis Colts in last season's Sauce Gardner blockbuster trade, is signed through 2027. Tight end Mason Taylor is under contract through 2028. Tight end Kenyon Sadiq and wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr ., both 2026 first-round picks, are signed through 2029.

 Hall and Wilson are locked up through 2028 and 2030, respectively, so you can see why Hall has talked about having stability and continuity for a change. In theory, the group will grow together, presumably with a long-term quarterback solution arriving in 2027.

 The key is player development. Hall and Wilson are the only proven players; the others still are feeling their way through the early stages of their careers. Growing pains are likely.

 Which brings us back to Mitchell, the most experienced of the bunch -- a 2024 second-round pick with 56 receptions in three seasons. In Indianapolis, he was inconsistent, had some drops and lost playing time before being shipped to New York.

 Initially perceived as a "throw in" in the Gardner trade, in which the Jets also received two first-round picks, Mitchell actually was a prime target for the front office. No Mitchell, no deal. He flashed a little last season (24 catches in eight games for the Jets) and became the talk of the offseason, settling into the team and raising expectations.

 "A new start, a new beginning, new quarterback, new system," Mitchell said. "I mean, I love it. I love the challenge. I love embracing what we have here."

 In the offseason, Mitchell hopped on a flight and flew to Miami to work out with newly acquired quarterback Geno Smith . For five days, Mitchell, Smith and Taylor powered through oppressive heat and humidity in an effort to build chemistry before training camp.

 Early in camp, Hall named Mitchell, Taylor, Sadiq and running back Braelon Allen as the four players who could help lift the offense to a higher level -- which is to say, out of the basement. They finished 29th in scoring, their 10th straight year in the bottom 10.

 

 Sadiq hasn't been available; he has missed the past eight practices because of a setback from offseason hernia surgery. He's expected to return by Week 1, but it's fair to wonder about residual effects from the layoff.

 Taylor and Allen are having good camps, with Allen's role increasing now that Hall (strained groin) is out for two to three weeks , according to coach Aaron Glenn. And let's not forget about Cooper. The Jets thought enough of him to trade into the bottom of the first round, but he has been up and down.

 Playing with the backups, Cooper made two catches for 31 yards against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the preseason opener Friday, but his role for the regular season is uncertain. He has lost reps to Isaiah Williams , the biggest surprise in camp. Williams is drawing effusive praise from the coaches. Cooper is experiencing "little pitfalls," according to Jefferson -- not uncommon for a rookie.

 Still, there is optimism.

 "It feels different this year," Wilson said. "It just does."

 Call it a Bat signal.

title: Riq Woolen impresses at Eagles' practice

title: 2026 Philadelphia Eagles training camp: Latest intel, updates
summary: Catch up on our updates from Eagles training camp, including intel on QBs, position battles and potential breakouts.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL training camps have kicked off around the league, and our team reporters are on the ground each day following all the action. Eagles reporter Tim McManus has the latest intel on standouts, highlights, position battles, depth chart movement, cut decisions and -- of course -- the quarterbacks room.

 What follows is everything we are seeing and hearing at Eagles camp. How will quarterback  Jalen Hurts fare in the reimagined offense? Who are the breakout players to watch, especially for fantasy football? And which players on the roster bubble could make the final 53?

 Dive in to all the updates and be sure to check back for more information.

 
 Camp updates for all 32 NFL teams 

 
 

 

 Latest Eagles news 
 
 Moro Ojomo, Fred Johnson scuffle at Eagles camp 
 Eagles QB Jalen Hurts' speed in camp drawing rave reviews 
 Epenesa grateful to be Eagle after 'weird' Browns situation 
 Eagles' Nolan Smith apologizes for 'unacceptable' speeding arrest 
 Eagles, DT Carter agree to four-year, $152M extension 
 

 

 Thursday, Aug. 20 

 Cornerback  Riq Woolen had the type of rollercoaster day that matched the narrative surrounding his career to this point. The best example came on back-to-back red zone plays. On the first rep, New England quarterback  Drake Maye was able to float one past Woolen and into the hands of wide receiver  Romeo Doubs for the score. On the next play, Woolen stepped in front of A.J. Brown and took the interception the other way for a pick-six. Later in the session, Woolen appeared to lose Doubs in coverage and clapped his hands in frustration as the receiver caught a TD in the back of the end zone.

 Woolen was one of the top standouts during the spring but has had a mixed summer. In order to level up and help make this the best corner group in the game, he'll need to show a bit more consistency in the regular season.

 Other observations: 

 
 Woolen also helped deliver the play of the day, knocking loose a ball to Brown late in the session. Outside linebacker Jalyx Hunt then snatched the ball out of midair for the interception. 
 Brown had another strong showing against his former team. He and Quinyon Mitchell had another tremendous rep where Brown was able to fight through physical coverage to gain just enough separation to haul in a touchdown along the right side. He then went over to the bleachers and flexed for the fans, igniting the crowd. 
 It was a choppy day for the Eagles offense, which focused more on the passing game after finding success on the ground the day prior against New England. Jalen Hurts threw a couple more interceptions after tossing three on Wednesday. 
 Receivers DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon remained limited with hamstring injuries. Lemon was in full pads and continues to ramp up his work. It looks like he'll be back in action before long. 
 
 

 Wednesday, Aug. 19 
 Day 1 of the Eagles-Patriots joint practices did not disappoint. Wide receiver  A.J. Brown was the focal point, and the session started with a battle with corner Quinyon Mitchell during one-on-ones, which ended in an incompletion deep down the left sideline. Brown said with a smile afterwards that Mitchell got away with a hold.

 Brown cleaned up from there, though, hauling in all six passes that went his way during 7-on-7 and team drills. The highlight was a beauty of a deep ball down the right sideline by quarterback  Drake Maye . Brown was able to beat cornerback  Riq Woolen at the line of scrimmage and hauled in the pass at the boundary. Overall, the Eagles' first-team defense had a difficult time slowing Maye and the Patriots' first-team offensive attack.

 Other observations:  

 
 
 It was a mixed bag for QB Jalen Hurts . He threw multiple interceptions but also had arguably his best pass of the summer -- a dime deep down the left side for WR  Elijah Moore , who hauled in the catch and then tossed the ball in the air in celebration.

 
 
 The interior offensive line was giving up too much pressure against a stout Patriots front. That would be problematic if it continues into regular season game action.

 
 
 Receivers DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon (hamstring) were both listed as limited. Lemon mostly worked off to the side but is moving better than we have seen since sustaining the injury early on in camp.

 
 

 

 
 Monday, Aug. 17 
 Eagles No. 1 receiver DeVonta Smith returned to the practice field after sitting out the previous seven sessions because of a hamstring injury. Smith was a limited participant but looked like his normal self -- explosive, quick getting in and out of breaks -- during individual drills. Monday also marked the return of corners Quinyon Mitchell (glute) and  Cooper DeJean  (groin).

 Rookie receiver Makai Lemon (hamstring) sat out his eighth straight practice but has been ramping up his side work over the past handful of days.

 More observations: 

 
 Quarterback Jalen Hurts and the offense had an unremarkable day. Hurts didn't throw downfield much. One pass he did let fly was intercepted by Michael Carter II , who got good positioning on Quez Watkins to make the play. 
 Hurts was able to connect with Hollywood Brown for a chunk gain. Brown found a pocket in the defense between Zack Baun and Riq Woolen and Hurts zipped it in. 
 

 

 

 Who is the Eagles' top performer so far at camp? 

 WR Darius Cooper . No one has made more of their opportunities than Cooper, the 2025 undrafted free agent out of Tarleton State. He came out of nowhere to make the team as a rookie and is making another strong push this summer, standing out in a deep group that includes Hollywood Brown , Elijah Moore and Dontayvion Wicks . Hamstring injuries have sidelined both DeVonta Smith and rookie Makai Lemon for most of camp. Cooper has stepped in and has developed good rapport with QB  Jalen Hurts while showing off strong hands and a willingness to go over the middle.

 What still needs to be answered over the course of preseason games? 
 How will the offensive operation look? The starters are expected to sit out the preseason but there is still plenty to learn about how things function under new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion . He has never called plays and has yet to commit to whether he'll be doing so from the booth or the sideline on game days. The team's hope is the offense is quick out of the huddle, light on penalties and looks efficient during Mannion's test-drive.

 

 Thursday, Aug. 13 
 Quarterback Jalen Hurts had an up-and-down day. He was intercepted by CB Mac McWilliams on an end-zone fade to Hollywood Brown during 7-on-7s early in practice. He got into a flow as the session went on, though, hitting Elijah Moore and Dontayvion Wicks in rhythm before connecting with tight end Dallas Goedert over the middle for a touchdown. Later, Hurts and Wicks hooked up for a touchdown in the corner of the end zone over Riq Woolen , who has come back to earth some this summer following a highly-productive spring.

 More observations:  

 
 Someone should block linebacker  Jalyx Hunt . He's come free far too many times this camp, including from the left side on Thursday to blow up the play. 
 Cooper DeJean (groin) and Quinyon Mitchell (glute) were both sidelined. They were replaced in the lineup by McWilliams and Michael Carter II , respectively. 
 Brown dropped a short pass from Hurts in the red zone. The competition feels tight further down the receiver depth chart, with Darius Cooper , Moore, Brown, Britain Covey and Johnny Wilson among those hoping to find their way onto the 53-man roster. 
 

 
 Tuesday, Aug. 11 
 Quarterback Jalen Hurts and receiver Elijah Moore connected for another big play on Tuesday.

 Hurts uncorked a deep shot for Moore, who sped past safety  Andre' Sam  and hauled in the pass for a touchdown. Moore celebrated by punting the ball well over the practice field gate.

 Hurts has been without DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon the past six practices because of hamstring injuries but is finding a lot…
